reviews.verdict: Our Tiptap run installed 972 packages, used 881 MB, and passed all 1,921 tests, so the code is well exercised but the workspace is substantial.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a finished toolbar and polished editor screen: the README calls Tiptap headless and leaves the interface to you.

reviews.name: symfony
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run Symfony because PHP was unsupported and commit f1072d8 had no Dockerfile, so this review cannot offer a first-party build or test result.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need a framework our Debian harness can verify automatically: PHP was outside its supported ecosystems and the repository had no Dockerfile, so we did not run it.

reviews.name: nginx
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run nginx at commit 8fa349c because it had no C harness and the repository supplied no Dockerfile, so this review cannot promise a source build from our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Windows production operators: the README calls the Windows build a proof of concept intended only for development and testing.

reviews.name: kit
reviews.verdict: SvelteKit is worth evaluating for a Svelte application that needs routing and configurable rendering.
reviews.skip_if: Teams committed to React or Vue components; Next.js and Nuxt respectively deserve consideration instead.

reviews.name: react
reviews.verdict: React fits teams that want component-based interfaces and can choose the surrounding stack.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting React alone to supply routing and data fetching Readers looking for proof of application performance, deployment readiness or security from this sandbox run Contributors expecting the recorded source build to complete without addressing its missing Java executable

reviews.name: Ghost
reviews.verdict: Ghost is the best fit when the publication itself is the product and members, email, and subscriptions should share one editorial system.
reviews.skip_if: Self-hosters who require another provider for Ghost's built-in newsletters: bulk delivery currently supports only the Mailgun API.

reviews.name: register
reviews.verdict: Our is-a.dev checkout installed and passed its tests in 5 seconds, confirming that the registry's automated checks are cheap to reproduce before opening a pull request.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses, commercial projects, or political sites: the terms prohibit commercial, for-profit, and political use.

reviews.name: angular
reviews.verdict: Our Angular source run installed 2,163 packages, then the 183-second build and 70-second test steps both failed, so framework contribution is much harder than creating an app with the published CLI.
reviews.skip_if: Small sites where a few interactive components are the whole requirement: Angular's compiler, dependency injection, router, forms, and release discipline add more framework than that job needs.

reviews.name: expo
reviews.verdict: Our Expo install stopped after 16 seconds because pnpm 11.23.0 missed the repository's required `^10.33.0`, so exact tooling is part of the entry cost even before native SDKs.
reviews.skip_if: Web-only products with no native roadmap: Expo's iOS, Android, React Native, module, and app-store surface adds work that Vite or another browser-first stack avoids.

reviews.name: tailwindcss
reviews.verdict: Our Tailwind CSS checkout passed 5,496 of 5,497 tests, but its Oxide build failed after 81 seconds, so application users can trust the tested core more readily than new contributors can trust a clean source build.
reviews.skip_if: Sites that must support browsers older than Chrome 111, Safari 16.4, or Firefox 128: the v4 compatibility page says to stay on v3.4 for those targets.

reviews.name: astro
reviews.verdict: Our Astro install took 87 seconds and 1,180 MB, and the build passed in 68 seconds, but the repository test task exited 1 after 338 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Applications where nearly every screen is one stateful client interface: Astro's component-island model requires deliberate hydration and may add boundaries without much benefit.

reviews.name: svelte
reviews.verdict: Our Svelte build passed in 133 seconds, and 7,657 tests passed before the suite exited at Chromium launch with 165 skipped.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require drop-in compatibility with a React or Vue component catalog: Svelte components use a different compiler and component model.

reviews.name: react
reviews.verdict: Our React run installed 1,800 packages and passed 6,925 of 6,957 tests, but its source build stopped because `java` was missing, so using React is much easier than contributing to React itself.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an all-in-one web framework: the official installation guide recommends starting new React apps with a framework because React alone does not provide routing or data fetching.

reviews.name: next.js
reviews.verdict: Our Next.js build finished in 96 seconds, but its full test command exceeded 900 seconds, so application setup is approachable while framework contribution is heavy.
reviews.skip_if: Small static sites that need little browser JavaScript or server behavior: Next.js adds a server framework and a larger mental model that such sites may never use.

reviews.name: awesome-ai-agents
reviews.verdict: Our Awesome AI Agents run installed 3 packages in 2 seconds, built in 26 seconds, and passed 6 of 6 tests in 5 seconds, so the catalog tooling gave us a clean result.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who want security, cost, or task-quality rankings: the catalog describes projects but does not benchmark each one.

reviews.name: netron
reviews.verdict: Our Netron run installed 327 packages in 26 seconds, but its build and tests both failed, so using the viewer is easier than developing the repository on a generic Linux box.
reviews.skip_if: Linux maintainers expecting the default build command to produce every desktop target: our build invoked a universal macOS package and failed because that step only runs on Darwin.

reviews.name: gradio
reviews.verdict: Our Gradio source build passed in 74 seconds, but its test command reported an error and stayed in watch mode until the 900-second timeout.
reviews.skip_if: Teams treating a share link as permanent hosting: the sharing guide says links expire after a week and your machine must stay running.

reviews.name: go-micro
reviews.verdict: Our Go Micro run built in 102 seconds and passed all 162 tests in 97 seconds, so v6 is worth a serious trial for Go teams that want agents and services in one process model.
reviews.skip_if: Polyglot teams seeking a language-neutral application framework: service and agent code is Go, even though external callers can use HTTP, gRPC, MCP, or A2A.

reviews.name: no-negative-echo
reviews.verdict: Start with the AGENTS.md rule if persistent writing instructions are enough; install No Negative Echo for its additional workflow and scanner.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring deterministic review of a sentence's meaning.

reviews.name: genkit
reviews.verdict: Our Genkit build succeeded, but it took 407 seconds after an 8-second install, so source contributors should budget for a slow loop even though dependency setup was quick.
reviews.skip_if: Python or Dart teams that require the same stability promise as JavaScript and Go: the README labels Python beta and Dart preview.

reviews.name: ultralytics
reviews.verdict: Our Ultralytics run installed 109 packages and occupied 5,982 MB, then its tests stopped on missing `libGL.so.1`, so the friendly Python API still needs a deliberate runtime image.
reviews.skip_if: Closed-source commercial products whose owners will neither meet AGPL-3.0 terms nor buy an Enterprise license: the README presents those as the two licensing routes.

reviews.name: pytorch
reviews.verdict: Use the official binary route to evaluate PyTorch for an application, then validate your actual model and hardware.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting this recorded sandbox run to demonstrate a working source build.

reviews.name: onnxruntime
reviews.verdict: Our ONNX Runtime run installed 66 packages in 16 seconds and built in 3 seconds, but it found no test target, so the result supports a quick package trial rather than a claim about the full native stack.
reviews.skip_if: Teams unwilling to add ONNX export and compatibility checks to a framework-native workflow: the runtime consumes ONNX graphs, and provider support varies by operator.

reviews.name: watermarks-remover
reviews.verdict: Our watermarks-remover run installed 55 packages in 6 seconds and passed its 96-second test run, making the core a credible trial for authorized file hygiene.
reviews.skip_if: Archives, newsrooms, or compliance teams that must preserve provenance: the tool can remove C2PA and generator metadata they may need as evidence.

reviews.name: Fabric
reviews.verdict: Our Fabric run built in 266 seconds, but 3 of 71 tested packages failed in the extension template area, so adopt it around a few reviewed Patterns before making it shared infrastructure.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a green fresh-container test gate: our run ended with 68 passing packages and 3 failures in the extension template package.

reviews.name: typescript-sdk
reviews.verdict: Our TypeScript SDK checkout installed 877 packages in 25 seconds and occupied 665 MB, but its default build and test stages were both skipped because the root exposed neither target.
reviews.skip_if: Applications pinned below Node.js 20: every current core, client, and server package declares Node 20 or newer.

reviews.name: firecrawl-mcp-server
reviews.verdict: Our Firecrawl MCP Server run installed 339 packages in 21 seconds and passed all 123 tests, so the adapter itself is easy to trial.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting this package to be a private crawler by itself: local mode still calls Firecrawl cloud or a separately operated Firecrawl API.

reviews.name: humanizer
reviews.verdict: Our Humanizer run installed 35 packages in 10 seconds, built in 4 seconds, and found no test target, so setup is trivial while rewrite reliability remains a manual judgment.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a standalone editor: Humanizer is an instruction file and needs a compatible AI agent to perform the rewrite.

reviews.name: apfel
reviews.verdict: apfel is a must-have utility for any developer or power user on a modern Mac.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users, as it's exclusive to Apple Silicon Macs running recent macOS versions.

reviews.name: Front-End-Checklist
reviews.verdict: Our Front-End Checklist run built in 124 seconds and passed all 20 Jest tests in 39 seconds, but the contributor install still occupied 1,421 MB.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking proof that a page is accessible: the checklist itself requires testing with NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, or TalkBack because automation cannot settle screen-reader behavior.

reviews.name: claude-howto
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 24 seconds, built in 8 seconds, and found no test target, so Claude How To is easy to inspect but did not prove its examples through an automated suite.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs configuration details to be authoritative without checking Anthropic's docs: open issue 176 reports an inverted skill-precedence rule and the wrong shape and purpose for `skillOverrides`.

reviews.name: agent-skills
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 0 packages in 6 seconds and passed 1 test in 2 seconds, so Agent Skills is cheap to inspect but only lightly proven by the path we ran.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting every direct request to trigger the right workflow automatically: issue 620 reports 0 of 6 activations across several code-in-prompt tasks under Claude Code 2.1.283.

reviews.name: ui-ux-pro-max-skill
reviews.verdict: Our UI UX Pro Max run installed 32 packages in 15 seconds, built in 5 seconds, and returned 0 audit findings, making it cheap to trial in an agent-driven frontend project.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting finished visual assets from the open-source edition: the README reserves AI image creation, logos, and broader brand work for the premium version.

reviews.name: browser-tools-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our browser-tools-mcp run built in 8 seconds and passed 355 of 356 tests, with the one failure in degraded attachment handling and 0 audit findings.
reviews.skip_if: Playwright-style test authors who need the agent to drive a clean, reproducible browser: the README recommends automation-first MCP servers for that job.

reviews.name: kong
reviews.verdict: Our Kong fixture built in 22 seconds and passed all 6 tests, but those results cover a small Rust workspace rather than the running gateway.
reviews.skip_if: Teams treating a green Cargo run as proof that Kong itself works: our 6 passing tests covered only `spec/fixtures/proxy_wasm_filters`, not the Lua gateway.

reviews.name: agentic-awesome-skills
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 11 packages in 3 seconds, then the build failed on a missing Python `yaml` module and the tests hit the 900-second cap, so Agentic Awesome Skills is easier to consume than to develop from a bare Node…
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting the catalogue to choose the best skill: AAS Core has no ranking or semantic suitability check, so Codex or Claude makes that judgment.

reviews.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our Chrome DevTools MCP run installed 1,130 packages and used 615 MB, then its tests failed after 131 seconds in Puppeteer's Chrome launch and connection path.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require Firefox, Safari, or guaranteed support for another Chromium browser: the project officially supports only Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing.

reviews.name: litellm
reviews.verdict: Our LiteLLM run installed 379 packages in 22 seconds with 0 known vulnerabilities, but the root project offered no build or test target, so it proved dependency resolution rather than release readiness.
reviews.skip_if: A small application committed to one provider: LiteLLM's 12,122-file checkout and gateway controls add far more surface than a direct vendor SDK.

reviews.name: appium
reviews.verdict: Our Appium run passed all 416 tests after a 61-second install, but it left 573 MB of dependencies and 14 high-severity audit findings, so it earns its keep only when one automation protocol must cover several app platforms.
reviews.skip_if: Android-only or iOS-only teams happy with vendor tools: Appium adds an HTTP server, a client, and a driver between the test and the platform API.

reviews.name: gogcli
reviews.verdict: Use gogcli when its shared Workspace interface and explicit automation controls solve a concrete scripting problem for you.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who want to avoid creating and authorizing a Google Cloud Desktop OAuth client.

reviews.name: fastlane
reviews.verdict: fastlane has 42,092 GitHub stars, a last push one day ago, and a 2.239.0 release six days before this review, but our run measured zero install, build, or test steps because the repo has no supported ecosystem.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that only ship web or backend services and never touch mobile app stores Developers who refuse to manage a Ruby toolchain and native SDK dependencies Projects that need a self-contained Docker image and do not want to build their…

reviews.name: rclone
reviews.verdict: Our rclone run built successfully in 176 seconds but finished its test step with 223 passing results and 15 failures, so this checkout needs closer inspection before a patched release.
reviews.skip_if: Archive owners expecting sync to preserve destination-only files: the documented sync command can delete them.

reviews.name: lego
reviews.verdict: Our lego install never completed: after 682 seconds, Go module downloads ended on `proxy.golang.org` stream errors before build or tests began.
reviews.skip_if: Hermetic source builds without a Go module proxy or populated cache: our install failed after 682 seconds while downloading the toolchain and provider SDKs.

reviews.name: Karabiner-Elements
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox found 25 known npm vulnerabilities in the vendored Duktape debugger and could not build or test the macOS app, so the 42-second install is not evidence that Karabiner-Elements itself passed a health check.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users: the README supports only macOS, with current binaries limited to macOS 13 through 27.

reviews.name: mobile-mcp
reviews.verdict: Trial Mobile MCP for supervised native-app exploration if you can configure a device environment and verify the results.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring Mobile MCP's WebView inspection or device file push and pull tools: the supplied roadmap lists both as planned.

reviews.name: puppeteer
reviews.verdict: Our Puppeteer run built in 68 seconds, then finished with 9 passing and 144 failing tests, so adopting it means validating your exact browser host instead of trusting a successful compile.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require Safari or WebKit coverage: Puppeteer's documented browser targets are Chrome and Firefox.

reviews.name: hatchet
reviews.verdict: Pilot Hatchet if retained workflow history and recovery controls address a concrete application need.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean repository test run before adoption: our stored parser summary contains failing package results.

reviews.name: ai-job-search
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 15 seconds and pytest reported 494 passed with 0 failures, so AI Job Search has unusually credible engineering underneath its prompt files.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking unattended mass submission: the workflow drafts and reviews materials, then leaves the actual application to the candidate.

reviews.name: keda
reviews.verdict: KEDA is worth evaluating when event-driven Kubernetes scaling, including activation from zero, is the requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for an autoscaler outside Kubernetes.

reviews.name: karpenter-provider-aws
reviews.verdict: Our Karpenter build passed in 180 seconds, but tests ended with 19 of 21 packages failing, so source contributors need the project's intended test environment before treating a generic Go run as healthy.
reviews.skip_if: Kubernetes teams outside AWS: this repository implements the AWS provider, while other clouds use separate Karpenter providers or managed services.

reviews.name: agent-browser
reviews.verdict: Our install of commit 39a74c7 took 138 seconds, pulled 1,097 packages, and left 931 MB on disk, while the checkout exposed no build or test target.
reviews.skip_if: Firefox test suites: the documented engines are Chrome or Chromium plus Safari on iOS, with no Firefox path.

reviews.name: gh-aw
reviews.verdict: Evaluate gh-aw for supervised repository tasks that need interpretation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams replacing deterministic builds, tests, linting, or deployments.

reviews.name: App-Store-Connect-CLI
reviews.verdict: App Store Connect CLI is worth evaluating for command-driven Apple release work, with a workflow-specific acceptance check before adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring an official Apple-supported client.

reviews.name: airflow
reviews.verdict: Choose Apache Airflow 3.3.2 when its Python workflow model and shared scheduling interface justify operating a Linux deployment and production database.
reviews.skip_if: Continuous stream processing: Airflow explicitly describes itself as unsuitable for streaming, although it can consume stream data in batches.

reviews.name: huginn
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Huginn when self-hosted monitoring justifies maintaining a database, web process, and worker.
reviews.skip_if: Readers requiring a verified application deployment or passing Ruby specs: our run established neither.

reviews.name: windmill
reviews.verdict: Windmill is worth evaluating when developer-owned scripts also need workflows and internal interfaces.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking evidence here of production throughput, deployment reliability or successful business workflows: our sandbox did not test those.

reviews.name: ALEAPP
reviews.verdict: Our ALEAPP run passed 1,130 tests with 0 failures in 55 seconds, making it an easy recommendation for Android examiners who will verify important artifacts against source data.
reviews.skip_if: Examiners who need every SQLite sidecar handled from archives: open issue 14 says most zip and tar patterns ignore matching `-wal` and `-journal` files, which can omit records.

reviews.name: awesome-jev-projects
reviews.verdict: Our Awesome Jev Projects run installed 93 packages and passed all 399 tests, so the catalog machinery is better checked than a typical awesome list.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers seeking independent runtime benchmarks: the verification document says no project runtime or performance verification is claimed.

reviews.name: turbovec
reviews.verdict: Our TurboVec run passed all 883 tests, but the suite took 500 seconds, evidence of a serious correctness effort rather than proof of the README's speed claims.
reviews.skip_if: Services that need a network API, replication, or tenant isolation: the README explicitly describes TurboVec as a library rather than a server.

reviews.name: awesome-jev
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 0 packages, built in 7 seconds, and passed all 4 tests, so the catalog mechanics are unusually easy to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who want a ranked shortlist: inclusion shows source evidence for Jev use, not product quality, security, or fitness for production.

reviews.name: awesome-jev
reviews.verdict: Our run built awesome-jev in 10 seconds, but there was no test target, so its 570 listed entries are leads rather than verified recommendations.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who want a ranked shortlist of production-ready tools: the README says listings are not quality, security, maturity, or runtime endorsements.

reviews.name: awesome-fly
reviews.verdict: Our count of commit ed5e006 found 103 entries across 8 resource sections, making Awesome Fly the most useful starting map for this fast-growing niche.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a runnable fly-brain package: this repository is a curated README, not a simulator or dataset.

reviews.name: osquery
reviews.verdict: Our October 2 sandbox could not clone osquery, so this review has no install, build, or test result to balance against the documentation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a central console out of the box: the README points to separate fleet managers and says the osquery project does not endorse, recommend, or test them.

reviews.name: cockroach
reviews.verdict: Our 396-second test run ended with 1,026 of 1,126 Go test entries failing even though install and build passed, so a generic source checkout is a poor adoption shortcut.
reviews.skip_if: Small applications that only need one database server: the production guide calls for at least 3 nodes to tolerate 1 node failure.

reviews.name: dbt
reviews.verdict: Our dbt checkout installed 35 packages in 26 seconds and built in 2 seconds, but no detected test target ran, so that clean result does not justify a v2 migration.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need stable v2 behavior and file formats today: the README calls v2 beta and warns that APIs, behavior, and on-disk formats may change.

reviews.name: GeoLibre
reviews.verdict: Our GeoLibre run passed all 8,352 tests, but installation took 550 seconds, used 2,569 MB, and left 23 npm audit findings to triage.
reviews.skip_if: Source contributors with a small development image or slow CI: our install pulled 1,668 packages, used 2,569 MB, and took 550 seconds.

reviews.name: matplotlib
reviews.verdict: Matplotlib is a reasonable choice for Python figures across publication and interactive environments, based on its documented scope.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring this review to demonstrate successful rendering, GUI interaction or deployment: those workloads were not tested Contributors requiring a passing source-test run before adoption: our recorded run did not provide one Projects whose dependency budget cannot accommodate the 44…

reviews.name: domain-list-community
reviews.verdict: Use domain-list-community for Project V domain categories when you will review the data and define the routing policy.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a complete proxy application or deployment configuration Teams treating domain inclusion as a security or threat verdict Operators who need demonstrated routing behavior in their client before adopting a data source

reviews.name: postgres
reviews.verdict: PostgreSQL is a supported choice to evaluate for applications that need relational SQL capabilities and a team-operated database server.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking proof of passing regression tests from this sandbox record Teams expecting this review to establish workload performance or production readiness Beginners expecting the repository README to contain a complete source-build walkthrough Teams unable to take responsibility for database…

reviews.name: TrackersListCollection
reviews.verdict: TrackersListCollection is a practical source of tracker configuration data when you already have a BitTorrent client and accept public peer discovery.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a torrent client: these files supply tracker addresses to a client you already use.

reviews.name: scikit-learn
reviews.verdict: Our scikit-learn source run installed 42 packages in 863 seconds and built successfully, but its test step failed because the editable loader could not find the requested Ninja executable.
reviews.skip_if: Teams designing custom deep neural networks or reinforcement learning systems: the project FAQ explicitly excludes those areas.

reviews.name: trackerslist
reviews.verdict: Choose trackerslist for its published tracker lists when you can validate the result in your own client and network.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking evidence of faster downloads: our sandbox did not run a torrent workload.

reviews.name: worldview
reviews.verdict: Our Worldview run installed 1,680 packages, built successfully in 382 seconds, and passed all 9,477 Jest tests, which makes it a credible base for teams that specifically need NASA-style imagery browsing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that primarily need dataset search, filtering, and bulk download: Worldview sends data-download work to Earthdata Search rather than replacing that catalog.

reviews.name: typeorm
reviews.verdict: Our TypeORM run installed 962 packages and used 550 MB, then its test command failed after 38 seconds, so the source checkout demands more care than the first entity example suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Teams building against one SQL database that would rather keep queries close to SQL: TypeORM's README spans many drivers, runtimes, and two persistence patterns.

reviews.name: kafka
reviews.verdict: Our Kafka sandbox installed the 45-package Python committer-tools environment in 34 seconds and built it in 26 seconds, but pytest collected 0 tests and exited 5.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers seeking proof that the broker is easy to deploy: our 34-second install covered `committer-tools`, not a running Kafka cluster.

reviews.name: elasticsearch
reviews.verdict: Our Elasticsearch source install did not finish within 900 seconds on 3 CPUs and 10 GB of RAM, so contributing from source is a heavyweight commitment even before a build or test result.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting a quick source setup on a modest machine: our 3-CPU, 10 GB sandbox did not finish installation within 900 seconds.

reviews.name: alloy
reviews.verdict: Use Alloy when one team owns several telemetry signals and wants one programmable agent that speaks OpenTelemetry and Grafana's native ecosystems.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that only need to tail a few log files: Alloy's multi-signal component graph adds concepts and configuration that a focused log shipper avoids.

reviews.name: iptv
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 328 packages, passed all 25 tests, and found 5 known dependency vulnerabilities, so iptv-org/iptv suits viewers who can treat every outside stream as temporary.
reviews.skip_if: Viewers who need guaranteed uptime or picture quality: the repository points to streams run by outside hosts and explicitly says it cannot control them.

reviews.name: google-timeline-visualizer
reviews.verdict: Our Timeline Visualizer run installed 42 packages in 32 seconds and passed all 36 tests, making the Python path unusually easy to verify for a location-video tool.
reviews.skip_if: People unwilling to sideload Android software: the README says the app is not yet on Google Play and requires installing an APK from GitHub.

reviews.name: tempo
reviews.verdict: Our Tempo run built in 204 seconds, but 1 of 54 tested packages failed, so the measured commit needs a test investigation before an internal build is promoted.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking one install with collection, storage, authentication, and a full user interface: Tempo is the backend, and the official architecture puts collectors before it and Grafana after it.

reviews.name: scrapy
reviews.verdict: Our Scrapy run passed 2,673 tests but finished with 7 failures and 76 collection/setup errors after 432 seconds, so the framework is proven in scope but this checkout did not clear a fresh-container suite.
reviews.skip_if: Python 3.10 or older environments: the current README requires Python 3.11 or newer.

reviews.name: supabase
reviews.verdict: Our Supabase run installed 3,193 packages in 136 seconds, then the build failed after 23 seconds in the docs federated-content task, so contributing to the full monorepo demands more patience than adopting the hosted product.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who require a clean root build in a fresh Debian container: our 23-second build stopped in the docs federated-content task.

reviews.name: kyverno
reviews.verdict: Our Kyverno run built successfully in 457 seconds and passed all 284 reported tests in 725 seconds, making commit fe09190 a credible source setup for a Kubernetes policy trial.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a replacement for Kubernetes RBAC: the README says Kyverno complements access control.

reviews.name: client_golang
reviews.verdict: Our client_golang run installed 44 packages in 17 seconds and built in 37 seconds, but 5 of 31 test targets failed, so pin the library and run its tests on your supported Go and operating-system matrix.
reviews.skip_if: Projects pinned to Go 1.24 or older: v1.24.1 requires Go 1.25, and the main branch has already moved its module requirement to Go 1.26.

reviews.name: kubescape
reviews.verdict: Our Kubescape run passed all 135 tests, but installing and building it took 639 seconds and pulled 1,607 packages, so source-level ownership is substantial.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that only need a small YAML linter: Kubescape also pulls in image scanning, remediation, patching, operator, and runtime concerns.

reviews.name: vscodium
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 316 packages in 9 seconds and reported 6 known vulnerabilities in the `font-size` helper, so it did not prove that the VSCodium editor builds cleanly.
reviews.skip_if: Developers dependent on proprietary Microsoft extensions or debuggers: the project documents C#, C++, and Remote Development restrictions outside official VS Code.

reviews.name: OpenCore-Legacy-Patcher
reviews.verdict: Our OpenCore Legacy Patcher run installed 35 packages in 11 seconds and found 0 known vulnerabilities, but the repository exposed no test target for us to run.
reviews.skip_if: Apple Silicon or PowerPC Mac owners: the supported-model guide explicitly excludes both platforms.

reviews.name: PythonRobotics
reviews.verdict: Our PythonRobotics run installed 68 packages in 15 seconds, then pytest collected 0 tests and exited 5, so it is easier to explore than to trust as a ready-made dependency.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a versioned Python dependency: the README tells users to clone the repository and run scripts from individual directories, and GitHub has no latest release.

reviews.name: awesome-sysadmin
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run commit 3086cad because Awesome Sysadmin has no supported language ecosystem and no Dockerfile: it is a catalog, not an application.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting installation instructions or hands-on comparisons: most entries are a short description, license, platform, and link.

reviews.name: iTerm2-Color-Schemes
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 36 packages in 14 seconds and built in 1 second, but it found no test target, so this is an easy catalog to consume and a less reassuring codebase to change.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a tested software package: the repository exposes no tests script or target, and our sandbox therefore skipped tests.

reviews.name: sqlfluff
reviews.verdict: Our SQLFluff run built in 8 seconds, but the test suite was only at 54% when our 900-second cap expired, so adoption is easier than contribution on a modest CI box.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a quick full contributor suite on modest CI hardware: our run reached 54% before the 900-second test cap.

reviews.name: git-flight-rules
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 157 documentation packages in 22 seconds, but no build or tests ran because this 14-file repository is a handbook rather than a Git diagnostic tool.
reviews.skip_if: Absolute beginners who need Git's object model explained before running commands: the guide is arranged as fixes and assumes terms such as HEAD, ref, upstream, and rebase.

reviews.name: libuv
reviews.verdict: Our libuv run installed in 10 seconds and built in 30 seconds, but CTest ended with 0 passed and 2 failed targets after 49 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers looking for HTTP, TLS, WebSocket, or coroutine abstractions: libuv exposes lower-level handles, requests, streams, and callbacks.

reviews.name: firebase-ios-sdk
reviews.verdict: Our 62-second run installed 657 packages and found 11 moderate advisories in the nested Functions backend, while the Apple SDK build and tests were unavailable in that npm path.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring every shipped component to be open source: Firebase Analytics is excluded from this repository and distributed as a compiled binary.

reviews.name: awesome-cli-apps
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run Awesome CLI Apps because it is a Shell-labeled catalog with no Dockerfile or supported executable ecosystem.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who want install commands, platform matrices, or side-by-side evaluations: entries are usually a link and one sentence.

reviews.name: retrofit
reviews.verdict: Our Retrofit checkout installed in 57 seconds, but both the 13-second build and 14-second test run failed because the sandbox had no Android SDK location.
reviews.skip_if: Kotlin Multiplatform teams sharing one client across Android, iOS, JavaScript, and native targets: Retrofit supports Android and the JVM.

reviews.name: go-redis
reviews.verdict: Our run built Go-Redis in 47 seconds, but 5 of 35 test results failed after a 380-second run, so the official client still needs validation against your Redis topology.
reviews.skip_if: Projects pinned below Go 1.24: the measured commit declares Go 1.24 as its minimum.

reviews.name: agent-manager
reviews.verdict: Our Agent Manager run built in 47 seconds and passed all 56 tests, making it an easy trial for developers already juggling several supported terminal agents.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need cost or token accounting inside the manager: the README says cost tracking is not available.

reviews.name: navi
reviews.verdict: Choose navi when dynamic argument selection helps you use command recipes you can review.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need only command-reference examples; consider tldr pages or cheat.

reviews.name: microservices-demo
reviews.verdict: Our checkout service build finished in 36 seconds, but 3 of 5 test checks failed on a `status.Errorf` format-string error, so Online Boutique is better classroom infrastructure than copy-ready application code.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a commerce starter: the README says there is no signup or login, while payment, shipping, and email are mocks.

reviews.name: dust
reviews.verdict: Our dust run installed 63 packages in 3 seconds and passed all 166 tests, making it an easy recommendation for one-shot disk investigations.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who wants to browse and delete files inside the same interface: dust prints a report, while open issue 506 asks for integration with an interactive file manager.

reviews.name: hackingtool
reviews.verdict: Our HackingTool run passed 278 of 278 tests in 7 seconds after a 25-second install, making the core launcher unusually easy to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users: the README says the application supports Linux and macOS and exits on Windows.

reviews.name: DmNote
reviews.verdict: DM Note is worth evaluating for a customized rhythm-game overlay on Windows or macOS.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users requiring support from the main project: its README recommends a community fork.

reviews.name: asdf
reviews.verdict: Our asdf checkout installed 119 packages in 24 seconds and built in 25 seconds, but 5 of 41 tests failed, so the core was easy to compile without earning a clean pass.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need the core project to secure every installer they run: asdf's security policy covers core only and leaves each plugin to its creator.

reviews.name: C-Plus-Plus
reviews.verdict: Our 431-file checkout built in 64 seconds, and its test step succeeded in 0 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams seeking a versioned, linked algorithms library: the repository builds separate executables and GitHub has no latest release.

reviews.name: smolvm
reviews.verdict: Our smolvm run installed 338 packages, built successfully, and passed all 2,200 tests in 477 seconds total, making it the cleanest source result in this group.
reviews.skip_if: Hosts without Hypervisor.framework, KVM, or Windows Hypervisor Platform: smolvm depends on those platform virtualization backends.

reviews.name: x64dbg
reviews.verdict: Our x64dbg sandbox run installed its Python remote-server subproject in 21 seconds, but it did not build the Windows debugger, so the quick result does not prove an easy desktop source build.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or Linux users seeking a finished native debugger: the README defines x64dbg as a Windows tool, and the May 2026 release still calls the Linux debugger experimental.

reviews.name: gcx
reviews.verdict: Our gcx run installed 57 packages in 20 seconds and built in 4, but it exposed no test target and pip-audit found 1 known vulnerability.
reviews.skip_if: Operators on Grafana 11 or older: gcx detects versions below 12 and exits, while Grafana 12 is no longer actively supported.

reviews.name: blockbench
reviews.verdict: Our Blockbench run installed 735 packages in 31 seconds, but it had no default build or test target and npm audit found 22 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Studios that need sculpting, simulation, compositing, or photoreal rendering: the README defines Blockbench around low-poly models and pixel-art textures.

reviews.name: rspack
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed Rspack's 1,230-package contributor tree in 24 seconds, but the checkout exposed no build or test target for our generic runner.
reviews.skip_if: Projects pinned below Node.js 20.19 or 22.12: Rspack 2 requires one of those branches or newer.

reviews.name: vitest
reviews.verdict: Our Vitest run passed 2,086 tests but exited 1 after a single `test/edge.test.ts` failure, so the measured checkout was close to green and still not green.
reviews.skip_if: Projects pinned below Node.js 22.12 or Vite 6.4: Vitest 5 does not support those older runtimes.

reviews.name: swagger-ui
reviews.verdict: Our Swagger UI build succeeded in 55 seconds after a 1,854-package install, but the full test command exited with code 1 after 344 seconds even as Jest reported 866 passed and 0 failed.
reviews.skip_if: Contributor environments with a tight disk or dependency budget: our install pulled 1,854 packages and occupied 581 MB before the build.

reviews.name: crystal
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run commit 59835a3 because the harness had no supported Crystal ecosystem and the repository supplied no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Teams moving an existing Ruby application unchanged: the README says Ruby compatibility is not a goal.

reviews.name: pydantic
reviews.verdict: Our Pydantic run installed 39 packages in 89 seconds, but the build and tests both failed in 2 seconds, so this source checkout is not a clean recommendation for contributors.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require unchanged input verification but will not enable strict mode: Pydantic checks the resulting object and coerces values by default.

reviews.name: OCRmyPDF
reviews.verdict: Our build succeeded in 6 seconds, but the repository's test command stopped after 8 seconds because pytest did not recognize `-n`.
reviews.skip_if: People who want a polished point-and-click desktop app rather than a CLI Teams unwilling to manage Tesseract, Ghostscript, and language-pack dependencies Workflows that need human-quality recognition guaranteed on every difficult scan Users who only need OCR on photographs and do…

reviews.name: WxJava
reviews.verdict: Our WxJava sandbox installed in 63 seconds, built in 81 seconds, and passed all 272 Maven tests, which makes this large SDK practical to trial.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams that require maintained first-party guidance: the main README and linked wiki are Chinese, with no parallel English guide in the repository.

reviews.name: rollup
reviews.verdict: Our installation stopped after 608 seconds at a wasm-pack v0.15.0 download that timed out.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners who want a source checkout to install without troubleshooting, because our install stopped on an external wasm-pack download Teams wanting a full application framework with routing, development UI, and deployment conventions included Projects centered on CommonJS inputs that do…

reviews.name: stats
reviews.verdict: We did not run Stats in our 3-CPU Debian sandbox because commit 85543cb is a Swift macOS app, an unsupported ecosystem there, and the repository has no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users: the README supports only macOS 12 and newer.

reviews.name: k6
reviews.verdict: Evaluate k6 if JavaScript load tests, explicit thresholds, and several protocol options match your team's workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring demonstrated throughput or deployment results from this review Readers expecting the recorded checkout to have passed its repository tests Organizations whose software policy excludes AGPL-3.0 Teams whose primary requirement is Python test authoring

reviews.name: BetterDisplay
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox could not run BetterDisplay because the repository exposes no supported language and has no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who requires auditable or modifiable source: the public default branch contains only a README, and GitHub detects no language or license.

reviews.name: unleashed-firmware
reviews.verdict: Our Unleashed checkout occupied 199.7 MB, and pytest found 0 tests in `lib/nanopb`, so the 3-second nested build is not evidence that the firmware passed its test suite.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone without a Flipper Zero: this is device firmware, not a desktop radio toolkit or emulator.

reviews.name: desktop
reviews.verdict: Our GitHub Desktop install pulled 1,123 packages and occupied 1,232 MB, then its 124-second test run failed with only repeated `test failed` lines in the supplied tail.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users who require official packages and support: the README directs them to the community-maintained `shiftkey/desktop` fork.

reviews.name: LazyVim
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox could not execute commit 9997009 because the harness supports no Lua ecosystem and the repository has no Dockerfile, so we have no install or test result to offset the documentation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone staying on Neovim below 0.11.2: LazyVim now exits with an error on older versions.

reviews.name: lo
reviews.verdict: Use Lo for recurring collection transformations when its helpers improve the code your team maintains.
reviews.skip_if: Projects whose required operations already exist in the standard library and whose dependency policy favors using those directly.

reviews.name: resty
reviews.verdict: Resty is worth evaluating for Go HTTP, REST, and SSE work when its documented Go requirement fits your project.
reviews.skip_if: Projects that cannot meet the documented Go 1.23 minimum for v3.

reviews.name: awesome-react
reviews.verdict: Our 2026-09-07 sandbox found no runnable target at commit e6fd973, so awesome-react should be judged as an edited directory rather than software.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a ranked shortlist: the entries have short descriptions but no scores, maintenance checks, or side-by-side criteria, and issue 731 has requested sorting since 2017.

reviews.name: vtracer
reviews.verdict: Our VTracer run installed 83 packages in 9 seconds, built in 38 seconds, and passed all 172 tests in 51 seconds, making it the easiest repo here to trust for a trial.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that refuse alpha dependencies: the newest release is `1.0.0-alpha.4`, including the desktop apps and current library examples.

reviews.name: julia
reviews.verdict: Our Julia sandbox built the Rust MMTk component in 225 seconds, but its successful Cargo test step ran 0 tests, so it did not validate the full Julia runtime.
reviews.skip_if: Authors of short, frequently restarted commands who cannot tolerate compilation on first use: Julia's performance manual explicitly separates first-call latency from later execution.

reviews.name: awesome-cpp
reviews.verdict: Our lab found no runnable ecosystem or Dockerfile, so Awesome C++ works as a 1,392-link discovery index and should not be read as tested dependency advice.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting tested rankings or buyer-style comparisons: entries are short descriptions, without common benchmarks, security review, or a declared winner.

reviews.name: godot
reviews.verdict: Our Godot run installed 35 Python packages and passed its recorded build step, but pytest collected 0 tests, so it provides no native-engine validation.
reviews.skip_if: Studios expecting public console export templates: the README links a separate route requiring platform approval and private middleware or in-house porting.

reviews.name: TranslucentTB
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run TranslucentTB because the C++ repository has no supported harness ecosystem and no Dockerfile, so there is no measured install, build, or test outcome to lean on.
reviews.skip_if: macOS, Linux, or pre-Windows 10 users: the project is specifically for Windows 10 and Windows 11.

reviews.name: workmux
reviews.verdict: Our run of Workmux built successfully in 100 seconds and all 3,144 tests passed in 40 seconds, a strong outcome for a tool that can create, merge, and delete working environments.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who do not want a terminal multiplexer in their workflow: tmux is the recommended interface, and the WezTerm, Kitty, and Zellij backends are marked experimental.

reviews.name: bubbletea
reviews.verdict: Our Bubble Tea run installed 21 packages in 16 seconds, built in 13 seconds, and passed the reported test step in 4 seconds, making the measured revision straightforward to try.
reviews.skip_if: Teams migrating a v1 application without time for source changes: the upgrade guide changes imports, View's return type, key messages, and terminal settings.

reviews.name: checkstyle
reviews.verdict: Use Checkstyle if your team will maintain a Java coding policy and enforce it through a shared configuration.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose immediate goal is to rewrite source formatting automatically Teams seeking whole-program analysis of expression types and inheritance Projects unwilling to maintain a configuration and review compatibility changes

reviews.name: destructive_command_guard
reviews.verdict: Trial dcg as an extra command check if you can verify the hook and effective policy in your coding client.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone requiring an execution boundary that a caller cannot disable: the documented environment bypass disables protection for an invocation.

reviews.name: HelloGitHub
reviews.verdict: Our HelloGitHub run installed 35 packages in 10 seconds and built in 1 second, but tests were skipped and those results cover its Python support code.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking daily discovery updates: the README specifies publication on the 28th of each month.

reviews.name: awesome-rust
reviews.verdict: Use Awesome Rust to assemble a shortlist, then evaluate the destination projects yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need the directory to select a dependency for them.

reviews.name: bore
reviews.verdict: Use Bore for a temporary TCP tunnel if you can manage the forwarded service's protection and verify the deployment yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting Bore's shared secret to encrypt the forwarded traffic.

reviews.name: developer-roadmap
reviews.verdict: Our developer-roadmap run installed 31 packages in 10 seconds, but build and tests were skipped because this content repository provides neither target.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a learning website they can deploy from this checkout: the contribution guide explicitly says it contains content and no app to run.

reviews.name: compose
reviews.verdict: Our Docker Compose run installed in 44 seconds, built in 69 seconds, and passed all 38 reported tests in 33 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing scheduled jobs from Compose itself: the v5.6.0 release supports manual job triggers only.

reviews.name: mcp-grafana
reviews.verdict: Grafana MCP server is worth a restricted trial for teams that already operate Grafana and need an assistant to cross dashboard and telemetry tasks.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the recorded repository checks to prove MCP startup, tool discovery or live datasource access.

reviews.name: hiring-without-whiteboards
reviews.verdict: Our Hiring Without Whiteboards run installed 243 packages in 5 seconds and passed its test step in 1 second, making the contributor setup easy to consider.
reviews.skip_if: Candidates who refuse unpaid take-home work: the README allows unpaid exercises, and payment is recommended rather than required.

reviews.name: ruby
reviews.verdict: Choose ruby/ruby for work that needs CRuby source and build control.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only need an installed Ruby executable.

reviews.name: swift
reviews.verdict: Our run installed Swift's `cmpcodesize` utility in 33 seconds and passed 3 of 3 tests, while the full compiler guide recommends 150 GB free for development.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only need to compile Swift code: released toolchains avoid a source setup that recommends 150 GB free.

reviews.name: usage
reviews.verdict: Our npm run installed 274 packages in 35 seconds, then found no standard build or test target, so it verified the documentation toolchain's dependencies rather than the Rust product.
reviews.skip_if: Authors of deliberately unusual parsers: the specification documentation says Usage targets standard GNU-style options and cannot model every CLI.

reviews.name: DefinitelyTyped
reviews.verdict: Our 62,655-file DefinitelyTyped checkout rejected npm after 72 seconds because contributors must use pnpm, while ordinary users can skip the monorepo and install one `@types` package.
reviews.skip_if: TypeScript library authors choosing where to publish new declarations: the README tells authors to bundle them with their own package.

reviews.name: zx
reviews.verdict: Our run of zx installed 531 packages in 14 seconds and built in 19 seconds, but its test command failed on Node 22 before unit tests ran.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who require a green suite on Node 22: our test command stopped with exit 9 because Node rejected `--experimental-transform-types`.

reviews.name: wasmtime
reviews.verdict: Wasmtime merits an evaluation for applications embedding WebAssembly through controlled host interfaces.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean test result from this review before adoption.

reviews.name: omarchy
reviews.verdict: Omarchy is compelling if its screenshots, shortcuts, and chosen applications already resemble the workstation you want.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require Secure Boot or TPM to stay enabled: the installation guide explicitly tells users to disable them in firmware.

reviews.name: rayhunter
reviews.verdict: Our Rayhunter build stopped after 147 seconds because embedded web assets were absent, and the test command hit the same compile failure in 16 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a phone app that works on arbitrary hardware: the docs recommend the Orbic RC400L for the Americas and TP-Link M7350 for Africa, Europe, and the Middle East.

reviews.name: TypeScript
reviews.verdict: Our TypeScript source run installed 241 packages in 15 seconds, then both build and tests failed on an unknown Go module directive.
reviews.skip_if: Applications expecting types to validate external data at runtime: the handbook says type annotations are erased from generated output.

reviews.name: LACT
reviews.verdict: Our LACT build stopped in 42 seconds because GTK 4.8.3 did not meet the required 4.14 floor, and the test command hit the same check before running tests.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who wants the same experience on Windows or macOS: LACT is specifically a Linux GPU tool.

reviews.name: go
reviews.verdict: Our Go source install failed after 2 seconds because the requested go1.28.0 toolchain was unavailable, so commit a3b72a4 did not give us a working source setup.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers seeking a routine toolchain install from a clone: the README directs ordinary users to official binaries, and our source install failed.

reviews.name: git-ai
reviews.verdict: Git AI is worth a workflow-specific pilot if agent provenance helps your reviews.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring complete authorship evidence without validating agent reporting.

reviews.name: ruff
reviews.verdict: Our Ruff run installed 36 packages in 482 seconds, then failed its build after 3 seconds, so source-build readiness remains unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Teams with custom Flake8 plugins: Ruff does not load third-party lint rules.

reviews.name: sherlock
reviews.verdict: Our Sherlock run installed 48 packages and built successfully, but its 25-test suite finished with 1 failure and 2 errors, so use it as a lead generator rather than an identity verdict.
reviews.skip_if: Investigators who need every hit to be conclusive: open issues document false positives on catch-all pages, parked domains, and WAF responses.

reviews.name: grype
reviews.verdict: Grype is worth evaluating for image, filesystem, and SBOM vulnerability scanning, especially when Syft already supplies your inventory.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring this review to establish detection accuracy or production readiness: our sandbox did not validate either.

reviews.name: system-design-primer
reviews.verdict: The System Design Primer is the definitive, free starting point for anyone serious about mastering system design for technical interviews.
reviews.skip_if: System design experts looking for cutting-edge research or highly specialized techniques; this is a primer, not an advanced academic text.

reviews.name: tmux
reviews.verdict: Our tmux run passed a 19-second install, a 21-second build, and a 3-second test step, making this checkout straightforward to try in the lab environment.
reviews.skip_if: Developers requiring a native Windows program: the README lists Unix platforms and gives no native Windows route.

reviews.name: neovim
reviews.verdict: Our Neovim source install failed after 3 seconds because CMake couldn't find a Lua 5.1-compatible interpreter, so that path wasn't ready to use in our fresh sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a complete code-navigation setup immediately: Neovim's LSP guide requires separately supplied servers, configuration, and activation.

reviews.name: ESP32-Bit-Pirate
reviews.verdict: ESP32 Bit Pirate is an essential tool for any modern electronics workbench.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners with zero electronics experience; while user-friendly, it assumes some knowledge of protocols like I2C or UART.

reviews.name: awesome-codex-plugins
reviews.verdict: Our sampled Ontoly wrapper installed 0 packages in 6 seconds and reported 0 known vulnerabilities, but that result covers 1 nested package inside a 249-entry marketplace.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone treating catalog admission as a code audit: the README says the scanner is a triage signal and explicitly warns that a scan is not a safety guarantee.

reviews.name: flue
reviews.verdict: Our Flue run installed 1,292 packages, used 1,520 MB, and then passed a 159-second build plus all 7 tests, so the framework is working and substantial rather than lightweight.
reviews.skip_if: Teams adding one model call to an existing app: our install pulled 1,292 packages and occupied 1,520 MB.

reviews.name: pydantic-ai
reviews.verdict: Our Pydantic AI run installed 122 packages in 23 seconds and built in 3 seconds, but its test command stopped after 2 seconds because `pytest_mock` was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting a fresh checkout to pass its suite after the measured install: our test command stopped in 2 seconds because `pytest_mock` was missing.

reviews.name: harness-sdk
reviews.verdict: Our harness-sdk run passed 4,733 of 4,733 Vitest tests in 88 seconds, but the install left 11 known npm vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Small applications that only need one model call and a few tools: our checkout installed 443 packages and occupied 398 MB before any provider workload.

reviews.name: notfair-plugin
reviews.verdict: Try NotFair Plugin for inspectable marketing workflows if its hosted account-data path fits your requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require connected account requests and results to remain local.

reviews.name: opik
reviews.verdict: Opik is a reasonable trial candidate for teams that need tracing and evaluations together with an Apache-2.0 self-hosting option.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking proof of production throughput, deployment reliability, or complete SDK compatibility: our run did not establish those results.

reviews.name: openclaude
reviews.verdict: Our OpenClaude run installed 596 packages in 35 seconds, built in 24 seconds, and passed its tests in 196 seconds, but that clean result does not resolve the repository's stated distribution problem.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require clear redistribution rights: the LICENSE says the underlying Claude Code source is proprietary and Anthropic has not authorized this distribution.

reviews.name: ollama
reviews.verdict: Ollama is worth a trial when its model-management API and existing integrations fit your application.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the local API to provide authentication for shared access.

reviews.name: node_exporter
reviews.verdict: Our Node Exporter build succeeded in 41 seconds after a 21-second install, but its test step failed after 8 seconds with named collector failures.
reviews.skip_if: Windows fleets: the README directs Windows users to Windows Exporter.

reviews.name: bindery
reviews.verdict: Our Bindery run passed all 124 tests in 264 seconds after a 74-second build, which is strong evidence for the codebase at commit 87ebea6.
reviews.skip_if: People who only need to read or stream an existing library: Bindery manages acquisition and pairs with Calibre-Web-Automated or Audiobookshelf rather than replacing them.

reviews.name: hysteria
reviews.verdict: Our Hysteria run installed 35 Python helper packages in 7 seconds, but it ran no proxy traffic or test suite, so the lab result confirms a tidy helper environment rather than the speed claim that defines the project.
reviews.skip_if: Networks that block UDP outright: the full client configuration lists UDP as the only current transport type.

reviews.name: awesome-cloudflare-selfhosted
reviews.verdict: Our run added 0 packages, built the generated list in 5 seconds, and passed all 61 parser tests in another 5 seconds, so the curation machinery is unusually easy to verify.
reviews.skip_if: People looking for Docker or VPS projects: the inclusion rules explicitly send those to Awesome Self-Hosted.

reviews.name: DocsGPT
reviews.verdict: Our DocsGPT run installed 279 packages and built in 12 seconds, but tests stopped during collection and pip-audit found 3 known vulnerabilities, so production adoption needs a dependency and test review first.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only need local PDF question answering: the 2,500-file repo contains agents, workflows, connectors, team controls, several deployment paths, and a frontend.

reviews.name: cap
reviews.verdict: Our Cap core run installed 143 packages in 35 seconds and passed all 144 tests, giving the embeddable path a clean starting point.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a CAPTCHA to stop every browser-driven bot: Cap's own instrumentation guide says headful stock Chrome drivers and headless Firefox can pass its checks.

reviews.name: yuvomi
reviews.verdict: Our Yuvomi test run reported 12 passes and 0 failures, then hit the 900-second cap, so its full test command is not a quick confidence check on a clean box.
reviews.skip_if: People who want a managed account with no server duties: Yuvomi supplies the software, while you operate the host, HTTPS, updates, and backups.

reviews.name: distribution
reviews.verdict: Our Distribution build passed in 86 seconds, but 3 of 77 test packages failed after a 419-second run, so adopt it as infrastructure you will test and operate, not as a finished appliance.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that want scanning, signing workflows, replication policy, and a user-facing administration layer in one product: Distribution supplies the registry core, not that full platform.

reviews.name: wg-easy
reviews.verdict: Our wg-easy install took 11 seconds and used 10 MB, but its build stopped in 3 seconds because Docker was unavailable, so trial it on a Linux host where you can grant network capabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who need a supported Dockerless install: the project's Dockerless guide says this path is not yet supported.

reviews.name: v2ray-core
reviews.verdict: Our V2Ray Core run passed all 167 tests after a 54-second install and 75-second build, which makes the source tree a credible base for an engineer who needs programmable proxy routing.
reviews.skip_if: People who want a click-to-connect VPN app: the official newcomer guide starts with a remote server, paired client and server JSON, and a separately configured browser proxy.

reviews.name: Mobile-Security-Framework-MobSF
reviews.verdict: Our MobSF run installed 129 packages in 35 seconds and built in 1 second, but pytest found 0 tests and exited 5 while pip-audit reported 51 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need dynamic analysis of Android 12 or newer: the official guide caps supported Android targets at version 11 and API 30.

reviews.name: mailcow-dockerized
reviews.verdict: Mailcow needs at least 6 GiB RAM plus 1 GiB swap and control of 10 inbound ports, so it belongs on a dedicated mail host with a named operator.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to run it on a NAS, OpenVZ, or LXC: the system requirements explicitly say those platforms are unsupported.

reviews.name: audiobookshelf
reviews.verdict: Our Audiobookshelf run installed 429 packages in 9 seconds and passed all 354 tests, but npm audit still found 54 known vulnerabilities, including 3 critical.
reviews.skip_if: Operators whose dependency policy requires a clean audit now: our npm audit found 54 known vulnerabilities, including 3 critical and 33 high-severity findings.

reviews.name: keepassxc
reviews.verdict: Our measured build succeeded in 24 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: People who want a managed account with automatic multi-device sync and recovery Families or teams that need built-in sharing, permissions, and administration Mobile-first users, because the listed first-party targets are desktop operating systems Anyone unwilling to own backup, synchronization, and…

reviews.name: Sonarr
reviews.verdict: Our Sonarr checkout installed 908 Yarn packages and built its web UI in 50 seconds, but it exposed no test target for our sandbox to run.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a streaming service or a source of TV files: the README describes a manager for Usenet and BitTorrent users, and the wiki requires a separate indexer plus download client.

reviews.name: docmost
reviews.verdict: Our Docmost run installed 1,942 packages, occupied 1,306 MB, and built in 42 seconds, but the checkout offered no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Small installations that insist on one binary or SQLite: the recommended Compose file runs Docmost, PostgreSQL, and Redis as separate services.

reviews.name: setup-ipsec-vpn
reviews.verdict: The installer needs root access and reachable UDP ports 500 and 4500, so it belongs on a dedicated server you can rebuild.
reviews.skip_if: Shared or valuable servers with hand-maintained firewall rules: the installer runs as root and rewrites packages, IPsec settings, firewall state, `sysctl.conf`, and `rc.local`.

reviews.name: mediamtx
reviews.verdict: Our MediaMTX build took 4 seconds, but only 122 of 127 tests passed, so v1.21.0 is easy to compile and still needs a reproduced green suite before a source-based production rollout.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting built-in transcoding: the re-encoding guide requires FFmpeg or GStreamer to change codec, format, or compression.

reviews.name: WordPress
reviews.verdict: Evaluate WordPress 7.1 with your editors on the intended hosting stack.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who need this sandbox result to demonstrate CMS installation, publishing, or production readiness.

reviews.name: livekit
reviews.verdict: LiveKit deserves an evaluation when you need programmable media rooms and its SDK coverage fits your clients.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a finished meeting application without building their own product experience.

reviews.name: v2
reviews.verdict: Miniflux is worth evaluating if you want a focused feed reader and accept responsibility for PostgreSQL.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who wants to avoid operating a database Readers who need compatibility with older browsers People whose main requirement is training a reader to highlight or hide stories Operators seeking evidence here of production capacity, successful migrations or a complete…

reviews.name: romm
reviews.verdict: Our RomM build succeeded in 5 seconds after a 44-second, 34-package install, but the lab found no test target to run.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a ROM source or storefront: the quick start assumes you already have the files and mount them into the library.

reviews.name: nginx-proxy-manager
reviews.verdict: Our install completed in 28 seconds with 373 packages, but this checkout gave us no build or test target to run.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who require configuration entirely in Git and reviewed through pull requests Large platforms that need dynamic service discovery, policy as code, or deep orchestration integration Anyone unwilling to expose and secure a separate administration surface on port 81 armv7…

reviews.name: appwrite
reviews.verdict: Our Appwrite root npm check installed 1 package in 5 seconds but found no build or test target, so it says nothing about whether the 382,524-line platform is ready to run.
reviews.skip_if: Small projects seeking a single lightweight executable: the self-hosted Compose file includes databases, Redis, a proxy, executors, schedulers, and many worker roles.

reviews.name: ntfy
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox build finished in 2 seconds, but pytest discovered 0 tests and exited 5.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a full incident-management platform with rotations, escalation policies, and audit workflows Operators who expect every repository test to run through a generic pytest command Organizations unwilling to own availability, upgrades, abuse controls, and mobile delivery constraints Users who…

reviews.name: incus
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Incus for full Linux system containers and virtual machines when you can own the host configuration and access policy.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking evidence that we launched a container or VM, tested cluster recovery, or measured workload performance.

reviews.name: istio
reviews.verdict: Our Istio run installed 597 packages and built successfully, but 8 of 151 tested packages failed after a 467-second test step, so source adopters need an environment-aware validation plan.
reviews.skip_if: Small deployments that can solve routing and TLS at an ingress gateway: Istio adds Istiod plus Envoy sidecars or ztunnel to the cluster.

reviews.name: coolify
reviews.verdict: Our Coolify checkout installed 55 packages in 76 seconds and built in 8 seconds, but its available package targets gave us no test suite to run.
reviews.skip_if: Shared-hosting customers or developers without root access: the installer refuses to run without root or sudo and writes under `/data/coolify`.

reviews.name: vault
reviews.verdict: Our Vault build succeeded after 550 seconds, but the test command reached 900 seconds with 15 failures, including database tests that could not reach Docker.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams with a few static secrets and no staff to operate another critical service: Vault adds initialization, unsealing, policies, storage, backups, upgrades, and incident procedures.

reviews.name: netbox
reviews.verdict: Our NetBox install added 126 packages and 371 MB, built in 10 seconds, and reported 8 known vulnerabilities, so adoption needs dependency review as well as network modeling work.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a controller that directly configures network devices: the README explicitly says NetBox does not interact with nodes.

reviews.name: Stirling-PDF
reviews.verdict: Our 23-second install covered only Stirling PDF's 122-package developer-tool folder, so it proves the repo tooling is tidy but says nothing about server readiness.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who require every useful administration feature under a conventional open-source license: the README calls the product open-core and links SSO and auditing to paid offerings.

reviews.name: envoy
reviews.verdict: Our Envoy run installed 49 Go packages and built the detected target, but all 3 attempted tests failed, so adopters should validate the exact proxy and extensions they will ship.
reviews.skip_if: Operators seeking a small static reverse-proxy configuration: Envoy's xDS control plane, filter chains, clusters, listeners, and runtime guards create a much larger operating surface.

reviews.name: discourse
reviews.verdict: Our Discourse install stopped after 68 seconds on an exact Node engine mismatch, so self-hosters should treat version pinning and operations as part of the product choice.
reviews.skip_if: Shared-hosting customers using cPanel, Plesk, or Webmin: the official install guide says only Docker-based production installs are supported.

reviews.name: bentopdf
reviews.verdict: BentoPDF is an excellent first choice for an internal PDF portal because the useful work happens in the browser and the self-hosted image does not remove PDF features.
reviews.skip_if: Proprietary products whose owners will not publish their modifications under AGPL-3.0 or buy the separate commercial license.

reviews.name: puter
reviews.verdict: Puter is unusually ambitious and, based on our clean install and build, much more tangible than its grand internet-computer label might suggest.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a small, single-purpose file server, because Puter is a full web desktop Operators who require a supplied automated test target before deployment Organizations that cannot meet AGPL-3.0 obligations Very small servers, because our npm install alone occupied 1,152…

reviews.name: hister
reviews.verdict: Hister is one of the more useful self-hosted answers to the question, 'Where did I read that?' Its binary setup, full-text capture, query language, terminal UI, and cautious MCP output make it worth trying on a private machine.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to store copies of sensitive signed-in pages: the browser extension submits rendered text and HTML, and full HTML previews are enabled by default.

reviews.name: luci
reviews.verdict: Use LuCI when the device already runs OpenWrt and humans need to administer it.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a standalone Node web app: this repository is an OpenWrt feed, and its npm dependencies are documentation and lint tooling rather than a runnable router UI.

reviews.name: nomad
reviews.verdict: Our Nomad checkout installed 1,517 pnpm packages in 47 seconds, but it exposed no build or test target, so our run did not validate the scheduler binary.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations with an OSI-open-source-only procurement rule: current Nomad uses Business Source License 1.1 and later converts each version to MPL 2.0.

reviews.name: coder
reviews.verdict: Our Coder checkout installed 189 pnpm packages in 16 seconds, but it exposed no build or test target to the harness, so we did not verify the 1.47-million-line platform.
reviews.skip_if: Solo developers who only need one remote machine: Coder adds a control plane, Terraform templates, workspace agents, and a database to that simpler job.

reviews.name: firecracker
reviews.verdict: Our Firecracker source build installed 118 packages in 38 seconds, then failed because the linker could not find `-lseccomp`, so a source checkout needs more host preparation than the successful install step suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want a complete container platform: Firecracker exposes a host API for one microVM process, while orchestration, image management, network allocation, and recovery remain outside the project.

reviews.name: plane
reviews.verdict: Plane is one of the more credible self-hosted choices for teams that have outgrown a board but resent Jira's weight.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams that only need a shared Kanban board: Plane's workspaces, modules, cycles, pages, analytics, and service stack add administration they may never use.

reviews.name: go-ethereum
reviews.verdict: Geth is a sensible default execution client when you want broad Ethereum compatibility, current protocol work, and mature operator documentation.
reviews.skip_if: Operators looking for a lightweight mainnet service: the README asks for at least four CPU cores, 8 GB RAM, 1 TB of free storage, and steady bandwidth.

reviews.name: authelia
reviews.verdict: Our Authelia build completed in 229 seconds, but 4 of 25 test groups failed after a 510-second run, so adopters should reproduce the suite on their deployment platform before trusting an upgrade.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an identity service with no infrastructure ownership: production setup includes HTTPS, proxy integration, secret files, storage, notification delivery, and access rules.

reviews.name: seaweedfs
reviews.verdict: Our run of SeaweedFS installed 1,160 packages and built successfully, but only 14 of 31 test results passed before the 900-second cap, so it belongs with operators who can reproduce its full integration environment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that want storage they can deploy and ignore: the README says balancing, vacuum, erasure coding, and repair run on demand.

reviews.name: CPA-Manager-Plus
reviews.verdict: Our CPA Manager Plus run passed a 36-second build and a 51-second test step, but npm audit still found 13 vulnerabilities, including 10 high-severity advisories.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without CPA or CLIProxyAPI: the README says CPAMP observes and manages that gateway and does not forward model traffic itself.

reviews.name: kubernetes
reviews.verdict: Our Kubernetes run built successfully in 584 seconds, but the test command was still running at 900 seconds after reporting 438 passes and 0 failures.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams running a few services on one host: the production setup requires cluster networking, a container runtime, node administration, and coordinated upgrades.

reviews.name: strapi
reviews.verdict: Shortlist Strapi for visual content modeling and APIs consumed by a separate frontend.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the CMS alone to deliver their customer-facing website.

reviews.name: reactive-resume
reviews.verdict: Our Reactive Resume run installed 1,259 packages in 63 seconds, then passed its 36-second build and 136-second test run, so the code is healthy enough to trial but costly to modify casually.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors looking for a small frontend project: our checkout had 1,478 files, and the pnpm install pulled 1,259 packages onto 1,489 MB of disk.

reviews.name: code-server
reviews.verdict: Our code-server source install ran for 447 seconds and failed in native-keymap's node-gyp step, so most users should install a release artifact rather than build this 253.5 MB checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting user isolation, workspace lifecycle, and policy management in this one process: the README directs multi-user deployments to coder/coder.

reviews.name: rancher
reviews.verdict: Our Rancher build took 544 seconds, and its tests reached our 900-second cap with 184 passes and 19 localhost-dependent failures.
reviews.skip_if: A small team with one straightforward cluster: Rancher adds another privileged control plane, upgrade schedule, and failure domain.

reviews.name: netbird
reviews.verdict: Our NetBird build passed in 8 seconds, but the Go test command timed out at 900 seconds after recording 104 passing and 11 failing package results.
reviews.skip_if: Operators looking for a tiny two-host VPN: NetBird adds centralized management, signaling, relays, identity, policy, and an admin layer around WireGuard.

reviews.name: pocket-id
reviews.verdict: Our Pocket ID build passed in 38 seconds, but its Playwright run stopped with 2 failures and left 182 tests unrun, so test the complete sign-in path before moving real accounts.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that must retain passwords as a fallback: the README says Pocket ID supports only passkey authentication.

reviews.name: go2tv
reviews.verdict: Our Go2TV run installed 51 packages in 9 seconds and passed all 32 tests, making it an unusually low-friction trial for direct home-network casting.
reviews.skip_if: Households that want indexed libraries, user accounts, watch history, and TV apps: Go2TV is a sender, while its web mode exposes selected folders and playback controls.

reviews.name: sing-box
reviews.verdict: Our sing-box build succeeded in 107 seconds, but 3 of 18 test groups failed, so experienced network operators should treat a source build as something to verify rather than install blindly.
reviews.skip_if: People looking for a normal click-to-connect consumer VPN: the core is driven by a large JSON configuration surface, while graphical clients and profile providers sit around it.

reviews.name: firefly-iii
reviews.verdict: Our Firefly III checkout installed 781 npm packages in 29 seconds, but it exposed no npm build or test target, so that clean result does not prove the PHP application is ready to hold your financial history.
