reviews.name: ui
reviews.verdict: Our shadcn/ui checkout installed 1,680 packages in 61 seconds, but both build and tests stopped at an unavailable Bun command, so its contributor setup needs more than a successful pnpm install.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a package upgrade to maintain all their customized components: the README asks you to build your own library, so your local changes need an owner.

reviews.name: voyager
reviews.verdict: Our Voyager run passed all 12,084 tests, but its build failed after 3 seconds because catalog freshness requires full Git history.
reviews.skip_if: Gemini Enterprise users expecting folders and timelines: the README says only Prompt Manager supports that product.

reviews.name: faster-whisper
reviews.verdict: Our faster-whisper run passed all 19 tests, but its 62-package environment carried 6 known vulnerabilities in pip-audit.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a ready-made authenticated HTTP service: the README presents a Python library and points to separate server integrations.

reviews.name: awesome-claude-video-skills
reviews.verdict: Awesome Claude Video Skills lists 295 video-tool repositories, but its SAFE labels grade READMEs and installation steps rather than certify the code.
reviews.skip_if: Teams treating the SAFE badge as a code audit: the README defines the grade around READMEs and installation steps.

reviews.name: awesome-claude-5-5-videos
reviews.verdict: Use Awesome Claude 5.5 Videos to choose a production approach and inspect the sources behind an example.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting the collection's maintenance scripts to produce a finished film.

reviews.name: MiniCPM-V
reviews.verdict: Our MiniCPM-V run installed 35 packages in 9 seconds and built in 1 second, but tests were skipped because no runnable target was found, leaving model behavior unverified by our lab.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting MiniCPM-V 4.7 to load in stock Ollama without checking the backend: issue 1149 reports an unrecognized projector on Ollama 0.40.3.

reviews.name: pm-skills
reviews.verdict: Our PM Skills run installed 35 packages in 5 seconds and passed all 15 tests, making it an inexpensive instruction pack to try with an existing assistant.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting identical slash commands across assistants: the README limits those workflows outside Claude hosts.

reviews.name: burn
reviews.verdict: Our Burn checkout spent the full 900-second cap on the build and another 900 seconds on tests without completing either, after a 1,195-package install.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who need a fast full-workspace verification loop: our build and test commands each hit the 900-second cap while still compiling.

reviews.name: video-shotcraft
reviews.verdict: Our Video Shotcraft run installed 57 packages in 4 seconds and passed all 23 tests, so trying the skill costs little even though making a good film does not.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers expecting prompt-to-video with no production work: the skill requires product inspection, storyboarding, screen capture, Remotion implementation, audio work, renders, and final review.

reviews.name: crush-monitor
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 189 packages in 14 seconds and all 77 tests passed, so Crush Monitor's software path is in better shape than its playful premise suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone whose messages must remain offline: original chat text is sent to the selected model provider for analysis.

reviews.name: paperless-gpt
reviews.verdict: Our Paperless-GPT build finished in 2 seconds, but 3 of 11 Go test packages failed, including a root-package setup failure whose cause was absent from the log tail.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone without Paperless-ngx: this is a companion service, not a standalone document archive.

reviews.name: laya
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Laya if typed local decisions fit your application and you can own the accuracy checks.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need this review to establish prediction accuracy, runtime latency or deployment reliability: our run did not establish those results.

reviews.name: SemIf-OpenJev
reviews.verdict: Our OpenJev run passed 67 tests with 0 failures, but installation pulled 83 packages, occupied 7,074 MB, and pip-audit found 5 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a drop-in Jev-compatible web service: the README documents a scoring CLI, while issue 38 asks for an API server and pull request 27 remains open.

reviews.name: handraw-style
reviews.verdict: Our handraw-style run installed 35 packages in 17 seconds, built in 5 seconds, and had no test target, so the catalog is easy to try but its behavior is not regression-tested in the repository.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a tested software component: our run found no test target, no tests directory, and no CI workflow.

reviews.name: dlssg_for_sm86
reviews.verdict: Our harness could not run commit 9621db5 because it found no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile, so we have no independent install, build, or test result for this binary mod.
reviews.skip_if: Linux, Vulkan, AMD, or Intel users: the documented target is Windows 10/11 x64, D3D12, and NVIDIA RTX 20/30 hardware.

reviews.name: screenwriting-skills
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run commit 357d134 because it has no supported executable target or Dockerfile, so we cannot measure whether its 26 skills improve a script.
reviews.skip_if: Non-Chinese readers who require direct audit of every instruction: the README admits that runtime translation does not make the Chinese source bodies readable.

reviews.name: reef
reviews.verdict: Our Reef run built in 10 seconds, but its test suite reached only 33% before the 900-second cap and had already shown multiple failures.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams that only need an inference endpoint: Reef adds feedback ingestion, recipes, evaluation, version history, and release delivery around that endpoint.

reviews.name: Bonsai-demo
reviews.verdict: Our Bonsai Demo run passed 38 of 38 tests in 13 seconds, but it did not download or evaluate the 27B model, so the green suite proves the tooling rather than the model's answers.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who require stock llama.cpp: all Bonsai 2 formats still need PrismML's fork, and the support guide warns that one upstream format can load yet produce bad output.

reviews.name: qwen-audio-agent
reviews.verdict: Our Qwen Audio Agent run passed all 1,581 tests, but its 748 packages carried 3 high and 4 moderate audit findings, so the engineering depth does not erase dependency review.
reviews.skip_if: Small voice widgets that do not need a background agent: our install pulled 748 packages and occupied 397 MB.

reviews.name: SkillOpt
reviews.verdict: Our SkillOpt run passed 1,499 tests after a 116-package, 652 MB install, so the research engine earns a serious trial.
reviews.skip_if: Teams hoping one good chat transcript will improve an agent automatically: the research path expects benchmark splits, scored rollouts, and held-out validation.

reviews.name: gallery
reviews.verdict: Our 3-CPU, 8 GB sandbox produced no install, build, or test result for Gallery because the Kotlin repo fell outside the harness and supplied no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an embeddable inference SDK or headless server: Gallery is distributed as an interactive app, while its README points developers to separate Google AI Edge tools.

reviews.name: awesome-grokbot
reviews.verdict: Our awesome-grokbot install took 7 seconds, its build took 1 second, and its audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, making the catalog easy to inspect for a Grok Bot user who wants a faster way to find public configurations.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need tested agent behavior: the maintainer checks whether each share page loads but says no listed bot has been imported and behavior-tested.

reviews.name: Step-Code
reviews.verdict: Our Step Code run installed 304 packages, built successfully, and passed all 15 tests, making it a credible trial for developers already using Step's model service.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want a built-in choice of model vendors: the README says the default Step Code entry point has one built-in provider, Step.

reviews.name: reverify
reviews.verdict: Our Reverify run installed 36 packages in 17 seconds, built in 1 second, and reported 0 known vulnerabilities, but it skipped tests because no target was discovered.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs every `VERIFIED` result to be informative on current main: open issue 22 shows empty and all-wildcard claims receiving that verdict with positive weight.

reviews.name: A2A
reviews.verdict: Our A2A checkout installed 35 packages in 7 seconds and built in 1 second, but the repository exposed no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only need an LLM to call a database or fixed tool: the project's own comparison assigns that job to MCP rather than A2A.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Our constant-time-analysis run installed 36 packages in 19 seconds and built in 1 second, but that project exposed no test target for us to run.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting an agent skill to certify code as safe: the constant-time plugin labels branch findings for review, and its skill adds human judgment around analyzer output.

reviews.name: superpowers-zh
reviews.verdict: Our superpowers-zh install finished in 3 seconds with 0 packages added, but commit 78cb4f6 exposed no build or test target for us to run.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams that need the fork's extra material: the README sends English readers to the upstream project, while the China-specific skills are documented in Chinese.

reviews.name: yolov5
reviews.verdict: Our run of YOLOv5 installed 89 packages using 6,001 MB, then stopped test collection because `libGL.so.1` was missing, so a fresh project should start with the main Ultralytics repository instead.
reviews.skip_if: Fresh Ultralytics projects: maintainer issue 13796 says new models, features, documentation, and production workflows live in `ultralytics/ultralytics`.

reviews.name: eve
reviews.verdict: Our Eve run installed 2,573 packages and used 2,815 MB, then 8,673 tests passed and 1 was skipped with no failures.
reviews.skip_if: Small projects with a tight dependency budget: our install pulled 2,573 packages and occupied 2,815 MB before any model assets or application data.

reviews.name: garak
reviews.verdict: Our Garak environment installed 240 packages and used 6,435 MB, while its tests reached only 19% before the 900-second cap and had already printed a failure marker.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a normalized certification score: Garak's FAQ says probe scores have no scientific validity and should not be compared across different probes.

reviews.name: alphagenome
reviews.verdict: Trial the AlphaGenome client for a focused research question, then verify a documented prediction with your own credentials, coordinates and tissue metadata before scaling.
reviews.skip_if: Clinical decisions or medical and other professional advice: the documented prediction terms prohibit those uses.

reviews.name: openmed
reviews.verdict: Trial OpenMed if local clinical extraction and de-identification fit your requirements and you can own model and deployment validation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a compliance certificate or guaranteed removal of every identifier.

reviews.name: career-ops
reviews.verdict: Our Career Ops run installed 8 packages in 39 seconds and used 23 MB, but build and tests were skipped, leaving its job-search workflow unverified by that run.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking automatic applications or email delivery: the README explicitly limits the system to preparation and drafts, with submission left to you.

reviews.name: onnx
reviews.verdict: ONNX is worth evaluating for model interchange.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a complete model training or serving application Teams seeking evidence here that a particular model or runtime works Engineers who need a confirmed installation procedure for their environment, because our recorded installation did not finish

reviews.name: awesome-design-md
reviews.verdict: Use awesome-design-md as an editable visual brief, then verify the interface your agent produces.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose immediate need is working component code Readers expecting this review to establish compatibility with a particular agent or model Projects that require verified accessibility, visual fidelity or permission to reproduce another site's identity

reviews.name: models
reviews.verdict: Our TensorFlow Model Garden run installed 141 packages in 33 seconds, used 2,903 MB, and passed the build, giving TensorFlow teams a workable starting environment without a verified test result.
reviews.skip_if: Developers whose application already uses PyTorch: these implementations and training components depend on TensorFlow APIs.

reviews.name: mediapipe
reviews.verdict: Our MediaPipe pnpm install failed after 6 seconds because protobufjs@7.5.6 build scripts were ignored, leaving that checkout path unvalidated.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring no outbound usage metrics: the README says Tasks send performance and utilization metrics to Google even though input data stays on the device.

reviews.name: oh-story-claudecode
reviews.verdict: Use it if you write Chinese web fiction and already live in Claude Code, Codex, or a similar file-aware agent: the workflow is unusually specific, actively maintained, and more disciplined than a folder of prompts.
reviews.skip_if: Writers who want an English-first interface and examples, because the primary documentation and workflow vocabulary are Chinese Anyone expecting a polished desktop writing app with no terminal or agent configuration Authors who want autonomous publication, because this is a writing…

reviews.name: CopilotKit
reviews.verdict: Our CopilotKit run installed 4,778 packages and used 4,450 MB, then returned exit 1 from the test command despite 29 passing tests and 0 failed assertions.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a small chat widget with a light contributor setup: our install pulled 4,778 packages and occupied 4,450 MB.

reviews.name: CyberStrikeAI
reviews.verdict: Our CyberStrikeAI run installed 88 packages in 14 seconds and built in 1 second, but it skipped tests because the harness found no test target, so fast setup is stronger evidence than release confidence.
reviews.skip_if: Public or lightly protected multi-tenant services: the security model treats anyone who can log in as an operator, and the hardening guide calls for IP, VPN, or bastion restrictions.

reviews.name: maka
reviews.verdict: Our Maka run installed 985 packages and used 1,403 MB, then its test command exited 1 after 724 seconds despite reporting 261 passed and 0 failed.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require an approved Apache source release: the README says Maka has not made one yet.

reviews.name: dashi-ppt-skill
reviews.verdict: Dashi PPT Skill is worth a controlled trial for editable presentation drafts.
reviews.skip_if: Designers who need pixel-by-pixel control: the README explicitly excludes that use case.

reviews.name: cua
reviews.verdict: Cua deserves a component-level trial when an agent needs desktop controls, local VMs, or computer-use evaluation tools.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who require this review to demonstrate successful desktop tasks, VM startup, or agent task completion: our run tested none of those workloads.

reviews.name: modlens
reviews.verdict: Our modlens run installed 120 packages, built in 5 seconds, and passed 818 of 823 tests with 5 skipped, so its repository mechanics are unusually easy to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Security teams that require an OS sandbox around untrusted images: the security guide says subprocess isolation reduces exposure but is not a security boundary.

reviews.name: CLI-Anything
reviews.verdict: Use CLI-Anything if you can own and verify the wrapper for a specific application task.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing sandbox test command before evaluation: our recorded pytest command exited with code 1.

reviews.name: OpenMAIC
reviews.verdict: Our OpenMAIC run installed 2,546 packages and built successfully, but 1 test timed out after 8,848 had passed, so adoption should start with a pinned sandbox and your own release gate.
reviews.skip_if: Schools that need built-in student accounts, roles, or class isolation: the documented Compose setup is a personal installation with one owner, and OpenMAIC has no built-in gateway authenticator.

reviews.name: next-ai-draw-io
reviews.verdict: Our run passed all 174 tests, but npm audit reported 51 known vulnerabilities, so Next AI Draw.io fits a trusted local or tightly controlled deployment better than an exposed shared service.
reviews.skip_if: Operators planning an internet-facing service without extra controls: open issue 921 reports unauthenticated SSRF in URL import for versions through 0.4.16.

reviews.name: multica
reviews.verdict: Our Multica run passed all 5,961 tests but failed its 14-second build in `@multica/desktop`, so the codebase has strong test coverage and a real source-build barrier at the measured commit.
reviews.skip_if: SaaS vendors or product builders who need a standard permissive license: Multica's custom license restricts third-party hosting and commercial embedding without a commercial license.

reviews.name: baoyu-skills
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Baoyu Skills one publishing workflow at a time.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing test command before evaluation: our recorded command exited with code 1.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: If your organization lives and breathes Google Cloud, `google/skills` is an essential toolkit for building the next generation of infrastructure automation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone working primarily with AWS, Azure, or other cloud providers, as the skills are entirely GCP-specific.

reviews.name: prime-agent
reviews.verdict: Our Prime Agent run built in 268 seconds and reached 775 passing tests with no failures, but the full command was still running when the 900-second cap stopped it.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting the agent itself to contain untrusted work: the README says its worker and kernel processes are not a security sandbox, and generated Python runs with the user's permissions.

reviews.name: lumen
reviews.verdict: Try Lumen for its documented terminal annotation workflow if you can validate it on your own repository and terminal.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require this review to establish reliable interactive operation: our sandbox record covers installation, compilation, and the test command.

reviews.name: code2prompt
reviews.verdict: Code2Prompt is worth a scoped trial if you want an inspectable repository prompt with filtering and template controls.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need a measured comparison of context quality, token savings or repository traversal speed.

reviews.name: langgraph
reviews.verdict: Our LangGraph CLI run installed 66 packages in 41 seconds and built in 6 seconds, but pytest ran 0 of the 510 collected tests because it rejected `asyncio_mode`.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want a high-level agent with planning and file tools out of the box: the README directs that use case to Deep Agents.

reviews.name: agno
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Agno when you want to own both Python agent code and its service infrastructure.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a verified live model response or production deployment before adoption: our run tested neither.

reviews.name: ragflow
reviews.verdict: Our RAGFlow run installed 34 packages in 58 seconds and built in 11 seconds, but the test command exited after 10 seconds because a Zhipu AI key was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Small servers: the README recommends 4 CPU cores, 16 GB of RAM, and 50 GB of free disk before local models or optional components.

reviews.name: new-api
reviews.verdict: Our New API run built in 6 seconds, but 5 of 89 Go test packages failed, so adopt it only if its broad gateway console is worth your own release gate.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that cannot accept AGPLv3 obligations and the README's added visible attribution and original-project link requirements for modified user interfaces.

reviews.name: oh-my-openagent
reviews.verdict: Our OmO run installed 476 packages and used 2,178 MB, built in 58 seconds, then remained unfinished when the test suite hit 900 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Vendors planning to resell or bundle OmO: the Sustainable Use License allows internal business use but restricts paid distribution and service use.

reviews.name: chatbox
reviews.verdict: Our Chatbox run built in 171 seconds and passed 4,506 of 4,596 tests, but 2 attachment-ownership tests failed.
reviews.skip_if: Maintainers who require a green fresh-container suite: our run finished with 4,506 tests passed, 2 failed, and 88 skipped.

reviews.name: free-claude-code
reviews.verdict: Our Free Claude Code run installed 116 packages and built in 8 seconds, but its test command failed before collection because `pytest_asyncio` was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Release pipelines that require a green suite in a fresh container: our test command stopped before collection because `pytest_asyncio` was missing.

reviews.name: hermes-agent
reviews.verdict: Try Hermes Agent in a restricted environment if persistent memory, skills, scheduling, and messaging match your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need a verified provider connection, assistant conversation, messaging delivery, or scheduled workload: our sandbox did not test those.

reviews.name: osaurus
reviews.verdict: Osaurus merits a trial for Apple Silicon users who want agents, memory, and tools in one native application.
reviews.skip_if: Windows, Linux, or Intel Mac users seeking to install Osaurus itself.

reviews.name: mcp
reviews.verdict: Evaluate awslabs/mcp one server at a time.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring measured evidence that a server starts, authenticates, deploys resources or enforces permission switches.

reviews.name: Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep
reviews.verdict: Our Feishu bridge run installed 43 packages in 19 seconds and built successfully, but pytest found 0 tests and exited 5.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers who cannot review generated code, experiments, and claims: the documented loop can write scripts, run experiments, revise a paper, and continue automatically when `AUTO_PROCEED=true`.

reviews.name: xiaohongshu-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our run built xiaohongshu-mcp in 40 seconds and passed all 16 tests, so the code is easier to verify than the browser account it controls.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require an official Xiaohongshu API contract: the project drives the website, and open issue 860 documents reply targeting and emoji confirmation errors after page behavior changed.

reviews.name: nuclear
reviews.verdict: Nuclear is worth a packaged trial for desktop listeners who accept plugin-dependent sources.
reviews.skip_if: Listeners who need this review to establish reliable playback or catalog availability: our run did neither.

reviews.name: FunASR
reviews.verdict: Our FunASR run used 6,040 MB and built in 7 seconds, but pytest executed 0 tests because collection/setup ended with `SystemExit: 2`.
reviews.skip_if: Disk-constrained environments: our install added 155 packages and occupied 6,040 MB before downloading the model weights needed for inference.

reviews.name: page-agent
reviews.verdict: Our Page Agent run installed 742 packages and used 460 MB, then passed its build and all 4 tests, while npm audit still found 4 high-severity advisories.
reviews.skip_if: Server-side scraping or unattended browser jobs: the README says Page Agent is for client-side web enhancement.

reviews.name: FastGPT
reviews.verdict: Our FastGPT run pulled 2,598 packages and occupied 2,480 MB, then its test command failed because Turborepo could not find `@fastgpt/admin`.
reviews.skip_if: Companies building a similar multi-tenant SaaS without written permission: the FastGPT license requires a commercial agreement for that use.

reviews.name: Vibe-Trading
reviews.verdict: Our Vibe-Trading run installed 209 packages, used 800 MB, and reached only 62% of the tests before the 900-second cap, so it fits teams willing to audit a large research system rather than depend on a quick green check.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a fresh-container test suite to finish inside 15 minutes: our run was still at 62% when the 900-second limit expired.

reviews.name: nacos
reviews.verdict: Shortlist Nacos for combined discovery and configuration when your team can own deployment and upgrade validation.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that need only a few configuration values and have no requirement for a service registry.

reviews.name: awesome-claude-skills
reviews.verdict: Our Slack GIF Creator run installed 39 packages in 28 seconds and built in 9 seconds, but the repository supplied no test target, so Awesome Claude Skills is a useful catalog rather than evidence that every entry is safe to…
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require one uniformly licensed bundle: the README says individual skills may have different licenses, and GitHub detects no root license.

reviews.name: Figma-Context-MCP
reviews.verdict: Our Framelink MCP run installed 354 packages, built in 18 seconds, and passed its tests in 29 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot provide a Figma personal access token: the README makes that credential mandatory.

reviews.name: opencode
reviews.verdict: Our OpenCode install reached the 900-second cap without finishing, so contributors should prove the Bun workspace on their own machine before committing to it.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who need a dependable fresh-container bootstrap: our Bun install hit the 900-second limit before it finished.

reviews.name: servers
reviews.verdict: Our run built all 156 files in 19 seconds, but it had no test target and npm audit found 9 known vulnerabilities, so this is useful teaching code with a clear production boundary.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone shopping for ready-made integrations: the README sends that reader to the MCP Registry.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 39 packages in 23 seconds and built successfully, yet pytest collected 0 tests, so Anthropic Skills is useful source material rather than a pre-validated toolkit.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking one uniformly open-source package: the README says the DOCX, PDF, PPTX, and XLSX skills are source available rather than open source.

reviews.name: taste-skill
reviews.verdict: Taste Skill is an essential tool for anyone serious about using AI for frontend development.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require pixel-perfect, hand-crafted UIs built to a rigid, pre-existing design system.

reviews.name: Obtainium
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run Obtainium at commit 6a17d53 because it lacked Dart support and the repository had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting APKMirror downloads: the README marks that source as track-only.

reviews.name: herdr-projects
reviews.verdict: Our v0.2.34 run built in 44 seconds and passed 648 of 650 tests, with one logged failure caused by a missing `rsync` executable, so the core is substantial but the fresh-container suite is not clean.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who do not already use Herdr: the plugin requires Herdr 0.9.1 or newer and is not a standalone agent runner.

reviews.name: ok-wuthering-waves
reviews.verdict: Our pytest run exited 1 after 2 seconds because `cv2` was missing, even though 11 tests and 5 subtests passed, so source contributors do not get a clean fresh-container check at commit f5f38c8.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to risk a Wuthering Waves account: the project's English disclaimer says the publisher prohibits macro scripts and automated farming and may freeze or permanently ban accounts.

reviews.name: youtube-dl-gui
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Open Video Downloader if you want yt-dlp through desktop controls and can check a representative download before relying on it.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who require evidence of a successful packaged download: our run did not establish that.

reviews.name: volcano
reviews.verdict: Volcano merits a cluster evaluation when its batch scheduling policies match your requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a job runner that operates without Kubernetes.

reviews.name: kudu
reviews.verdict: Our Kudu run installed 564 packages, built in 16 seconds, and passed 2,613 of 2,614 tests with 1 skip, which is strong evidence for the checked-out code.
reviews.skip_if: Administrators planning unattended `--clean` runs without first reviewing scan output: Kudu's disclaimer makes the user responsible for deletions and system instability.

reviews.name: SpotX
reviews.verdict: SpotX is worth considering for technically confident Windows users who specifically want its documented client patches and accept the installation changes.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking a patch whose Windows behavior we have verified Microsoft Store Spotify users who want to retain that distribution macOS or Linux users choosing this Windows repository People who cannot authorize client replacement, update blocking, or downloaded script execution…

reviews.name: espanso
reviews.verdict: Trial Espanso if you want desktop snippets in YAML and can check them in your actual applications.
reviews.skip_if: People who need this review to establish desktop compatibility: our sandbox did not test interactive expansion or a released package.

reviews.name: WiiUDownloader
reviews.verdict: Our build succeeded in 28 seconds on a fresh Debian container and produced no test output (0 passed, 0 failed of 0), so this is a small, compiling, active tool with no automated test safety net.
reviews.skip_if: People who expect a legal, Nintendo-sanctioned storefront; this downloads from Nintendo's CDN and may violate copyright law Users who prefer a command-line interface or library; this is a GTK GUI with no CLI documented Anyone who wants a tested build…

reviews.name: selenium
reviews.verdict: Our Selenium source-checkout install failed in 11 seconds because pnpm reported an ignored esbuild build script, leaving that setup unresolved.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a fresh Node clone to be ready after pnpm install: our source-checkout attempt failed in 11 seconds, and the README directs contributors to a Bazel-based environment.

reviews.name: pi-autoresearch
reviews.verdict: Trial pi-autoresearch if you already use pi, need experiments that change code, and can supply a credible measurement script.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a standalone optimizer without pi.

reviews.name: OpenWA
reviews.verdict: OpenWA is worth evaluating for internal automation when you can accept losing or relinking a dedicated number.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs to automate a primary personal or business number without accepting restriction or ban risk.

reviews.name: agent-deck
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Agent Deck for supervised management of multiple coding-agent sessions.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified unattended deployment: our sandbox did not establish that outcome.

reviews.name: yt-dlp
reviews.verdict: Use yt-dlp when archive files, format selection and configurable download jobs justify maintaining its dependencies and update policy.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking desktop controls rather than command-line options; Parabolic provides an interface around yt-dlp.

reviews.name: skill-up
reviews.verdict: Consider skill-up when you need repeatable checks on Skill behavior, agent responses, or workspace changes.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking evidence that we successfully ran Codex evaluations: our sandbox did not test that workload.

reviews.name: actions-runner-controller
reviews.verdict: ARC is a reasonable choice for teams that intend to manage GitHub Actions runner capacity as a Kubernetes workload.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that want self-hosted runners without operating Kubernetes.

reviews.name: chinese-independent-blogs
reviews.verdict: Our Chinese Independent Blogs run installed 0 packages in 1 second, while build and tests were skipped, so the easy root setup establishes little about feed health or website operation.
reviews.skip_if: Readers requiring English descriptions and setup guidance: the README and frontend guide are Chinese, without a separate English README.

reviews.name: ai-engineering-interview-questions-company-wise
reviews.verdict: This 35-company collection is a useful interview map, and our lab did not run it because the repository is Markdown with no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Candidates expecting an official or guaranteed question bank: the README says questions come from public reports and loops change by team, level, and region.

reviews.name: HowToLiveBetter
reviews.verdict: Our EPUB run installed 1 package in 6 seconds and built in 5 seconds, but no automated test target checked the 649 advice entries or their evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need an authoritative English edition: the linked translation is maintained in another repository and may be behind the Chinese text.

reviews.name: polyledger
reviews.verdict: Our PolyLedger run installed 48 packages, passed all 41 tests, and reported 0 known vulnerabilities, making it an easy recommendation for historical Polymarket analysis.
reviews.skip_if: Live trading systems: PolyLedger stays 64 blocks behind the chain head and does not reconcile already-written reorgs.

reviews.name: helix-db
reviews.verdict: Our HelixDB build passed in 412 seconds and 1,844 completed tests had zero failures, but the full test command exceeded 900 seconds, so this is a serious database evaluation rather than a quick dependency choice.
reviews.skip_if: CI pipelines that need a quick complete source check: our build took 412 seconds, and `cargo test` was still running when the 900-second limit ended.

reviews.name: pathway
reviews.verdict: Our Pathway checkout installed 35 packages in 545 seconds, then its build and all 4 pytest collection or setup groups failed within 1 second.
reviews.skip_if: Windows teams that need a native supported runtime: the README supports macOS and Linux and sends other systems to a virtual machine.

reviews.name: excelize
reviews.verdict: In our Go 1.24 sandbox, Excelize failed to install after 39 seconds when commit 0434413 triggered a Go 1.26.0 toolchain download that did not complete module verification.
reviews.skip_if: Projects pinned to Go 1.24 or earlier: v2.11.0 requires Go 1.25, while the tested master commit declares Go 1.26.

reviews.name: bokeh
reviews.verdict: Our install completed in 52 seconds, but both the 17-second build and 8-second test command exited 1.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a source checkout to build and test cleanly with no investigation; our measured build and test commands both failed Developers seeking a tiny plotting dependency; the checkout and installed environment are substantial Projects that only need static…

reviews.name: quickwit
reviews.verdict: Our Quickwit build took 560 seconds and 2 of 2,178 tests failed, so its object-storage design deserves a staged trial rather than a blind Elasticsearch replacement.
reviews.skip_if: Metrics teams looking for a supported all-in-one observability database: the README says metrics are on the roadmap, and the 0.9 release calls the source-tree metrics work an unsupported prototype.

reviews.name: IPTV
reviews.verdict: Our Free-TV/IPTV run installed 35 packages in 22 seconds and built in 27 seconds, but it skipped tests and did not play any of the 2,053 stream entries.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs guaranteed channel uptime: issue 211 says URLs change often, and issue 1153 reports four named Slovak stations failing in one player.

reviews.name: google-maps-scraper
reviews.verdict: Google Maps Scraper is worth a controlled pilot when you need documented Maps-specific exports and can operate the collection process yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who require independently verified scraping throughput or extraction accuracy from this review Teams expecting our successful build to establish that the Web UI, REST API or SaaS deployment works in production Users seeking a maintenance-free hosted service

reviews.name: mongo
reviews.verdict: Our MongoDB run installed 93 packages in 20 seconds, while server build and tests were skipped, so the successful install leaves the database itself unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations limited to OSI-approved software: the README specifies SSPL v1 for current server releases, and MongoDB confirms that SSPL is not OSI approved.

reviews.name: opentelemetry-collector-contrib
reviews.verdict: Choose Contrib for required integrations whose individual stability and ownership meet your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring every included component to have the same stability or support commitment.

reviews.name: influxdb
reviews.verdict: Our InfluxDB 3 Core run installed 797 packages, then both the build and tests failed because the linker could not find `libpython3.11`.
reviews.skip_if: Flux-dependent users expecting the current branch to preserve the 2.x query model: the README puts Flux on the separate `main-2.x` branch, while 3 Core lists SQL and InfluxQL.

reviews.name: dbgate
reviews.verdict: DbGate is a good fit for developers who want one familiar interface across SQL, document, and key-value databases, especially when both desktop and self-hosted web access matter.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need every listed connector in the free edition: the README marks Redshift, CosmosDB, Firestore, and Turso support as Premium.

reviews.name: awesome-free-apps
reviews.verdict: Awesome Free Apps is a very good browsing shelf and a poor substitute for product research.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive users who treat inclusion as a safety audit: an open report says one listed app's expired domain now leads to an illegal gambling site.

reviews.name: milvus
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Milvus for hybrid retrieval and independently scalable database services, starting with the smallest deployment that answers your workload.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need this review to establish query latency, recall or production capacity; our run measured none of those.

reviews.name: kibana
reviews.verdict: Our Kibana install took 761 seconds and 3,122 MB, then the distributable build failed after 38 seconds, so building this source tree is specialist work even before Elasticsearch enters the picture.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that do not use Elasticsearch: Kibana is coupled to it and rejects several version mismatches.

reviews.name: flights
reviews.verdict: Use fast-flights for prototypes and internal searches where you can validate itineraries and handle scraper maintenance.
reviews.skip_if: Applications requiring this review to establish complete live itinerary coverage.

reviews.name: liteparse
reviews.verdict: Our LiteParse source build spent 378 seconds compiling before a Tesseract language-data download timed out, and the test step failed on the same download path.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting high-fidelity Markdown from dense tables, multi-column pages, charts, handwriting, or scans: the README directs those cases to the hosted LlamaParse service.

reviews.name: txtai
reviews.verdict: Txtai is worth evaluating if combining retrieval and model workflows reduces the application code you need to assemble.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring demonstrated retrieval quality or runtime performance from this review: our sandbox did not measure either.

reviews.name: superset
reviews.verdict: Our Superset run installed 163 packages and built successfully, but pytest stopped after 200 collection/setup errors because its SQLite test database lacked the `css_templates` table.
reviews.skip_if: Teams committed to a native Windows deployment: the Docker Compose guide says Windows has no official support.

reviews.name: airbyte
reviews.verdict: Shortlist Airbyte for its connector platform, then validate the connections your workload requires.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking measured sync throughput, deployment reliability, or connector correctness: our run tested none of these.

reviews.name: compose-samples
reviews.verdict: Jetcaster mocks audio playback and Reply uses static local email data, so compose-samples is a UI reference collection you must extend before shipping a product.
reviews.skip_if: Teams shipping a podcast player from the sample unchanged: Jetcaster explicitly mocks playback despite fetching real podcast metadata.

reviews.name: mcp-extensions
reviews.verdict: Our MCP Extensions checkout installed 255 packages in 9 seconds and built in 8 seconds, but had no test target to run.
reviews.skip_if: Developers promising the same experience in every MCP client: these extensions explicitly target ChatGPT.

reviews.name: solidity
reviews.verdict: Our Solidity source setup failed after 1 second because CMake could not find the required Boost 1.83.0 headers and components, so we have no completed build or test result to recommend from this run.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners looking for the shortest route to a contract: the README directs them to the browser-based Remix editor.

reviews.name: SwiftUI-Agent-Skill
reviews.verdict: SwiftUI Agent Skill was not executed by our October 9 harness because it had no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile, so we have no measured evidence of better generated apps.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting verified model-quality gains: our harness did not execute this instruction repository.

reviews.name: velxio
reviews.verdict: Our 7-second run installed 6 root npm packages but found no build or test target, so it did not verify the simulator application.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need every advertised board on premises: STM32, Raspberry Pi Linux, ESP32-C6, and partner boards are excluded from the self-hosted image.

reviews.name: pipenv
reviews.verdict: Our Pipenv run installed 79 packages in 53 seconds, but the build exited 1 and pytest finished with 199 failures, so commit 2de4850 is hard to recommend as a clean contributor checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Projects standardized on pyproject.toml for dependency metadata: Pipenv's documented workflow centers on Pipfile and Pipfile.lock.

reviews.name: raddebugger
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run RAD Debugger at commit 98467d0 because the lab lacks a supported C ecosystem and the repo has no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or ARM developers: the README limits current debugging support to local x64 Windows and preliminary local x64 Linux.

reviews.name: wtfjs
reviews.verdict: Our WTFJS run installed 448 packages and found 50 known vulnerabilities, so the global CLI is hard to justify for a handbook you can read on GitHub.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean dependency audit before installing a global CLI: our npm audit found 50 known vulnerabilities, including 2 critical and 37 high.

reviews.name: RustScan
reviews.verdict: Our RustScan run installed in 8 seconds and passed all 168 tests, so it is an easy recommendation for authorized TCP discovery before Nmap.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone scanning systems without explicit permission: the usage guide says the default 3,000 ports per second can damage a server or get the source IP blocked.

reviews.name: e2e
reviews.verdict: Our e2e run passed 3,159 of 3,161 tests, with 2 skipped, but its 1,415-package install occupied 1,861 MB, so the engineering is convincing and the local footprint is heavy.
reviews.skip_if: Projects with a tight dependency budget: our pnpm install pulled 1,415 packages and occupied 1,861 MB.

reviews.name: plexo
reviews.verdict: Try Plexo if independent connections are available and you can verify routing and completed-file integrity on your own system.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting Wi-Fi and Ethernet connected to the same router to add internet bandwidth.

reviews.name: responsively-app
reviews.verdict: Our Responsively helper run installed 546 packages in 57 seconds and built in 9 seconds, but it had no test target, so the clean build is useful rather than conclusive.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need proof on real phones or several browser engines: the MCP docs say previews run in the app's browser, not on physical devices.

reviews.name: pi-gui
reviews.verdict: Our pi-gui run used 1,760 MB and completed the build in 59 seconds, but the recursive test command still exited 1 after 107 seconds despite a 9-of-9 node:test summary.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac users: the official macOS build is Apple Silicon only, and issue 92 requests an x64 release.

reviews.name: ToolReplay
reviews.verdict: Our ToolReplay run installed 36 packages in 33 seconds and passed all 34 tests in 7 seconds, making it the cleanest measured setup in this batch.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking live re-execution: replay compares recorded responses inside one transcript and never calls the original tools.

reviews.name: birdview
reviews.verdict: Try Birdview 0.3.1 when reviewing an agent's architectural assumptions before a substantial edit would help you decide whether to approve its plan.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring enforced file restrictions or independently observed agent activity.

reviews.name: tailcat
reviews.verdict: Our tailcat run built successfully but only 10 of 15 test outcomes passed, so the project is useful for supervised one-off tunnels rather than a clean production gate today.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean test gate: our run reported 10 passed and 5 failed, including SSH, receive drop-box, and copy round-trip cases.

reviews.name: SwitchHosts
reviews.verdict: Our SwitchHosts run installed 441 packages and passed all 84 Vitest checks, but the full suite exited 101 because Cargo could not find `gdk-3.0`, so the packaged v5.0.2 download is the safer route than a source build.
reviews.skip_if: Headless servers or shell-only workflows: SwitchHosts is a Tauri desktop app, so a CLI such as hostctl is a better fit.

reviews.name: 3dviz-pro-max
reviews.verdict: Our 3dviz-pro-max run installed 35 packages in 13 seconds, built in 4 seconds, and reported 249 passing tests with 0 failures and 12 skips.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a point-and-click 3D application or a prompt-to-mesh model: the skill directs an agent and supplies starting material, but the host agent creates the artifact.

reviews.name: Ikemen-GO
reviews.verdict: Use Ikemen GO as a candidate for running or adapting M.U.G.E.N content if its compatibility policy and platform requirements fit your project.
reviews.skip_if: Projects that require every M.U.G.E.N bug or undocumented behavior to carry over unchanged.

reviews.name: Codex-Dream-Skin
reviews.verdict: Our run passed all 28 Node tests but the combined test command still exited 127 after the macOS-only work was skipped, so Linux can verify only part of this tool.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive machines where another local process must never inspect the Codex renderer: Dream Skin's loopback CDP connection has no authentication and can expose visible session data.

reviews.name: macos-sysdata
reviews.verdict: Our macos-sysdata run installed 35 packages in 28 seconds, used 37 MB, and completed its detected build in 10 seconds, but it exposed no standard test target to our Debian runner.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking reusable open-source code: the current license is proprietary and forbids redistribution or a distributable fork without permission.

reviews.name: coursebook
reviews.verdict: Our Coursebook checkout installed 42 packages in 9 seconds and built in 0 seconds, but it exposed no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Complete programming beginners: the README assumes a prior programming-language course and familiarity with assembly instructions.

reviews.name: GSYVideoPlayer
reviews.verdict: Our install stage took 70 seconds, but both the build and test commands failed in 10 seconds because the checkout could not find an Android SDK.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors whose build image lacks the Android SDK: our build and test commands both stopped because Gradle could not find `ANDROID_HOME` or `sdk.dir`.

reviews.name: zeron
reviews.verdict: Our Zeron build and test runs both spent 900 seconds compiling without reaching completion, so use the prebuilt v0.2.86 release unless you are ready for a large Rust workspace.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a coding model or agent subscription in the box: Zeron controls separately installed agents and leaves their authentication as another step.

reviews.name: skill-cabinet
reviews.verdict: Our Skill Cabinet run installed 263 packages in 9 seconds, used 73 MB, and passed all 64 tests in 2 seconds, so the core is easy to trial on one workstation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a shared or remote inventory: the product document defines one operator, and the server binds only to `127.0.0.1`.

reviews.name: Cybersecurity-Projects
reviews.verdict: Our `fastapi-420` run installed 108 packages in 16 seconds and passed its build and test steps, which makes this a credible study project for Python 3.14 developers.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers expecting 70 finished applications: the root README says full source is available for 42 of the 70 listed projects.

reviews.name: crabbox
reviews.verdict: Our Crabbox build succeeded in 333 seconds, but its test run hit the 900-second cap with 49 passing and 26 failing targets out of 75, so source contributors should expect a long investigation before trusting this checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone treating remote execution as a hostile-code sandbox: the README explicitly says Crabbox trusts the local user, repository configuration, project tooling, and coordinator operators.

reviews.name: 100-exercises-to-learn-rust
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 128 packages in 2 seconds, then the root build and test commands both failed on deliberately unfinished exercises.
reviews.skip_if: People learning programming for the first time: the course says it assumes experience in at least one other language.

reviews.name: deja-vu
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 2 npm packages in 5 seconds, but found no build or test target, so that clean run says little about the Go binary users depend on.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need one shared memory service across coworkers: SSH sync moves records between machines, while repository-carried team memory remains open issue 528.

reviews.name: UTM
reviews.verdict: Our UTM run installed 35 Python packages in 6 seconds, but a 0-second successful build cannot establish that the Swift app compiles.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux host users: UTM's front end starts at macOS 11 and iOS 11+, so they should use QEMU or another host-native manager.

reviews.name: lore
reviews.verdict: Our Lore install took 13 seconds and its 1-second build passed, but pytest stopped after 1 second on an unrecognized `--dist` option before it could run the suite.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that require stable APIs and on-disk formats today: Lore is pre-1.0, and its README says interfaces, formats, and APIs may change between releases.

reviews.name: termux-app
reviews.verdict: Our Termux install took 57 seconds, but both the 7-second build and 7-second test step stopped because the Android SDK path was absent.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need a persistent background workload: the README says Android 12+ can kill phantom processes once the system-wide count exceeds 32 processes.

reviews.name: omnyssh
reviews.verdict: Our OmnySSH build passed in 114 seconds, and all 886 tests passed in 42 seconds after a 14-second install.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who must keep saved passwords encrypted at rest: open issue 100 reports a password remaining visible in `hosts.toml` after key setup.

reviews.name: dora
reviews.verdict: Our Dora test command hit the 900-second cap with 2 tests passed and 0 failed while Cargo was still compiling, despite a 19-second install and 1-second build.
reviews.skip_if: Hard real-time control systems: Dora's tuning guide says it cannot guarantee hard real time, and its `--rt` flag promotes the daemon's main thread rather than every worker or node.

reviews.name: BrewUI
reviews.verdict: BrewUI requires macOS Tahoe 26 or newer, and our Debian lab could not run its Swift code, so our recommendation rests on the documented workflow and current issue record rather than a hands-on result.
reviews.skip_if: Macs below macOS Tahoe 26: the current README lists Tahoe 26 or newer as a requirement.

reviews.name: sharp
reviews.verdict: Our source build failed in 4 seconds, despite dependency installation succeeding in 30 seconds with 0 known audit vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a hosted image CDN with storage, caching and delivery included Browser-only applications, because sharp is designed around server-side Node-API runtimes Contributors expecting a fresh source checkout to build and test with no extra diagnosis Projects pinned below Node.js…

reviews.name: shields
reviews.verdict: Start with the hosted Shields.io badge catalog if it covers your README's needs.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who need this review to establish deployment readiness Teams expecting a small local installation: our recorded dependency footprint was 951 MB Readers looking for a hosted-service uptime or throughput benchmark, which our run did not provide

reviews.name: beekeeper-studio
reviews.verdict: Our Beekeeper Studio checkout installed 3,626 packages and occupied 1,738 MB, but it exposed no build or test target, so contributors get an installed tree without a project-level verification step.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need Oracle, Cassandra, ScyllaDB, Firebird, LibSQL, ClickHouse, DuckDB, SQL Anywhere, MongoDB, Trino, Presto, or DynamoDB for free: the README marks those drivers as paid-only.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Try one specialist on a bounded interface task if you can verify its report in a browser and inspect any edits.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring deterministic lint results or a verified accessibility assessment.

reviews.name: sofka
reviews.verdict: Our build completed in 151 seconds, but 4 of 1,362 tests failed.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a graphical desktop or browser interface Windows-first users, because the documented binaries cover macOS and Linux macOS teams that require signed and notarized release binaries today Risk-averse production teams that require a fully passing upstream test suite Users…

reviews.name: NativeScript
reviews.verdict: NativeScript merits a prototype when JavaScript or TypeScript and direct native API access match your requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking evidence here that an iOS or Android application compiled successfully Teams unwilling to prepare a native development environment Buyers who require reconciled dependency advisory results before approving a framework

reviews.name: aseprite
reviews.verdict: Our Aseprite run completed a 3-second build inside its Python benchmark subtree, then pytest discovered 0 tests, so it does not verify the desktop editor.
reviews.skip_if: Teams shipping a modified editor to customers: the EULA restricts distribution and limits source modification to personal purposes or contributions.

reviews.name: serverless
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Serverless Framework when its AWS service configuration fits your application and your team accepts v4 authentication and licensing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring an entirely permissive distribution: the npm module includes proprietary software.

reviews.name: notepad-plus-plus
reviews.verdict: We could not run Notepad++ in our Debian sandbox: our harness had no supported C++ ecosystem and the repository supplied no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or macOS users, because the README defines Microsoft Windows as the supported environment Teams needing a container-native editor, because the repository has no Dockerfile Buyers who require a reproducible Linux-based build result from this review, because our harness could…

reviews.name: Magisk
reviews.verdict: Our Magisk install failed after 2 seconds because stable Cargo rejected a nightly-only manifest feature, so the native checkout needs a different toolchain than our sandbox supplied.
reviews.skip_if: Owners of phones whose bootloader cannot be unlocked: the official installation guide requires an unlocked bootloader.

reviews.name: FFmpeg
reviews.verdict: Our FFmpeg source install failed in 3 seconds at commit 7ef5a79 because configure could not find a suitable NASM assembler, so the root README alone didn't get our fresh Debian sandbox running.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting the root README to cover a fresh-container source setup: it omits NASM, and our install stopped at that check.

reviews.name: glide
reviews.verdict: Shortlist Glide for an Android ImageView app that needs image loading and caching.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking evidence here that Glide ran successfully on an Android device: our sandbox did not establish that.

reviews.name: helix
reviews.verdict: Our Helix run installed 327 packages in 43 seconds, but its build and tests each timed out at 900 seconds, leaving the source workflow unverified in our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Vim users who require a true Vi/Vim editing model: the FAQ says the maintainers do not intend to support that paradigm.

reviews.name: ghidra
reviews.verdict: Our Ghidra build and test steps each failed after 2 seconds because the JVM rejected UseCompactObjectHeaders, so the 6-second install did not deliver a usable source build.
reviews.skip_if: Source builders restricted to Java 21: the tested README requires JDK 25, and our JVM rejected UseCompactObjectHeaders.

reviews.name: Tech-OA-Interview-Questions
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 4 seconds after a 12-second install, but there was no test target to establish correctness.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a self-contained offline problem set, because many rows send you to FastPrep Candidates who need verified official questions, because the material is rebuilt from candidate reports Teams seeking a tested Python library or stable API Users who require…

reviews.name: theia
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Eclipse Theia when you need to develop a custom IDE and can own application integration and compatibility testing.
reviews.skip_if: Developers whose immediate goal is to access VS Code through a browser Teams requiring a successful build or runtime evaluation from this review Buyers treating support for the VS Code extension protocol as proof that every required extension works

reviews.name: googletest
reviews.verdict: Our GoogleTest install failed in 1 second because CMake could not find Abseil's package configuration, so validate dependency discovery before standardizing on it.
reviews.skip_if: Projects stuck below C++17: the README and v1.18.0 release require that language standard.

reviews.name: go-modern-guidelines
reviews.verdict: Our October 5, 2026 run at commit 155dc7c recorded successful installation, build and test commands.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an automatic source rewriter rather than instructions interpreted by an agent.

reviews.name: try-omarchy
reviews.verdict: Try Omarchy is worth evaluating when you specifically want Omarchy alongside macOS on Apple Silicon.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac owners or anyone without macOS 15 or newer.

reviews.name: nushell
reviews.verdict: Our Nushell build succeeded in 449 seconds, but 62 of 4,390 tests failed, so commit 0468000 didn't give us a clean suite in a fresh Debian sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting existing Bash or POSIX snippets to run unchanged: Nu has its own language, return rules, and environment scope.

reviews.name: BMAD-METHOD
reviews.verdict: Our BMAD-METHOD run installed 36 packages in 10 seconds and built successfully, but its test command exited with code 4 after pytest rejected -n.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a green fresh-container test command before adoption: our test step exited with code 4 because pytest rejected -n.

reviews.name: iina
reviews.verdict: IINA is worth trying for Mac users who want mpv playback with graphical controls and macOS interactions.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users choosing a player for their own desktop People whose Mac does not meet the download's architecture-specific system requirements Developers who need a source build validated in our Linux sandbox Readers seeking measured playback performance, battery use…

reviews.name: triton
reviews.verdict: Our Triton source install reached the 900-second cap and ended with a failed CMake build, so this is specialist compiler work even though the user wheel installs with pip.
reviews.skip_if: Application teams that only need to train or serve standard models: Triton is a kernel compiler, not a model framework or inference server.

reviews.name: nvm
reviews.verdict: NVM for Windows is worth a Windows pilot when its documented shim or link modes and project pinning match your requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a manager for macOS or Linux as well as Windows; compare fnm for that requirement.

reviews.name: llvm-project
reviews.verdict: Our LLVM sandbox installed 35 Python packages in 32 seconds, but its build failed after 10 seconds and tests were skipped, so we have no working native toolchain result from that run.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only need a working Clang compiler: the 23.1.3 release provides platform packages, avoiding a full source checkout.

reviews.name: whatsmeow
reviews.verdict: Our whatsmeow run installed 39 packages, built successfully, and passed 2 of 2 tests in 71 seconds total, which makes the code easy to trial but leaves live WhatsApp behavior untested.
reviews.skip_if: Products that require voice or video calls: the README lists calls as unimplemented.

reviews.name: anchor
reviews.verdict: Our Anchor checkout completed its npm install path in 9 seconds with 0 packages added, but exposed no build or test target for the harness.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a JavaScript smart-contract language: on-chain programs are written in Rust, while TypeScript is a client and test option.

reviews.name: purple
reviews.verdict: Trial Purple if keeping cloud inventory and remote container tools beside your existing SSH config would help your work.
reviews.skip_if: Readers needing verified Windows support: Purple's supplied README documents macOS and Linux.

reviews.name: printing-press-library
reviews.verdict: Our Printing Press Library test run failed in 8 seconds because its compiled test glob was not found, even though installation and build both succeeded and npm audit found 0 vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive operators expecting secret redaction to hide an entire token: issue 1595 says the shared masking code leaves the real last 4 characters visible in errors, URLs, and dry runs.

reviews.name: ui-skills
reviews.verdict: Our ui-skills install used 687 MB, then built in 42 seconds and passed all 58 tests in 13 seconds with 0 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a component library, design tokens, or generated assets: the registry mainly supplies prose instructions for agents.

reviews.name: GitNexus
reviews.verdict: GitNexus is worth evaluating for indexed relationship queries when its license fits your use.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a permissive license: GitNexus uses PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0.

reviews.name: SenPaiScanner
reviews.verdict: SenPai Scanner is worth evaluating when you already have a proxy configuration and want endpoint discovery, optional Xray validation and client exports together.
reviews.skip_if: Readers choosing a general vulnerability scanner: the documented workflow concerns Cloudflare endpoints and proxy validation.

reviews.name: dsh-web
reviews.verdict: Choose dsh-web for extensions inside an existing DeepSeek Harness workflow, and verify one useful plugin before adopting the complete bundle.
reviews.skip_if: Readers looking for an independent coding agent without a DeepSeek Harness installation.

reviews.name: webvm
reviews.verdict: Our WebVM checkout installed 233 packages and built in 61 seconds combined, but it offered no test target for checking the virtualization layer.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations assuming Apache 2.0 covers the complete deployed stack: the README says organizational use of the public CheerpX deployment requires a license, and separate hosting of a downloaded CheerpX build needs a commercial license.

reviews.name: yazi
reviews.verdict: Yazi is worth a trial for terminal users who need cross-directory selection and previews and accept configuration maintenance during public beta.
reviews.skip_if: Users who require configuration stability through upgrades: the project explicitly warns of breaking changes.

reviews.name: moby
reviews.verdict: Use Moby for an engine contribution or a container system whose engine behavior you intend to maintain.
reviews.skip_if: Application teams seeking a finished container product with commercial support.

reviews.name: gstack
reviews.verdict: Our gstack run installed 242 packages and built in 13 seconds, but its tests still timed out after 900 seconds with several failure groups in the log tail.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a green fresh-container test gate before adoption: our run timed out after 900 seconds, with failures still present in trust-policy, environment writeback, dashboard fallback, and remote-caller cases.

reviews.name: treehouse
