reviews.name: arnis
reviews.verdict: Arnis is worth a small geographic-generation trial, with successful source setup in our sandbox and a documented persistent Java workflow at the tested commit.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need measured generation speed or verified geographic accuracy: our run established neither.

reviews.name: lancedb
reviews.verdict: Evaluate LanceDB for embedded retrieval, then validate the exact SDK and storage path with representative application data.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who need this recorded source checkout to build successfully in the supplied sandbox without further investigation.

reviews.name: check-if-email-exists
reviews.verdict: Evaluate check-if-email-exists when you can operate outbound SMTP and preserve uncertain reachability results.
reviews.skip_if: Applications requiring a guaranteed mailbox verdict for every address.

reviews.name: Legendary_OSINT
reviews.verdict: Legendary_OSINT is a well-organized and highly useful directory for discovering intelligence-gathering tools.
reviews.skip_if: Users looking for a single, installable software package; this is a list of links, not a program.

reviews.name: payload
reviews.verdict: Trial Payload if your team wants the CMS, React admin, and frontend inside one Next.js application.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a CMS installation independent of Next.js.

reviews.name: yomiyasu
reviews.verdict: Our Yomiyasu sandbox passed all 273 tests after a 17-second install, which earns the checking tools a trial alongside a Japanese-speaking editor.
reviews.skip_if: English-only editorial teams: the README, examples, and operating guidance are Japanese, with no English README provided.

reviews.name: pi-agent-desktop
reviews.verdict: Our Pi Agent Desktop run passed all 2,844 tests, but installed 1,059 packages and reported 8 vulnerabilities, including 5 high severity findings.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac users seeking official downloads: the README explicitly excludes that architecture.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Our harness did not run Android Skills because Kotlin was unsupported and no Dockerfile was available, so we cannot endorse its agent output from execution evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Teams treating automated policy output as release approval: open issue 226 reports incorrect app identity selection followed by a compliant status.

reviews.name: librepods
reviews.verdict: We did not run LibrePods because our harness lacked Kotlin support and the checkout had no Dockerfile, so we cannot confirm its setup or hardware behavior.
reviews.skip_if: Owners of unsupported, unrooted Android phones: the Android guide requires root and Xposed outside its named exceptions.

reviews.name: flux
reviews.verdict: Our Flux run passed 32 Go tests in 66 seconds after a successful 19-second install and 28-second build.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users expecting a desktop-independent package: the documented target is Arch or Omarchy with Wayland and systemd user services, plus Qt and desktop runtime dependencies.

reviews.name: HaloBattery
reviews.verdict: Our HaloBattery run built in 4 seconds but its test step failed, with 506 passing cases, 3 failures, and 14 collection/setup errors in the Linux sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or macOS users seeking a supported desktop tray app: the documented application targets Windows.

reviews.name: ai-system-design
reviews.verdict: AI System Design had no supported executable project in our lab inspection, so it offers a written design framework rather than a deployable application or verified performance results.
reviews.skip_if: Learners who need runnable exercises: the checkout contains Markdown and supporting assets rather than lesson implementations.

reviews.name: repowise
reviews.verdict: Our RepoWise run built successfully in 151 seconds, but its workspace tests exited 1 after 210 seconds and npm audit reported 12 high-severity vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Template-heavy teams requiring a complete dependency map: the language matrix lists Django/Jinja and other template dialects as invisible, plus skipped Svelte and Vue binding forms.

reviews.name: dashi-taskboard
reviews.verdict: Our Dashi run passed all 9 Vitest tests, but npm audit reported 13 known vulnerabilities, including 6 high.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring individual permissions or verified authorship: cloud usernames are display names and one password grants full access.

reviews.name: external-secrets
reviews.verdict: Our External Secrets Operator run built in 235 seconds but failed 15 of 29 tested packages, so commit 088f9e5 does not earn an unconditional production upgrade from this evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that forbid secret values from becoming Kubernetes Secret objects: ESO's core job is to create or update those objects.

reviews.name: photosuite
reviews.verdict: Our PhotoSuite build and test commands each hit a 900-second cap after an 18-second, 532-package install, so source adoption demands patience even on a 3-CPU, 12 GB machine.
reviews.skip_if: Studios that require proven lossless Photoshop round trips: the README calls full PSD compatibility an intention and a work in progress.

reviews.name: grokbot-field-notes
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run Grokbot Field Notes because it exposed no supported ecosystem and had no Dockerfile, confirming that this is a handbook rather than executable software.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for Grok Bot source code, an SDK, or a self-hosted agent: the repository contains guidance and templates rather than the product.

reviews.name: Compositor
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run Compositor because Swift is unsupported in the sandbox and the repo has no Dockerfile, so this review cannot certify its build or tests.
reviews.skip_if: Windows, Linux, Intel Mac, or older-macOS users: Compositor requires macOS 26 or later on Apple Silicon.

reviews.name: uniterm
reviews.verdict: Our uniTerm run built in 2 seconds, but 5 of 29 tested Go packages failed, including a WebDAV password round-trip test named in the log tail.
reviews.skip_if: Security teams that prohibit autonomous agents from reaching production shells: uniTerm can execute multi-round commands, and its built-in agent has a bypass mode.

reviews.name: window-sweaters
reviews.verdict: Our Linux run stopped at the platform boundary: the build failed in 8 seconds and the tests failed in 7 because the required macOS runtime and frameworks were unavailable.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users: the app links macOS frameworks and targets macOS 13 or later.

reviews.name: pstack-claude
reviews.verdict: We did not execute pstack-claude because our harness had no supported JavaScript ecosystem path and the repo had no Dockerfile, so this verdict rests on inspected documentation and repository activity rather than a lab pass.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want a quiet, minimal agent setup: the Claude Code and Codex plugins install a startup routing hook, and Codex requires you to trust it.

reviews.name: mjbatch
reviews.verdict: Our mjbatch run installed 44 packages in 117 seconds, built in 6 seconds, and passed all 43 tests, making v0.1.2 a credible small library for CPU-batched MuJoCo work.
reviews.skip_if: GPU-first simulation stacks: mjbatch uses a C++ CPU thread pool and makes no GPU execution claim.

reviews.name: UMR
reviews.verdict: Our UMR run installed 35 packages in 20 seconds and built in 6 seconds, but it supplied no test target to verify a retargeted trajectory.
reviews.skip_if: Users who cannot accept the SMPL-X provider's terms: the required body-model files are deliberately absent from the repository.

reviews.name: gander
reviews.verdict: Our Gander run finished installation in 23 seconds, then the build and test commands stopped in the Gradle wrapper's fetch path after 13 and 14 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs to edit, annotate, sync, or collaborate on documents: Gander is a local viewer with no accounts or network access.

reviews.name: codenotch
reviews.verdict: Our Windows-tree check resolved 486 packages, then both the 190-second build and 20-second test run failed during compilation, so Codenotch is easier to recommend as a packaged macOS app than as source you build everywhere.
reviews.skip_if: Security policies that forbid reading local CLI sessions, keychains, credential files, or editor databases, even read-only.

reviews.name: Kaku
reviews.verdict: Our Kaku checkout installed 736 packages, then both build and tests failed on an unresolved `macos` import, so the source tree did not validate in our Debian sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users: the README and FAQ say Kaku is currently macOS-only.

reviews.name: wechat-miniapp-radar
reviews.verdict: Our WeChat Miniapp Radar run installed 431 packages, used 629 MB, and built in 26 seconds, but npm audit found 17 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need English product and contributor documentation: the README, developer guide, interface copy, and generated weekly material are Chinese.

reviews.name: kitter
reviews.verdict: Our Kitter build completed in 98 seconds and all 204 tests passed, the cleanest verification result in this batch.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that want every repository to hold an independent, pinned skill copy: Kitter links projects to one maintained source, so updates reach every linked installation.

reviews.name: exodium
reviews.verdict: Our Exodium run installed 657 packages and used 413 MB, then passed all 277 tests after successful install and build steps totaling 30 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Managed desktops that prohibit unsigned applications: Windows and macOS releases are not code-signed and require documented bypass steps.

reviews.name: devops-exercises
reviews.verdict: Our Flask challenge install took 6 seconds and added 42 packages, but pytest collected 0 tests and exited 5, so DevOps Exercises works better as study material than as a verified software project.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners seeking a linear curriculum: the README presents 2,624 questions across many topics and warns that learning every listed technology is not the goal.

reviews.name: scriptc
reviews.verdict: Our ScriptC checkout installed 407 packages and built in 23 seconds combined, but its tests were still running when our 900-second cap stopped them.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting any existing Node application to compile unchanged: unsupported static code becomes a diagnostic, and dynamic mode still has compatibility gaps.

reviews.name: rift
reviews.verdict: Our Rift run installed 195 packages in 9 seconds, but its build and test commands both exited 101 after the compiler reported that it could not execute `cc1obj`.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or Windows users: Rift is distributed as a universal macOS binary and depends on macOS frameworks.

reviews.name: vol-rs
reviews.verdict: Our vol-rs run passed all 266 tests, but the release build took 218 seconds, so the port is easier to trust than it is quick to compile.
reviews.skip_if: Labs that require proven macOS analysis today: the README says the macOS plugins have not been run against a real Mac capture.

reviews.name: bend
reviews.verdict: Our Bend checkout installed 4 Bun packages in 8 seconds and used 7 MB, but it exposed no build or test target for our sandbox to run.
reviews.skip_if: Production back ends that need built-in TLS, HTTP, JSON, or regex today: the README says those libraries are absent and require foreign code.

reviews.name: PhotoGIMP
reviews.verdict: PhotoGIMP is worth a backed-up trial when Photoshop-style controls would make GIMP easier for you to use.
reviews.skip_if: GIMP 2.10 users: the documented requirement is GIMP 3.0 or newer.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Our commit a5321ff run installed 0 packages in 1 second and found no build or test target, so BuilderIO/skills is easy to copy but not independently proven by its own test suite.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require executable tests for every published instruction pack: our checkout had no test target or tests directory.

reviews.name: tty7
reviews.verdict: Our tty7 build ran for 637 seconds and failed because the linker could not find `xkbcommon-x11`, so source adopters should prove the full Linux toolchain before committing to it.
reviews.skip_if: Linux developers expecting a generic Rust image to compile the app unaided: our source build stopped because the linker could not find `xkbcommon-x11`.

reviews.name: gitdiagram
reviews.verdict: Our GitDiagram install stopped after 2 seconds with an npm `EOVERRIDE`, so self-hosters should budget for a Bun-specific setup and several managed services before they see a diagram.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need an npm-based setup to work unchanged: our install stopped with an `EOVERRIDE` involving the direct `dompurify` dependency, while the project documents Bun 1.3.x as its package manager.

reviews.name: tinycast
reviews.verdict: Our Tinycast sandbox stopped after 13 seconds because pnpm refused to run two esbuild build scripts, so evaluating the source is a deliberate macOS developer task rather than a one-command checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users: Tinycast is a native macOS application, and the current source requirements specify macOS 26 and Xcode 26.

reviews.name: act
reviews.verdict: Our Act build passed in 48 seconds, but only 4 of 7 test results passed and the 106-second suite exited 1.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require exact GitHub-hosted runner behavior: the user guide says the default images omit tools, and even properly installed software can behave differently inside Docker.

reviews.name: ligolo-ng
reviews.verdict: Our Ligolo-ng run installed 198 packages and built successfully, but 3 of 9 test targets failed, so pentesters should trial the exact routing and scanning workflow before adopting it.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who cannot create a TUN interface on the proxy host: the README says the agent needs no elevated rights, while the relay does.

reviews.name: agent-skills
reviews.verdict: Our Agent Skills run installed 1,603 packages and 1,024 MB, passed all 76 tests, and still returned 30 npm advisories, so this is a useful catalog to inspect rather than a security shortcut.
reviews.skip_if: Security teams that require a clean dependency audit before evaluation: our npm audit found 30 known vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 25 high-severity findings.

reviews.name: tabby
reviews.verdict: Our source install failed after 92 seconds, so Tabby is not an automatic recommendation for teams that insist on reproducible builds from a fresh checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone prioritizing low memory use, because the project explicitly says it is not lightweight Teams that require a clean, reproducible install from a fresh source checkout without troubleshooting Users who only need a fast, minimal terminal and no integrated connection…

reviews.name: iloader
reviews.verdict: Our build completed in 11 seconds after a 42-second install.
reviews.skip_if: People who want an App Store-like, fully supported installation path Teams needing a tested automation library or headless service Users unwilling to sign in with an Apple ID inside a third-party desktop app Anyone expecting automatic app refresh today, because…

reviews.name: carbon-lang
reviews.verdict: Our Carbon checkout installed 35 packages in 16 seconds and passed its 4-second build step, but it exposed no test target for our sandbox to run.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams choosing a language now: Carbon calls itself experimental, and its milestones reserve production use for 1.0 after the 0.2 evaluation stage.

reviews.name: deskflow
reviews.verdict: Deskflow is a reasonable candidate for a desk where several computers already have displays and the remaining problem is input sharing.
reviews.skip_if: People who need video switching as well as keyboard and mouse sharing Anyone treating this review as confirmation that their particular computer pair works Linux users whose systems cannot meet the native requirements and who cannot use Flatpak People expecting…

reviews.name: elixir
reviews.verdict: Elixir belongs on a shortlist when the Erlang VM's approach to scalable, fault-tolerant applications matches the team's needs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose deployment environment cannot include the Erlang runtime.

reviews.name: typst
reviews.verdict: Our Typst source build took 783 seconds and Cargo reported 50 passed with 0 failed, making a release binary the sensible starting point for authors who do not need to modify the compiler.
reviews.skip_if: Teams required to deliver LaTeX source or preserve existing document classes: Typst uses a different syntax and template system, even though its guide describes Pandoc conversion.

reviews.name: tokio
reviews.verdict: Tokio passed all 4,367 cargo tests in our sandbox after a 4-second install and 12-second build, making this checkout a credible starting point for an I/O-bound Rust service.
reviews.skip_if: Compute-only programs: Tokio's tutorial recommends Rayon for parallel calculations.

reviews.name: system-design-notes
reviews.verdict: We could not run install, build, or tests because the repository has no supported language ecosystem and no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking deployable software, because this repository is reading material Readers who need a finished, self-contained course, because the README calls the notes a work in progress Organizations that require a clearly stated open-source license

reviews.name: wloc
reviews.verdict: Our wloc Worker install took 7 seconds and all 22 tests passed, but iOS 27 beta 6 blocks the certificate interception the complete tool depends on.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone on iOS 27 beta 6 or later: the README says Apple blocks the required MITM interception at certificate validation.

reviews.name: PowerToys
reviews.verdict: PowerToys is worth evaluating if several tools in its documented collection address your Windows workflow.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking a supported macOS, Linux or 32-bit Windows installation: Microsoft's installation requirements specify Windows 11 or Windows 10 version 2004 or newer, with x64 or ARM64 hardware.

reviews.name: tabler-icons
reviews.verdict: Our repository build and test commands both exited 137 at commit a4ce140 on October 12, 2026.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who require a demonstrated successful monorepo build in our recorded sandbox Teams assuming every outline icon has a filled equivalent Readers seeking measured application bundle size, rendering performance or accessibility results

reviews.name: gpui-kit
reviews.verdict: Evaluate GPUI Kit for its supplied Rust UI layers if you can first verify native setup on your target machines.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a successful sandbox build as a prerequisite: our recorded build and test commands both stopped at linking.

reviews.name: ImHex
reviews.verdict: Our ImHex source install failed after 2 seconds because CMake could not find dbus-1, so a fresh Debian checkout needs system preparation before it can become a working editor.
reviews.skip_if: Teams using parsed bitfields as evidence without independent checks: open issue 2929 reports incorrect values with implicit alignment.

reviews.name: sequelize
reviews.verdict: Our Sequelize source build failed after 100 seconds at @sequelize/cli:build, so contributors should investigate that failure before assuming the checkout is ready.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a stable newest-major API: the README still labels Sequelize 7 alpha.

reviews.name: loguru
reviews.verdict: Loguru merits an application trial when you own sink configuration and want a concise logging interface.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting exception-variable diagnostics to be safe for sensitive production data without configuration.

reviews.name: waveterm
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Wave Terminal if remote editing and previews address a concrete workstation need.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who require a verified desktop build or performance benchmark before choosing a terminal Teams that need credential-storage behavior and dependency advisory applicability established before approval Users expecting documented AI command execution: the supplied commit-specific README lists that capability as…

reviews.name: bytebase
reviews.verdict: Bytebase merits a controlled trial when database change approvals and access governance are both requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose immediate requirement is only schema migration delivery; compare Liquibase and Atlas first.

reviews.name: delta
reviews.verdict: Try delta when syntax highlighting and wrapped side-by-side views meet your terminal Git review needs.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who primarily need structural comparison of code; consider Difftastic for that task.

reviews.name: Hyprland
reviews.verdict: Our Hyprland sandbox installed 36 packages in 135 seconds and built the Tracy Python subproject in 1 second, then pytest exited with code 5 after finding no tests.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a complete desktop from the compositor package: the installation guide assigns apps and integrations to the user, and the utilities guide requires separate services for notifications and screen sharing.

reviews.name: bevy
reviews.verdict: Our Bevy run installed 523 packages in 18 seconds and built successfully in 527 seconds, but the test command timed out at 900 seconds with compilation still in the log.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a stable engine API throughout development: the README warns of breaking releases and migrations that may be difficult.

reviews.name: mermaid
reviews.verdict: Choose Mermaid when diagram definitions should change alongside reviewed documentation, especially if your host already renders them.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring fixed visual placement across renderer upgrades.

reviews.name: context-engineering-kit
reviews.verdict: Context Engineering Kit is worth evaluating one plugin at a time if Claude Code is your main client.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting identical behavior across coding assistants.

reviews.name: luvus
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Luvus for coordinating several coding agents, but validate delivery, search behavior and session recovery before relying on it.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing test command at the reviewed commit.

reviews.name: plannotator
reviews.verdict: Plannotator is worth evaluating when you need human annotations returned to a coding agent.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified account of the released binary or browser experience: our run did not test those workflows.

reviews.name: ipatool
reviews.verdict: ipatool is worth evaluating when App Store package retrieval needs a command-line interface.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking evidence here that authenticated downloads work: our sandbox did not test that workload.

reviews.name: gitbutler
reviews.verdict: Our GitButler install failed after 9 seconds before it produced a build or test result, so source contributors should expect to fix the runtime and pnpm configuration before judging the code.
reviews.skip_if: Companies building a competing Git client or service: the FSL-1.1-MIT license bars competing use until each version reaches its two-year conversion date.

reviews.name: claude-plugins-community
reviews.verdict: Use this marketplace when you want broad Claude plugin choice and are prepared to inspect each plugin before installation.
reviews.skip_if: Authors who want to submit or fix a listing with a normal pull request: the README says direct pull requests are closed automatically and submissions must use Anthropic's form.

reviews.name: security-audit-skill
reviews.verdict: Use this skill when you already trust your coding agent with a repository and want a disciplined, adversarial workflow for finding new bugs that scanners may miss.
reviews.skip_if: Agent hosts without reliable parallel subagents: the README makes them a requirement, and issue #11 reports that Antigravity terminates the parallel workers.

reviews.name: open-code-review
reviews.verdict: Our Open Code Review checkout failed its npm install in 8 seconds because the requested v0.0.0 Linux binary returned HTTP 404, leaving the review workflow untested in our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting npm installation inside a source checkout to work immediately: our commit selected version 0.0.0 and failed to download its binary.

reviews.name: warp
reviews.verdict: Our Warp run installed 1,410 packages in 91 seconds, but both build and tests timed out at 900 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting this checkout to provide the whole hosted service: the README calls it the client codebase, and the engineering guide connects it to a separate warp-server.

reviews.name: fscan
reviews.verdict: Trial fscan when its combined discovery and active-assessment modules match your authorized work.
reviews.skip_if: Administrators who need a validated asset inventory without conducting their own accuracy checks.

reviews.name: dsh-anchored-standard
reviews.verdict: Keep dsh-anchored-standard on the shortlist for request-shaping research, provided you can own its compatibility work.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need the maintainer to accept bug reports or compatibility patches: the repository was frozen on September 10, 2026.

reviews.name: developer-portfolios
reviews.verdict: Developer Portfolios is useful for finding examples before writing or redesigning a personal site.
reviews.skip_if: Readers expecting a portfolio website codebase to deploy.

reviews.name: zero
reviews.verdict: Trial Zero if hosted and local model choice fits your workflow and you can supervise the evaluation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking measured coding quality, runtime performance or successful automation from this review.

reviews.name: deepsec
reviews.verdict: Our Deepsec run built in 58 seconds and passed 2,379 of 2,411 tests, but one assertion failed, so the codebase is close to green rather than clean at commit a008d3e.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for predictable low-cost scanning: the README says large-codebase runs can cost thousands or tens of thousands of dollars at high thinking levels.

reviews.name: shannon
reviews.verdict: Our Shannon run installed 416 packages in 7 seconds and built in 11 seconds, but supplied no test result or completed pentest.
reviews.skip_if: Teams testing only an external URL: the open-source edition requires source access, while black-box testing belongs to commercial editions.

reviews.name: mubeng
reviews.verdict: Mubeng is worth evaluating for an existing authorized proxy pool when an HTTP listener fits your clients.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that require Mubeng itself to expose a SOCKS listener.

reviews.name: wails
reviews.verdict: Our Wails v2 build succeeded in 41 seconds, but the test step reported 9 failures out of 57, leaving this checkout short of a clean validation result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing one bundled rendering engine: Wails uses native engines, so a working interface on one platform does not establish compatibility elsewhere.

reviews.name: OpenCADStudio
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Open CAD Studio on copied drawings if its native DWG/DXF workflow or browser access fits your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing demonstrated compatibility with their production drawings before evaluation: our sandbox did not perform that qualification.

reviews.name: opencode
reviews.verdict: OpenCode merits a small trial if its terminal workflow and provider connections fit your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who require this review to demonstrate successful model-backed editing: our run did not test that workload.

reviews.name: lazydocker
reviews.verdict: Our Lazydocker run built in 34 seconds and passed all 12 reported Go tests, but an October user report shows the published Docker image failing to start against a current daemon.
reviews.skip_if: Users choosing the published Docker image to avoid compatibility work: open issue 846 reports that image rejecting a current daemon, and the README separately warns about missing logs and CPU usage in containerized runs.

reviews.name: ripgrep
reviews.verdict: ripgrep is a reasonable choice for daily source-code search when its default filtering matches your task.
reviews.skip_if: Authors who require a ubiquitous, POSIX-conforming command: the README recommends grep for that requirement.

reviews.name: RAG-Anything
reviews.verdict: RAG-Anything merits a controlled pilot when answers depend on mixed document content and a Python team can own parser and model integration.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing source suite before adoption: our recorded pytest run reported 200 failures.

reviews.name: unreal-agent
reviews.verdict: Our Unreal Agent run installed in 16 seconds, built in 24 seconds, and passed all 54 tests, making the measured checkout a practical developer trial.
reviews.skip_if: Users inspecting untrusted repositories with real provider credentials: issue 5 and its maintainer reply describe a runner that trusts workspace configuration.

reviews.name: jev-pruner
reviews.verdict: Our jev-pruner run installed 53 packages, passed all 291 tests, and reported 0 audit findings, so the offline pruning logic is better tested than most agent add-ons.
reviews.skip_if: Work involving secrets or private source that cannot leave your environment: the README says its credential heuristic does not redact content or stop it from being sent to Jev.

reviews.name: llm-d-router
reviews.verdict: Evaluate llm-d Router if endpoint placement across Kubernetes model servers is the problem you need to solve.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only need to serve a model on one machine and have no pool of endpoints to schedule.

reviews.name: kev
reviews.verdict: Our Kev install consumed 6,971 MB and its tests failed after 239 seconds, even though the 7-second build passed, so this is a serious ML stack rather than a small Python utility.
reviews.skip_if: Chat, summarization, or open-ended answers: Kev scores supplied options and does not generate prose.

reviews.name: ag-ui
reviews.verdict: Our AG-UI run installed 2,336 packages, then both the build and test wrappers exited 130 within 13 seconds, so the protocol deserves a focused package trial before any team adopts the whole monorepo.
reviews.skip_if: Apps that only need to connect an agent to tools or data: the README assigns that job to MCP, while AG-UI covers the agent-to-user interface connection.

reviews.name: agent-toolkit-for-aws
reviews.verdict: Our lab produced no install or test result because this Python repository had no supported harness path and no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot give an agent any AWS execution path: the managed MCP server can call AWS APIs and run scripts, so IAM design is part of setup.

reviews.name: mlc-llm
reviews.verdict: Our MLC LLM run built in 18 seconds but pytest stopped with 200 collection/setup errors and no passed test, so commit af58bcb is a high-capability deployment stack that needs a target-specific proof before adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Release pipelines that require a clean full upstream suite: our run stopped with 200 collection/setup errors, 0 passed tests, and 0 failed test cases.

reviews.name: claude-skills
reviews.verdict: Our claude-skills checkout built in 4 seconds, but pytest ran 0 tests and crashed during collection when an evaluator called `sys.exit(1)`.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a small, uniformly reviewed collection: the README advertises 388 skills across 20 domains, and individual packages vary widely in scope and authority.

reviews.name: 12306-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our 12306-mcp run installed 240 packages in 21 seconds and passed its build and launch-style test, but npm audit still found 5 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting ticket purchase or reservation: the README describes search tools, and open issue 60 asks for ordering as a missing feature.

reviews.name: dictionary-of-ai-coding
reviews.verdict: Our 6-second install pulled 42 packages and 49 MB, while the repository offered no build or test target, confirming that this is a reading resource with a small generator rather than a software tool.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs to copy, translate, or redistribute the entries under clear terms: the repository has no license, and open issue 21 asks the author to resolve that ambiguity.

reviews.name: reversa
reviews.verdict: Our 80-second Reversa install added 61 packages and passed an audit with 0 known vulnerabilities, but the measured commit exposed no build or test target for us to run.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose change-control rules cannot rely on agent instructions as a safety boundary: the README tells users to commit, keep a remote copy, and make a folder backup because AI agents can make mistakes.

reviews.name: llamafile
reviews.verdict: Our test run ended with 7 passed and 2 errors from missing wget and appium modules, so llamafile is not a turnkey development checkout despite its one-file runtime pitch.
reviews.skip_if: Users on Windows who need single-file models larger than 4 GB, since the README states executables over 4 GB will not run there Teams that need hosted, autoscaled inference with model versioning, billing, and an SLA, which a single local…

reviews.name: distilly

reviews.name: threeui

reviews.name: pdfcn

reviews.name: kage
reviews.verdict: Use Kage as a reference, a visual benchmark, or the starting point for a private experiment.

reviews.name: up

reviews.name: Libraries.dev

reviews.name: blitz

reviews.name: Ghost-Downloader-3
reviews.verdict: Our Ghost Downloader run installed 34 packages in 18 seconds, but tests stopped after 1 second because aiohttp was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Users on older systems: the README requires Windows 10+, macOS 13+, or glibc 2.35+ on Linux, and warns about CPUs without AVX.

reviews.name: invisible_dots
reviews.verdict: Our Invisible Dots run built in 40 seconds and passed 2,102 of 2,106 Vitest cases, but one secret-input test failed, so its broad suite was close rather than clean.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or ARM users: the guide supports only Linux and Windows on x86-64 with hardware virtualization.

reviews.name: typesafe-computer-use
reviews.verdict: Our run passed 729 tests with 0 failures after an 18-second install, so TypeSafe Computer Use has far more engineering underneath it than most two-week-old agent experiments.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs dependable unattended desktop automation today: the README labels jev beta, and open issue 58 reports six real-machine bugs on the commit we tested.

reviews.name: MacDuo
reviews.verdict: Mac Duo v0.1.15 delivers six lid-tracked effects, but its public builds are not notarized and several common MacBook models are unsupported.
reviews.skip_if: M1 MacBook Air or 13-inch M1/M2 MacBook Pro owners: the README lists those machines as unsupported because they lack the required continuous sensor behavior.

reviews.name: DLSS5-Swapper
reviews.verdict: Our source run installed 323 packages, but the build stopped for a missing DLSS 5 payload and 6 of 278 tests failed, so this is not a clean build-from-checkout project.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or Proton users seeking a supported binary: the README calls that path experimental community source and ships no Linux binary.

reviews.name: agent-fleet-manager
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 7 seconds, built in 1 second, and passed all 7 tests in 2 seconds, so Agent Fleet Manager is cheap to try but too young to trust as a distributed control plane.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a ready multi-agent runtime: the engine never interprets a route, launches no LLM, and leaves external worker dispatch to your code.

reviews.name: FreePEP
reviews.verdict: FreePEP passed all 32 pytest tests in 5 seconds in our sandbox, but the record does not establish a successful textbook download.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial archives or profitable services: the README expressly prohibits those uses.

reviews.name: fullsend
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 624 npm packages in 27 seconds and passed all 75 Vitest tests, but that clean result covers Fullsend's web workspace rather than an autonomous production fleet.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams wanting a local coding helper: GitHub setup requires repository administration, model inference, `gh`, and up to five separate agent applications.

reviews.name: newsjack
reviews.verdict: Our Newsjack install took 1 second and only 13 MB, but the repository exposed no build or test target to our npm harness, so adoption rests more on workflow fit than verified package behavior.
reviews.skip_if: Browser-only users who need scheduled monitoring: the getting-started guide says Limited Mode cannot save monitors, keep seen-state, or schedule runs.

reviews.name: yichen-skills
reviews.verdict: Our run of the X uploader installed 39 packages and passed all 89 tests with 0 known vulnerabilities, but that evidence covers one subproject inside a 21-skill collection.
reviews.skip_if: Companies, agencies, paid courses, client projects, or internal business deployments without written authorization: the root license prohibits those uses.

reviews.name: goreleaser
reviews.verdict: GoReleaser is worth evaluating when artifact building, packaging, and publication need one maintained configuration.
reviews.skip_if: Projects whose main need is version selection and release notes; compare release-it and semantic-release before adopting an artifact pipeline.

reviews.name: background-agents
reviews.verdict: Our Background Agents run installed 1,296 packages and 1,184 MB, built in 64 seconds, then exited 1 after a 408-second test run whose log included 18 failures and 1 error.
reviews.skip_if: Multi-tenant products or companies with strict per-user repository boundaries: the README says users share one GitHub App scope and session creation does not verify personal repository access.

reviews.name: krops
reviews.verdict: Our krops build took 75 seconds and all 100 Rust tests passed in 44 seconds, making the bootstrap code the strongest measured result in this group.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a supported product or self-service portal: the README calls krops a reference implementation that users should fork and adapt.

reviews.name: escrcpy
reviews.verdict: Our clean-container build failed after 24 seconds with exit code 127.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a verified source build that works immediately in a clean Node container Teams that require an included automated test suite before adopting a device-control tool Headless server workloads, because this is centered on an Electron-style graphical desktop workflow…

reviews.name: upload-artifact
reviews.verdict: Use upload-artifact v7 when signed-in, expiring workflow downloads fit the job and the README's platform restrictions are acceptable.
reviews.skip_if: GitHub Enterprise Server users adopting v7: the README says v4 and later are unsupported on GHES and directs users to v3.2.2 variants.

reviews.name: node-red
reviews.verdict: Choose Node-RED when visual event flows fit your application and your team can own authentication, persistence, and deployment checks.
reviews.skip_if: Operators planning to expose an unsecured editor beyond a trusted network.

reviews.name: web-access
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox produced no install, build, or test result for Web Access because its JavaScript skill layout was unsupported and it ships no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require English source documentation: the repository is Chinese-first and sends English readers to an external OpenAITX translation.

reviews.name: user-scanner
reviews.verdict: User Scanner is worth evaluating for investigator-led username and email research where someone will review profile links, collisions and inconclusive responses.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs an account match to prove who owns it.

reviews.name: agenta
reviews.verdict: Agenta merits a controlled trial for shared agents doing variable team work.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need only a coding environment: Agenta's current README positions it for work around and beyond code.

reviews.name: cli
reviews.verdict: Our Google Workspace CLI run installed 104 packages in 7 seconds and used 36 MB, then its test command stopped because Cargo was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring officially supported Google tooling or stable command behavior: the README disclaims official product support and warns of breaking changes before v1.0.

reviews.name: gkd
reviews.verdict: Our GKD run installed 6 packages in 5 seconds and used 35 MB, but skipped build and tests, leaving Android behavior unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting useful automation immediately after download: the README says GKD provides no default rules.

reviews.name: pipeline
reviews.verdict: Shortlist Tekton Pipelines when your platform team wants CI/CD expressed as Kubernetes resources and can own installation and upgrades.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking CI without a Kubernetes installation to operate: the installation guide requires Kubernetes 1.28 or later, kubectl, and cluster-admin privileges.

reviews.name: GitHub520
reviews.verdict: Our GitHub520 run installed 61 packages in 30 seconds and pip-audit found 12 known vulnerabilities, even though ordinary users do not need the Python updater.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams that need official operating instructions: the README is in Chinese and provides no English version.

reviews.name: suna
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Kortix for its repository-based agent configuration and human-reviewed changes if those requirements justify operating the platform.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified deployment walkthrough: our run did not reach that stage.

reviews.name: whatsapp-web.js
reviews.verdict: whatsapp-web.js is worth evaluating when its documented WhatsApp Web features justify operating a browser and accepting the project's account-risk warning.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require an integration authorized by WhatsApp: this project explicitly disclaims that authorization.

reviews.name: mcp-server
reviews.verdict: SV Number MCP Server merits a supervised trial when temporary inbound verification and its paid provider fit your approved workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Banking, payment or government accounts, which the README explicitly excludes.

reviews.name: OpenMausBot
reviews.verdict: Try OpenMausBot under supervision if separate bot conversations and approval cards solve a problem in your existing agent workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Wayland users who require bots to control their host desktop: the commit-matched README disables that capability.

reviews.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
reviews.verdict: MoneyPrinterTurbo is worth a controlled trial if its documented script-to-video workflow fits your publishing process.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean dependency audit before evaluation: our September 27, 2026 run recorded 41 advisories across 2 affected packages, with audit coverage unknown.

reviews.name: md2wechat-skill
reviews.verdict: Use md2wechat-skill for its documented agent workflow if you accept the service, credential and licensing requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Publishers expecting free AI mode to return finished HTML directly.

reviews.name: go-whatsapp-web-multidevice
reviews.verdict: Evaluate GOWA with a dedicated test account after reproducing the failing test command and collecting complete logs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring evidence of successful live messaging or account pairing from this review.

reviews.name: omniget
reviews.verdict: Our OmniGet run installed 367 packages in 16 seconds, passed a 71-second build and a 6-second test step, but npm audit found 9 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams with a zero-high-advisory release gate: npm audit found 6 high-severity vulnerabilities in our measured commit.

reviews.name: loopx
reviews.verdict: LoopX is worth a bounded trial if your agent work needs durable goals, explicit ownership and reviewable handoffs across sessions.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting an autonomous production controller: the README keeps dangerous permissions, publishing, production writes and final ownership with a person Readers who need independently measured productivity gains or equal-budget efficiency results from this review Operators expecting state preservation alone to…

reviews.name: k-skill
reviews.verdict: Start with one Korean service task, inspect its skill instructions and credential route, and verify the output against the underlying service.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting the KTX timetable helper to reserve or pay for tickets.

reviews.name: automatisch
reviews.verdict: Try Automatisch with one low-risk workflow if hosting the data yourself matters enough to justify operating it.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a deployment already validated by this review: our sandbox did not launch the application or exercise integrations.

reviews.name: OpenTerminal
reviews.verdict: Our OpenTerminal run passed its 53-second build and all 26 tests, but npm audit reported 14 vulnerabilities, including 5 critical.
reviews.skip_if: Traders needing execution-grade quotes: the README says public endpoint data can be delayed, incomplete, or wrong.

reviews.name: SETS
reviews.verdict: Our SETS run installed 0 packages and passed all 8 tests in 1 second, making the browser simulation easy to try for learning.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking live exchange execution: the README explicitly excludes exchange connections and real orders.

reviews.name: deconv-preflight
reviews.verdict: Our deconv-preflight run built in 1 second and passed all 27 tests in 4 seconds, making this small alpha worth trying for exact reference-ID and metadata checks.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers seeking cell-type proportion estimates: the README says this tool does not run deconvolution.

reviews.name: prophet
reviews.verdict: Our Prophet source install hit the 900-second cap without completing, so adopters should prove a pinned wheel or source build before trusting the friendly two-column API.
reviews.skip_if: Source-based build pipelines that need a quick deterministic install: our commit f931ceb installation hit the 900-second limit without completing.

reviews.name: live
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run commit d2c33fd because it found no supported JavaScript project ecosystem and no Dockerfile, so evaluate fanmingming/live as a Chinese-language asset feed, not a packaged application.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the 2 documentation files we found are in Chinese, with no English README in the tree.

reviews.name: awesome-submitlist
reviews.verdict: The September 28 snapshot contains 339 destinations, including 203 marked free and 158 marked dofollow, which makes it a useful starting queue for a human-led launch.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a submission bot; this repository lists destinations and does not file forms Automated outreach teams that need permission data, since the catalog does not say whether each site allows scripted submission Analysts who need independently sourced traffic figures;…

reviews.name: toasty
reviews.verdict: Our Toasty build took 279 seconds, then `cargo test` ran 274 seconds before integration-suite compilation failed, so teams should trial v0.11 on their own backend before adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require the repository's default test command to pass in a fresh container: our run stopped while compiling `toasty-driver-integration-suite`, and the log tail did not include the compiler diagnostic.

reviews.name: go-stock
reviews.verdict: Our go-stock build finished in 6 seconds, but 9 of 13 test groups failed, so treat v2026.09.23.4 as an active research tool rather than a trusted trading system.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the README, setup guides, and detailed manuals are written in Chinese, with no English README in the tree.

reviews.name: zenoh
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Zenoh for its combined pub/sub, query and storage model when that combination solves an application requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing test command on the measured commit before evaluation can proceed.

reviews.name: iggy
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Apache Iggy through its server workflow before selecting it for a workload.
reviews.skip_if: Teams treating a successful npm installation as evidence that the Rust server works.

reviews.name: shardingsphere
reviews.verdict: Apache ShardingSphere merits a focused evaluation when you need capabilities above databases you must retain.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting this review to establish workload compatibility or production readiness Applications without a concrete requirement that justifies another database access layer Readers seeking a replacement storage engine rather than capabilities above existing databases

reviews.name: ai-data-extractor
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 21 seconds and found 0 known vulnerabilities, but this 1,707-line extractor has no automated test target.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting guaranteed extraction from Windsurf or Trae: the README says their undocumented SQLite formats are parsed with a heuristic that can return zero conversations after a schema change.

reviews.name: cloudnative-pg
reviews.verdict: CloudNativePG is worth evaluating when your team already operates Kubernetes and wants PostgreSQL managed through that API.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a PostgreSQL manager outside Kubernetes.

reviews.name: opentelemetry-collector
reviews.verdict: OpenTelemetry Collector is worth evaluating when a team needs a configurable, vendor-neutral layer between telemetry producers and destinations.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a complete storage, dashboard, and alerting product in this repository.

reviews.name: polars
reviews.verdict: Polars is worth evaluating when its expression API and lazy execution fit your pipeline.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a measured Polars-versus-pandas speed comparison: our run contains no analytical workload benchmark.

reviews.name: memvid
reviews.verdict: Our Memvid build finished in 105 seconds, but the full test run hit the 900-second cap with 3 lexical tests still running beyond 60 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Multi-agent systems that need several processes writing at once: issue 218 says the current design has a single-writer limitation and requires a queue or central writer.

reviews.name: awesome-mac
reviews.verdict: Use Awesome Mac to discover macOS software, then check each candidate's current requirements, price, license, and release history.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need every listing to be open source or free: the directory does not restrict entries to those categories.

reviews.name: msgvault
reviews.verdict: Our msgvault build took 128 seconds, and the test run timed out at 900 seconds with 34 passed and 6 failed packages reported.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to run alpha storage software: the README says APIs, storage format, and CLI flags may change without notice.

reviews.name: wealthfolio
reviews.verdict: Wealthfolio is worth evaluating if you want local portfolio records and can use manual entry or CSV import; automatic brokerage sync is an optional paid service according to its README.
reviews.skip_if: Users who require free automatic brokerage sync: the README places that capability in the optional Connect subscription.

reviews.name: agent-office
reviews.verdict: Our Agent Office run passed all 614 tests after a 17-second install using 403 MB, giving a trusted team good grounds for a local trial.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing security isolation between tenants: the security docs say all workers run as the same OS user and can read other accounts' folders.

reviews.name: jevgrep
reviews.verdict: Our Jevgrep build passed in 7 seconds, but its test launcher failed with docker: command not found, so the sandbox did not verify the full suite.
reviews.skip_if: Repositories whose source cannot leave the machine: searches send eligible content to the saved provider.

reviews.name: disktree
reviews.verdict: Our disktree build failed after 775 seconds and its test step failed after 194 seconds because both could not link xkbcommon-x11, so fresh Debian setup exceeds the README's instructions.
reviews.skip_if: Headless server operators: Linux requires a Wayland or X11 session and a Vulkan-capable GPU.

reviews.name: xtool
reviews.verdict: We did not run xtool because our lab does not support Swift, so its documented iOS deployment workflow remains unverified in our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Developers avoiding Apple downloads or accounts: the Linux guide requires Xcode.xip and Apple authentication.

reviews.name: system-design-notes-zh
reviews.verdict: We did not run System Design Notes ZH because the lab found no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile, so this review offers no execution or performance validation.
reviews.skip_if: English-only readers: the explanations are Chinese even where headings include English labels.

reviews.name: asd-ste100-skill
reviews.verdict: Our ASD-STE100 Skill run installed 35 packages in 5 seconds and built in 1 second, but tests were skipped because no test target was available.
reviews.skip_if: Aerospace documentation teams requiring official STE compliance: the approved ASD dictionary is absent, and dictionary-dependent rules are advisory.

reviews.name: tolaria
reviews.verdict: Our Tolaria source install failed after 81 seconds because pnpm rejected ignored dependency build scripts, leaving no build or test result in the supplied run.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting pnpm install to work unchanged in a fresh container: our run stopped on ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS after 81 seconds.

reviews.name: KAI-Scheduler
reviews.verdict: Evaluate KAI-Scheduler for shared GPU allocation, gang scheduling and hierarchical team quotas if you can run a cluster acceptance trial.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking deployment without an existing Kubernetes cluster and Helm; the documented GPU path also requires NVIDIA GPU Operator.

reviews.name: open-ontologies
reviews.verdict: Our Open Ontologies build and test commands each exceeded 900 seconds, with the test run still compiling dependencies, so commit 9b2dfc2 is better tried through a release binary than built casually on a small CI runner.
reviews.skip_if: People looking for a visual ontology editor: the README explicitly directs that job to Protégé.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: The 2 skill files deliver two distinct outcomes, chat explanations under 150 words and self-contained HTML summaries, with no executable project for our lab to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting software with an executable test target: this repository is instruction and example content, with no supported runtime ecosystem or Dockerfile.

reviews.name: sys1grep
reviews.verdict: Our sys1grep run installed 0 packages in 7 seconds, then the 228-second test step exited 1 on `spinner: the count of requests: cat@slow`.
reviews.skip_if: Teams handling text they cannot send to an outside service: the default endpoint receives every searched line.

reviews.name: rea
reviews.verdict: REA is worth evaluating when an agent needs several analysis workflows and the reader will inspect the evidence behind its conclusions.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting native decompilation without a separate analysis provider.

reviews.name: abide
reviews.verdict: Trial Abide for instructions that need judgment, with human review of its rubric and feedback.
reviews.skip_if: Workflows that require unavailable checks to block an edit.

reviews.name: dsh-echocat-skill-panel
reviews.verdict: dsh-echocat-skill-panel is worth a controlled trial for existing DSH Desktop Beta users who need skill visibility and management.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a standalone skill manager for other agent applications.

reviews.name: AirCard
reviews.verdict: Our AirCard build finished in 2 seconds, but pytest ended with 9 failures, including 4 tests tied to files in the maintainer's personal Downloads folder.
reviews.skip_if: Apple Card owners expecting a static skin: the README says Apple Card uses dynamic rendering and is not covered by the normal artwork path.

reviews.name: github-ranking-audit
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 36 packages and passed all 26 tests in 53 seconds across install, build, and test, so GitHub Ranking Audit is easy to inspect and run.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a proven search-ranking predictor: the README says GitHub's exact weights are unpublished, while this tool assigns its own fixed percentages.

reviews.name: github-stars-history
reviews.verdict: Our GitHub Stars History run installed 36 packages in 32 seconds and passed all 8 tests, making it an easy choice for repeatable CSV or JSON star counts.
reviews.skip_if: Investigators who need to identify individual stargazers: GitHub's aggregate endpoint and this tool return counts, not identities.

reviews.name: FGOAC-scooby
reviews.verdict: Our lab produced 0 runtime measurements for FGOAC scooby because C# was unsupported and no Dockerfile existed, so this review cannot confirm its build or launch path.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a game download: the release contains no game files and only works over an existing local-platform install.

reviews.name: dev-sidecar
reviews.verdict: Our Dev-Sidecar install pulled 1,437 packages and occupied 1,156 MB, yet commit d889a0c offered neither a root build target nor a test target.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the README, setup instructions, troubleshooting, issue discussions, and release notes are primarily Chinese, with no English README at the root.

reviews.name: toolkit
reviews.verdict: Our Toolkit run installed 1,375 packages and used 1,869 MB, then its root test command exited 1 despite a visible 15-of-15 `node:test` pass, so contributors should expect a large and currently imperfect monorepo.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a general Sentry administration server: the README says MCP tool choices favor debugging and developer workflows rather than all Sentry functionality.

reviews.name: rune
reviews.verdict: Consider a focused Rune trial if its integrated editor and terminals fit your work.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need documented Windows support now: the supplied prerequisites describe Windows as coming soon.

reviews.name: touchHLE
reviews.verdict: Our touchHLE build ran for 149 seconds before missing Boost stopped it, and the 10-second test attempt hit the same prerequisite with exit 101.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting broad iOS compatibility: the README says the vast majority of 2.x, 3.x, and 4.x apps do not work.

reviews.name: tilelang
reviews.verdict: Our TileLang install hit the 900-second cap before build or tests, so adopt it as compiler infrastructure with a hardware-specific qualification plan.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a routine Python install: our fresh Debian run did not finish installation within 900 seconds.

reviews.name: vintage-latex
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not compile the 20 examples because it detected PowerShell as unsupported and found no Dockerfile, so our evidence stops at source inspection and the project's successful TeX Live workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a historically exact facsimile: the README calls the work period-inspired and explains that real publications vary by press, date, language, paper, and process.

reviews.name: roundhouse
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Roundhouse's analysis on one application, then make a separate conversion decision.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a verified production migration from this review: our sandbox did not run generated applications.

reviews.name: RTX40MFG-Unlock
reviews.verdict: We could not run commit 67f7476 in our Debian lab because the C++ project has no supported harness path or Dockerfile, and its own build guide says the checkout lacks required kernel caches.
reviews.skip_if: Players who need guaranteed per-game compatibility: open reports include crashes, missing menus, freezes, and visual artifacts across named games.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run commit abf5cd8 because it is a Markdown repository with no supported executable ecosystem or Dockerfile, so adoption rests on reading and trying the two skills yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a broad skill library: the README lists only Apple web apps and Letterboxd diaries.

reviews.name: omarchy-workspace-layout
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run Omarchy Workspace Layout because the harness found an unsupported JavaScript ecosystem and no Dockerfile, so there is no independent install or test result to soften its platform risk.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users outside Omarchy: the panel and service are Quickshell QML components loaded by omarchy-shell.

reviews.name: flea
reviews.verdict: Flea is worth a controlled trial on Omarchy, with your existing file manager available as a fallback.
reviews.skip_if: Plain Arch users: Omarchy and Quickshell are hard dependencies.

reviews.name: Submarine
reviews.verdict: Our Submarine run installed 155 packages in 6 seconds and built in 18 seconds, but the repository offered no test target, so v0.3.8 is a promising client that still needs a careful local trial.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that forbid unsigned desktop software: the README says current builds are unsigned and require bypassing Windows or macOS warnings.

reviews.name: kubernetes-the-hard-way
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox could not run commit 52eb26d because the repository has no supported language ecosystem or Dockerfile, while the real exercise requires four Debian 12 machines.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone trying to create a production cluster: the README explicitly says the result is not production ready, and all control-plane components run on one server.

reviews.name: ish
reviews.verdict: Our iSH submodule run installed 938 JavaScript packages in 75 seconds and reported 26 known vulnerabilities, while exposing no build or test target.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting full Linux or container compatibility: open issue 63 still lists cgroups and namespaces as missing for Docker, and the syscall tracker has unimplemented calls.

reviews.name: QtScrcpy
reviews.verdict: Our QtScrcpy run installed 38 packages in 15 seconds and built its macOS packaging helper in 2, but it did not expose a test target or exercise the C++ app.
reviews.skip_if: People who cannot enable ADB debugging: the README requires it for normal use, and wireless setup begins with a USB connection.

reviews.name: python-patterns
reviews.verdict: Our Python Patterns run installed 69 packages in 24 seconds and built in 0 seconds, but pytest stopped before collecting tests because it rejected `--randomly-seed=1234`.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a green test gate before adopting reference code: our pytest run exited 4 because it did not recognize `--randomly-seed=1234`.

reviews.name: makepad
reviews.verdict: Our Makepad run installed 439 packages in 8 seconds, but both the 411-second build and 364-second test run failed when the linker could not find PulseAudio and DRM libraries.
reviews.skip_if: Linux developers seeking a turnkey VJ build: the README says CUDA must be present, the lane is not regularly tested, and small fixes may be needed.

reviews.name: Codex-X
reviews.verdict: Our Codex-X run installed 77 packages in 6 seconds, but the desktop build failed after 44 seconds because `gdk-3.0` was unavailable.
reviews.skip_if: Linux developers expecting the documented build command to work in a fresh Debian image: our build stopped because the required `gdk-3.0` system library was missing.

reviews.name: goldie
reviews.verdict: Our Goldie run installed 219 packages in 94 seconds and built successfully in 97 seconds, but skipped tests because no script or target was available.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or Windows developers seeking local iOS capture: the README requires macOS, Xcode and iOS simulators.

reviews.name: happy
reviews.verdict: Our source install failed after 8 seconds with a pnpm configuration conflict across 9 workspaces.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a standalone coding agent, because Happy wraps Claude Code or Codex rather than replacing them Developers who need a source checkout to install cleanly without troubleshooting pnpm configuration Risk-averse production teams that require a small, clearly triaged issue…

reviews.name: AndroidMic
reviews.verdict: Our AndroidMic build failed after 338 seconds, and its 47-second test command failed at the same missing PipeWire system library after Cargo installed 750 packages.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling or unable to install a virtual audio device: the README calls that step required on Windows, Linux, and macOS.

reviews.name: validator
reviews.verdict: Go Playground Validator is worth evaluating when Go structs are your validation boundary and tag rules fit your review process.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require validation rules to be ordinary Go expressions rather than tag strings.

reviews.name: Acode
reviews.verdict: Acode is worth evaluating for Android file editing and website previews.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified desktop or iOS editor: the supplied Acode documentation describes an Android application.

reviews.name: core
reviews.verdict: Doom Emacs is a reasonable candidate for users who want curated configuration and accept responsibility for external dependencies, Lisp customization and synchronization.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need a successful installation or editor workload demonstrated by this review.

reviews.name: reactjs-interview-questions
reviews.verdict: Our React Interview Questions run installed 22 packages in 2 seconds, but build and tests were skipped because no targets were found, leaving the examples unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners seeking a course to follow in order: the README is a question index, while the hooks README mostly describes its Vite template.

reviews.name: stylex
reviews.verdict: Pilot StyleX when predictable component overrides justify compiler integration and stricter style authoring.
reviews.skip_if: Teams unwilling to rewrite raw style objects that use object spreads or ordinary helper calls: the documented static-analysis rules reject those patterns.

reviews.name: oh-my-posh
reviews.verdict: Consider Oh My Posh if a consistent prompt across several shells is worth editing profiles and configuring fonts.
reviews.skip_if: Users whose existing shell prompt already supplies everything they need.

reviews.name: v86
