reviews.name: fluxer
reviews.verdict: Trial Fluxer's browser and packaged clients if your community wants messaging and voice with a self-hosting option.
reviews.skip_if: Operators expecting a web tunnel alone to carry calls: the current operator guide requires a publicly reachable TURN server for calls behind a tunnel.

reviews.name: openflight
reviews.verdict: Our OpenFlight run installed 58 packages in 27 seconds, built in 8 seconds, and passed 1,341 tests, so the software deserves a trial if you are prepared to build the hardware.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who want a finished appliance: our 58-package install covered only software, while the roughly $400 build still needs assembly and radar setup.

reviews.name: filestash
reviews.verdict: Our Filestash build passed in 21 seconds, but all 109 Go packages failed during the 172-second test step, so source adopters do not have a clean baseline from our run.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who cannot test destructive file operations: open issue 994 reports WebDAV folder deletion on S3 also deleting a sibling with the same prefix, and the related fix remains an open pull request.

reviews.name: planka
reviews.verdict: Our PLANKA source install failed after 39 seconds during the server's Python virtual-environment setup, so the build and tests never ran.
reviews.skip_if: Agencies or consultants inviting paying clients into a Community instance: the license guide says third-party access in a commercial relationship requires Pro or Enterprise.

reviews.name: Antigravity-Manager
reviews.verdict: Our Antigravity Tools run built in 31 seconds, but it installed 817 packages, exposed no test target, and carried 22 known vulnerabilities, so we would keep it on one operator's trusted machine.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial adopters expecting an MIT or Apache license: the repository uses CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which restricts licensed use to noncommercial purposes.

reviews.name: flexprice
reviews.verdict: Flexprice merits a shadow evaluation when you need usage pricing, credits, and entitlements alongside existing payment systems.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose existing payment-provider integration already handles their pricing without additional billing logic.

reviews.name: cal.diy
reviews.verdict: Try cal.diy only as a personal, non-production instance you can maintain yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial or production scheduling: the maintainers direct those users to Cal.com.

reviews.name: InsForge
reviews.verdict: Trial InsForge if agent control over backend administration justifies maintaining the stack.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking measured application throughput, database scaling or production reliability; our run established none of these.

reviews.name: pangolin
reviews.verdict: Trial Pangolin if you need its documented combination of browser access and private resource access.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a demonstrated successful source build at commit 7319bf8.

reviews.name: cal.diy
reviews.verdict: Cal.diy is worth evaluating for a technically capable person who accepts its personal, non-production scope.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses seeking commercial scheduling infrastructure: the maintainers direct those users to Cal.com.

reviews.name: uptime-kuma
reviews.verdict: Uptime Kuma is worth evaluating for small teams that want self-hosted availability checks and public status pages.
reviews.skip_if: Deployments that require NFS or similar network filesystems for application data: the README explicitly excludes them.

reviews.name: how-to-live-better
reviews.verdict: Our how-to-live-better run installed 35 packages in 18 seconds and built successfully in 5 seconds, making regeneration approachable for a reader that already ships as HTML.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need English documentation or an English interface: this edition's README and reading controls are Chinese.

reviews.name: Search
reviews.verdict: Search did not run in our Debian sandbox because its Swift ecosystem was unsupported and it had no Dockerfile, so our recommendation is a documented-feature trial rather than a verified runtime endorsement.
reviews.skip_if: People who need tabs, history, and passwords synchronized between devices: the README explicitly excludes sync and cloud accounts.

reviews.name: JIZURA
reviews.verdict: Our JIZURA run installed 1 package in 5 seconds, but skipped build and tests, so the easy developer setup comes without evidence of a working finished export.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a verified After Effects handoff: the guide describes mock-environment checks, and open issue 40 reports color and tracking warnings in the real panel.

reviews.name: shapeshift
reviews.verdict: Our Shapeshift run passed all 172 tests and built in 24 seconds, but installation brought 947 packages and a 765 MB footprint for a browser-local utility.
reviews.skip_if: People who need synchronized, backed-up task records: the README stores saved cards in browser localStorage.

reviews.name: deskworlds
reviews.verdict: Our Deskworlds run added 0 packages, used 89 MB, and passed its test command in 22 seconds, but the native wallpaper still requires macOS 13 and a source install.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users seeking a desktop wallpaper installer: only the browser scenes run there.

reviews.name: yeti
reviews.verdict: Keep Yeti on a pinned evaluation track until its artifact status is clear and you have reproduced the test outcome.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a released npm artifact: the supplied installation guide explicitly says none is available yet.

reviews.name: hit-and-run-web
reviews.verdict: Our run passed all 135 tests in 12 seconds after a 9-second install, but the checkout itself occupied 1,228.7 MB and the project still lacks a full campaign playthrough.
reviews.skip_if: Hosts that need uncomplicated rights to every shipped file: the license covers original project code but explicitly excludes The Simpsons: Hit & Run artwork, characters, audio, scripts, and game data.

reviews.name: clay-safari
reviews.verdict: Our Clay Safari run installed 21 packages in 9 seconds and produced a successful build in 10 seconds, making it an unusually approachable 3D code study despite the absent test target.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need full English contributor documentation: most of the 10,279-byte README, including setup details, is in Chinese.

reviews.name: shadcn-admin
reviews.verdict: Our shadcn-admin install stopped after 11 seconds because pnpm blocked build scripts for Clerk and two esbuild versions, so we never reached its build or tests.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a drop-in starter: the README says this is not a starter project, and authentication is described as partial.

reviews.name: docs
reviews.verdict: Our Ink Docs build completed in 57 seconds after a 91-second install, but the measured checkout had no test target or Dockerfile, and the current repository declares no license.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a reusable documentation starter with clear reuse rights: on September 15, 2026, GitHub detected no license, and the repository root had no license file.

reviews.name: remix
reviews.verdict: Our Remix 3 run installed 575 packages in 30 seconds and built in 31 seconds, but tests failed after 17 seconds because Playwright browser executables were absent.
reviews.skip_if: Existing Remix v1 or v2 teams seeking the supported continuation of that React framework: the maintainers moved that path into React Router 7.

reviews.name: fasthttp
reviews.verdict: Start with `net/http`, as fasthttp's own README recommends for most cases.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without a measured reason to replace `net/http`.

reviews.name: material-design-icons
reviews.verdict: Our September 7 sandbox, with 3 CPUs and 8 GB RAM, could not clone google/material-design-icons, so we have no build or test result for it.
reviews.skip_if: npm users expecting a Google-maintained current package: the README says Google stopped maintaining this repo's npm package after v3 in 2016 and does not vet the replacements it links.

reviews.name: editor
reviews.verdict: Try Pascal Editor with a disposable building project if local editing and MCP access match your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing repository test command before evaluation: our recorded test command exited 1.

reviews.name: axios
reviews.verdict: Axios is worth considering when shared browser and Node.js request configuration, interceptors or form handling meet a concrete application need.
reviews.skip_if: Applications whose request needs are already met by their runtime's Fetch API and that have no use for Axios's additional configuration.

reviews.name: Graphite
reviews.verdict: Our Graphite dependency step installed 559 packages in 46 seconds, but both build and tests exceeded 900 seconds while Rust was still compiling.
reviews.skip_if: Production studios that need a stable document format or a 1.0 support promise: both remain roadmap items.

reviews.name: kumo
reviews.verdict: Kumo merits a consumer evaluation when Cloudflare's component system fits your React product.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a verified clean contributor baseline from this recorded checkout.

reviews.name: stremio-web
reviews.verdict: Stremio Web fits readers who want Stremio's addon experience in a browser or want to contribute to its interface.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting this UI repository to provide a complete media server by itself.

reviews.name: workout-guide
reviews.verdict: Our checkout built in 11 seconds and all five Vitest tests passed, so Workout Guide is a credible starting point for adding static exercise art without inventing a catalog.
reviews.skip_if: Products that need coaching, rep counting, timers, workout planning, or user progress: the project supplies exercise metadata and images, not a training engine.

reviews.name: edit
reviews.verdict: Use FMHY when you want a maintained map of free online resources and accept that many destinations are third-party sites requiring your own judgment.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors adding paid or trial-only services, coding libraries, Linux distributions, or multiplayer cheats: the contribution guide explicitly rejects those categories or directs readers elsewhere.

reviews.name: hugo
reviews.verdict: Hugo is a reasonable candidate for a static publication or documentation site when its templates, content model, and asset tooling fit the team.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting Hugo alone to supply request-time authentication, per-user responses, or application business logic.

reviews.name: router
reviews.verdict: Keep TanStack Router unless an application profile gives you a concrete reason to trial Speedy Router.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that require React 18 or documented Node 22 support.

reviews.name: topcoat
reviews.verdict: Our Topcoat run built in 241 seconds and all 239 tests passed in 151 seconds, giving this experimental framework a better code signal than its age suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams requiring API stability: the README calls Topcoat early-stage and experimental and says to expect breaking changes.

reviews.name: Viscose-carousel
reviews.verdict: Choose Viscose Carousel if its shader technique is worth the remaining application work.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing shareable project URLs and browser history behavior without implementing routing.

reviews.name: full-stack-fastapi-template
reviews.verdict: Adopt Full Stack FastAPI Template when its FastAPI, React and PostgreSQL choices fit and your team can validate and maintain the application.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking only a small backend API: this repository also includes a frontend, email tooling and deployment configuration.

reviews.name: web-check
reviews.verdict: Web-Check is worth evaluating when you need several website investigations in one dashboard and can supply the services and system packages behind your chosen checks.
reviews.skip_if: Operators needing a fully offline investigation workflow: some checks require external APIs.

reviews.name: Infographic
reviews.verdict: Our AntV Infographic run built in 31 seconds and passed its 83-second test step, but installation took 207 seconds, used 986 MB, and exposed 4 high-severity advisories.
reviews.skip_if: Teams with a strict dependency-advisory gate: our install reported 7 known vulnerabilities, including 4 high-severity findings.

reviews.name: electron
reviews.verdict: Electron is worth evaluating when a JavaScript desktop interface and bundled Chromium fit your product, and your team can own security and platform maintenance.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring proven low download size or memory use: this review contains no packaged-app or runtime benchmark.

reviews.name: core
reviews.verdict: Vue is worth evaluating for teams that want HTML-based templates, reactive state and incremental adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that require IE11: Vue 3 requires native ES2016 browser support.

reviews.name: annotated_deep_learning_paper_implementations
reviews.verdict: Our labml.ai installation occupied 5,379 MB and built successfully, but its test command ended with an optimizer timeout and a separate error.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing repository test run before adoption: our recorded command failed with an optimizer timeout and a separate collection/setup error.

reviews.name: KiroCrew
reviews.verdict: Kiro Crew completed dependency installation in 36 seconds and the build-labelled step in 50 seconds, but tests timed out after 900 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Operators expecting self-hosting to disable outbound telemetry by default: the README documents enabled usage heartbeats and official-app receipts, with opt-out controls.

reviews.name: openbot
reviews.verdict: OpenBot's repository checks passed, but its desktop workflows remain untested here.
reviews.skip_if: Users who require confirmation before each agent action.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Higgsfield AI Skills requires an authenticated Higgsfield CLI workflow, and our lab did not execute it.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring offline inference: the documented generation flow submits jobs through an authenticated Higgsfield CLI.

reviews.name: Beav
reviews.verdict: Our Beav run completed the npm step in 4 seconds but found no build or test target, leaving the desktop application unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need the source for the current desktop release: the repository identifies the public baseline as 2.5.0 and says later release notes do not publish corresponding source.

reviews.name: V3R1T4S
reviews.verdict: Use V3R1T4S for supervised research where you can inspect the object, checker and success criterion.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need outside expert review before relying on a finding.

reviews.name: hypoarena
reviews.verdict: Our Hypoarena run installed 48 packages into 176 MB and passed its build and 47-second test step, making the offline workbench practical to try.
reviews.skip_if: Scientists seeking answers from real papers out of the box: the default commands use synthetic corpora and scripted or replayed agents.

reviews.name: ollaya
reviews.verdict: Our Ollaya run installed 328 packages in 10 seconds, then failed to build after 150 seconds with undefined C++ symbols, so a fresh Debian source checkout needs more work before adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Developers needing a working source build in a fresh Debian container: our build and test commands both stopped at linking.

reviews.name: awesome-opus5-5-videos
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run Awesome Opus 5.5 Videos because the collection had no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile, so it offers no measured execution result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a runnable video pipeline: this is a prompt and reference collection, and our harness found no supported ecosystem.

reviews.name: Fuxi
reviews.verdict: We did not run FuXi at commit f70cb3a because our harness lacked a supported ecosystem and the checkout had no Dockerfile, so its runtime remains unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Developers requiring an open-source, forkable agent: the README and LICENSE say the implementation is proprietary and unpublished.

reviews.name: jarvis
reviews.verdict: Our Jarvis run used 7,014 MB after installation and ended with 23 failed tests, 177 collection/setup errors, and 121 known vulnerabilities reported by pip-audit.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial product teams expecting unrestricted reuse: the license requires a separate commercial license.

reviews.name: onetake
reviews.verdict: Try onetake for a noncommercial film experiment if you want to work with its continuity method and can review the resulting composition yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial teams relying on the public edition's license: the README prohibits commercial use and directs those users to onetake Pro.

reviews.name: omarchy-meeting-recorder
reviews.verdict: Our Omarchy Meeting Recorder build failed after 23 seconds because GTK 4.8.3 did not satisfy its GTK 4.12 minimum, so source setup needs a compatible desktop before you can judge the recorder.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting an older GTK desktop to compile it unchanged: our GTK 4.8.3 failed the required GTK 4.12 check.

reviews.name: AionUi
reviews.verdict: Our AionUi run passed 4,980 tests but failed its build after 81 seconds while preparing bundled AionCore resources, so we cannot recommend this commit as ready for source packaging.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users who need Antigravity with approval prompts: open issue 4317 reports failed tool hooks in v2.2.2, with Full Auto bypassing approval as the workaround.

reviews.name: bridgeclip
reviews.verdict: Our BridgeClip build passed in 11 seconds, but its test suite ended with 226 passes and 3 failures, so the source is a candidate for an attended trial rather than unattended publishing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose recordings must stay entirely offline: audio and transcripts go to OpenRouter, and some visual paths send sampled frames.

reviews.name: mini-AGI
reviews.verdict: Our mini-AGI run installed 35 packages in 15 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but supplied no test result because the repository had no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a dependable local assistant now: the README calls the model toy-level and says final weights are unavailable.

reviews.name: OpenIntelligentUI
reviews.verdict: Our OpenIntelligentUI run installed 1,196 packages into 1,276 MB, then passed its build and all 4 Vitest tests, making the repository a workable starting point for interactive answers.
reviews.skip_if: People requiring offline or credential-free chat: the browser flow requires both OpenAI and Jev keys and makes billed provider requests.

reviews.name: jev-chat-windows
reviews.verdict: Our JevChat-Windows run installed 35 packages in 28 seconds and built successfully, but skipped tests because no target was available.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users expecting a fully English interface and manual: the README is Chinese and interface choices are Chinese or Korean.

reviews.name: jev-chat-jarvis
reviews.verdict: We did not run Jev because our harness lacked Kotlin support and the repo had no Dockerfile, so we cannot endorse its Android execution or reply accuracy.
reviews.skip_if: WhatsApp Business users or people whose conversations happen in groups: the global README excludes both.

reviews.name: Decepticon
reviews.verdict: Our Decepticon run installed 1615 packages and used 1490 MB, but the web build failed after 32 seconds and npm audit reported 46 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Hosts whose policy forbids application access to the Docker socket: the documented architecture uses it to drive the sandbox.

reviews.name: cindy
reviews.verdict: Our Cindy install used 4,102 MB, then the build failed because Electron Forge couldn't find dpkg and fakeroot, so source adoption needs packaging preparation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing the complete backend in the same open repository: the README says this checkout contains only clients and shared packages.

reviews.name: Hy-MT2
reviews.verdict: Our Hy-MT2 run prepared IFMTBench with 37 packages and 38 MB, built in 1 second, and supplied no translation-quality result.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a ready translation API from cloning this repository: deployment requires separate model weights and an inference runtime.

reviews.name: jev-align
reviews.verdict: Our jev-align run installed 160 packages into 866 MB, passed its build and tests, and still returned 2 known vulnerabilities, so a trial is justified but a blind rollout is not.
reviews.skip_if: High-stakes evaluation teams until they examine issue #3: it reports a correct all-negative held-out round displayed as F1 0.000.

reviews.name: awesome-jev-tools
reviews.verdict: The 23 published category counts add up to 1,192 records, making awesome-jev-tools broad enough for discovery but far too broad to substitute for evaluation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking runnable software: this repository is a Markdown index with no supported executable ecosystem or Dockerfile.

reviews.name: agency-agents-app
reviews.verdict: Agency Agents App is worth evaluating if you want a desktop interface for installing and tracking persona files across coding tools.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking an agent runtime or orchestration system.

reviews.name: nimble
reviews.verdict: Our Nimble run installed 35 packages and built successfully, but its 143-test suite ended with 2 failures and 16 collection/setup errors, so this is a promising research recipe with unfinished setup edges.
reviews.skip_if: CPU-only Linux deployments: the README requires Apple Silicon on macOS or an NVIDIA GPU with BF16 support for local inference.

reviews.name: localjev
reviews.verdict: Our LocalJev run installed 9 packages in 12 seconds and passed all 19 tests, but it did not exercise the required model server or prove that its generated probabilities are calibrated.
reviews.skip_if: Systems that require probabilities read directly from model logits: the README says LocalJev's values are generated by the model and are not mathematically equivalent to OpenJev's structured read.

reviews.name: ZeroScript-Free
reviews.verdict: Our ZeroScript-Free run installed 35 packages in 7 seconds and built in 1, but it had no test target, so the code is easy to unpack and hard to verify automatically.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or Firefox users: the README supports Windows or macOS with Edge or Chrome, while Linux and Firefox support remain open requests.

reviews.name: jevlike
reviews.verdict: Our Jevlike run installed 64 packages and occupied 5,379 MB, then passed its single test in 16 seconds, so the model is easy to inspect but lightly proved.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a drop-in copy of TypeSafe's Jev: the README calls this an independent starter and says Jev's design is private.

reviews.name: ARTEX
reviews.verdict: Our ARTEX run built in 66 seconds, but its 99-second test step ended with 28 passing and 3 failing tests out of 31.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone conducting a real penetration test, including an authorized test of an owned system: the README expressly limits ARTEX to learning, source research, and isolated local validation, and forbids tests against any online or networked system.

reviews.name: reelbench-skills
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run commit 1b51af8 because the repository fell outside the supported runner and has no Dockerfile, so its scripts and advertised gates remain unverified by us.
reviews.skip_if: Editors who need automatic transcription, face recognition, or object detection: video-shots explicitly excludes all three.

reviews.name: flybook
reviews.verdict: Our run passed 41 tests and built in 5 seconds, but pip-audit reported 20 known vulnerabilities and the project has not demonstrated profitable learning.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a proven trading bot: the model documentation says no profitable learning or strategy improvement has been demonstrated.

reviews.name: crypto-rag
reviews.verdict: Our Crypto RAG run installed 35 packages in 15 seconds and passed its 5-second build, but it exposed no automated test target for retrieval, routing, or market calculations.
reviews.skip_if: Traders placing orders from the reported spread: the comparison mixes raw USDT and USD quotes without an explicit currency conversion.

reviews.name: Choruz
reviews.verdict: Our Choruz run installed 559 packages and used 954 MB, yet exposed no supported build or test target to our harness, so adopting it means accepting a large developer-preview system without our usual verification step.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a stable production contract today: the README labels Choruz a developer preview and warns that interfaces, configuration, and data formats may change incompatibly.

reviews.name: lieflat-gongwen
reviews.verdict: Our Lieflat Gongwen run installed 35 packages in 28 seconds and built in 5 seconds, but there was no test target to check its writing workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial writing services or paid software products: the PolyForm Noncommercial license bars commercial use without a separate agreement.

reviews.name: BettaFish
reviews.verdict: Our BettaFish run installed 207 packages into 6,564 MB, then the build failed and pytest finished with 25 passes, 3 failures, and 16 errors.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to expose the default web app directly to the internet: the maintainer-reviewed FAQ says it lacks a complete application-level authentication boundary.

reviews.name: UniMate
reviews.verdict: Our UniMate run installed 35 packages in 25 seconds and built in 7 seconds, but it exposed no test target and did not exercise checkpoint inference.
reviews.skip_if: Mac or Apple Silicon users: the maintainer says current inference supports NVIDIA CUDA only.

reviews.name: cyber-resume-reviewer-skill
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox produced no install, build, or test result for commit 263acc3 because the runner found no supported executable ecosystem and the repo has no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Recruiters building candidate ranking or interview prediction software: the skill expressly refuses both jobs.

reviews.name: holo-card
reviews.verdict: Our optional-API run installed 7 packages in 7 seconds and passed its tests in 14 seconds, but those tests use a mock provider and cannot judge the generated card.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a one-click filter: the README requires separate layer generation, matte repair, alignment checks, and visual inspection.

reviews.name: Awesome-OKF
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 16 seconds and passed all 9 tests, but the advertised PyPI command still fails because Awesome-OKF has not been published there.
reviews.skip_if: Users following the README's `pipx install awesome-okf` command: open issue 14 says the package has never been published to PyPI, so install from Git is required.

reviews.name: dream-loop
reviews.verdict: Our Dream Loop run installed 35 packages in 23 seconds and built in 10 seconds, but there was no test target and we did not exercise its visual loop, so the clean setup says nothing about output fidelity.
reviews.skip_if: Developers whose agent lacks image generation or vision: the skill requires both and tells the agent to stop when no target image can be supplied.

reviews.name: holo-card-studio
reviews.verdict: Use Holo Card Studio for a supervised trial when editable Blender output and a browser viewer fit your task.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring demonstrated unattended card generation from this review Users expecting our sandbox results to establish Blender-version or touch-device compatibility Print production teams seeking evidence of manufacturing-ready output; the supplied documentation describes digital scenes, images, and a viewer

reviews.name: novoweave
reviews.verdict: Our NovoWeave run installed 51 packages in 16 seconds and passed all 8 tests, proving that the scaffold is easy to inspect, not that it can design a protein.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs generated structures or sequences: the README says there are no weights, datasets, checkpoints, tensor kernels, loss functions, or samplers.

reviews.name: rizzo-pii
reviews.verdict: Our Rizzo PII install consumed 5,741 MB, and pytest crashed before collecting a single test, so the clean audit and 1-second build do not establish a safe document pipeline.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that need certified coverage outside Italian: the README says the other seven trained languages are not validated.

reviews.name: awesome-ai-agent-platforms
reviews.verdict: Our commit 1b2dff2 checkout installed 35 packages in 12 seconds and built in 2 seconds, but it had no test target for the 49 entries.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers seeking a ranked winner or performance comparison: the selection policy says inclusion is not an endorsement and does not use star counts, funding, or company size.

reviews.name: image-story-video-wizard
reviews.verdict: Our Image Story Video Wizard run passed all 9 tests in 7 seconds, but those checks cover the workflow package rather than TTS, image generation, or a final render.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a one-command video generator: the skill pauses for user decisions and depends on separately available writing, TTS, image, and rendering tools.

reviews.name: aipass-bridge
reviews.verdict: Our aipass-bridge run installed 629 packages, passed all 148 tests, and reported 0 known vulnerabilities, but the useful runtime still depends on a logged-in browser and an unauthenticated local port.
reviews.skip_if: Cursor, Cline, Continue, or similar agent users: the README says system prompts and earlier messages are dropped, so those clients lose their tools and transcript.

reviews.name: image-prompt-reverse
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox found no supported runtime and no Dockerfile at commit 4dead0a, so Image Prompt Reverse is a readable Codex instruction pack rather than software we could execute.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a standalone image-analysis program or API: the repository contains Codex instructions, reference Markdown, and interface metadata, with no supported runtime or Dockerfile.

reviews.name: freemocap
reviews.verdict: Our FreeMoCap build took 1 second, but 9 of 44 tests never collected because `libGL.so.1` was missing, and pip-audit found 4 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers who need dependable physical scale today: the v2.0.0-alpha.25 notes warn that skeleton reconstructions may be off by roughly 10%.

reviews.name: langextract
reviews.verdict: Consider LangExtract when reviewers need to trace extracted phrases back to a document.
reviews.skip_if: Workflows that require correct fields without validation or human review.

reviews.name: openrig
reviews.verdict: Our OpenRig run installed 492 packages, found 21 known vulnerabilities, and ended with 4 failed tests out of 201 after a successful 57-second build.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone wanting a small wrapper around one coding agent: our install pulled 492 packages and used 255 MB before any provider tooling.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run pashov/skills because the JavaScript repository had no supported execution ecosystem and no Dockerfile, so there is no build or test result to support a reliability claim.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a deterministic scanner with a conventional test binary: this repository is primarily agent instructions, scripts, and templates.

reviews.name: starnet
reviews.verdict: Our StarNet checkout occupied 3,365 MB, installed another 1,598 MB, and still ended its test command with exit code 1, so source adoption demands more patience than the playful station suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Linux desktop users: the install guide says Linux artifacts are internal and the public release train supports only Windows and macOS.

reviews.name: hexstellar
reviews.verdict: Our HexStellar install took 22 seconds and the build passed in 1 second, but the checkout had no test target for the 119-file client.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking an open-source solver they can inspect or modify: the license is proprietary, and the repository says the engine is sealed and remote.

reviews.name: autoclip
reviews.verdict: Our AutoClip run installed only 4 root npm packages in 3 seconds, while the full 71,462-line product exposed no root build or test target to our harness, so the lab result is far too narrow to call the pipeline proven.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting our lab result to validate the full product: it covered the root npm package, not Python, the nested frontend, Rust, FFmpeg, Redis, Celery, or a real video.

reviews.name: Portable-Local-Studio
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 30 packages in 4 seconds and built the frontend in 1 second, but the repository had no test target to exercise its four AI workspaces.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac owners: the README says macOS Intel hardware is completely unsupported.

reviews.name: GLiNER2
reviews.verdict: Our GLiNER2 run consumed 5,690 MB, found 10 known vulnerabilities, and still had not finished the tests after 900 seconds, so adoption needs an evaluation branch and a dependency-remediation plan.

reviews.name: react-native-continued-task
reviews.verdict: Our install pulled 1,820 packages and occupied 998 MB, while all 42 Jest tests passed in 5 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Apps that must support continued work on iOS 25 or earlier: the API reports unsupported below iOS 26.

reviews.name: DLSS5oneclick
reviews.verdict: Our commit 1588564 checkout installed 414 packages in 12 seconds, then failed both its build and tests on an unresolved `windows_sys` reference.
reviews.skip_if: Online players who cannot keep the modded install away from anti-cheat: the README says ReShade add-on injection can cause a kick or ban and refuses several detected systems.

reviews.name: portal-ai-plugins
reviews.verdict: Our 3-CPU, 8 GB lab did not run portal-ai-plugins because its TypeScript setup was outside the supported harness and the repository had no Dockerfile, so there is no measured build or test result to lean on.
reviews.skip_if: Developers without access to a Spotify Portal instance: setup requires an instance name, backend URL, authentication, and an action listing before any workflow is useful.

reviews.name: wx-cli
reviews.verdict: Our wx-cli run installed 274 packages and passed all 1,411 tests, but the supported runtime is still limited to Apple Silicon macOS.
reviews.skip_if: Windows, Linux, or Intel Mac users: the README supports only Apple Silicon macOS, and issue 17 is still a request for Windows support.

reviews.name: vibe-kanban
reviews.verdict: Our run of Vibe Kanban installed 897 packages in 89 seconds and occupied 966 MB, but it offered no standard root build or test target for our harness to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Teams buying a supported hosted kanban service: Bloop shut down, terminated subscriptions, and said remote issues, comments, projects, and organisations would be removed.

reviews.name: concat
reviews.verdict: Concat installed 665 packages in our sandbox but failed to build after 618 seconds because pkg-config could not find libavutil, leaving its editor and export behavior unverified by our run.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting Cargo alone to provide the media stack: our build and test commands stopped because pkg-config could not find libavutil.pc.

reviews.name: noty
reviews.verdict: We did not run Noty at commit f51dd30 in our 3-CPU Debian sandbox: its Swift macOS ecosystem was unsupported and the repository had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Windows, Linux, or older macOS users: the app requires macOS 15+, and the Windows request remains open.

reviews.name: forward-implementation-first
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox could not execute commit 2d4dd7e because this Shell repository has no supported build ecosystem or Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Short, interactive coding sessions: the README explicitly says to skip the skill for single-shot work.

reviews.name: ast-grep
reviews.verdict: Consider ast-grep for syntax-based searches, YAML checks, and rewrites whose selection criteria fit tree structure.
reviews.skip_if: Migrations whose correctness depends on types, resolved symbols, or cross-file references unless you supply and validate the necessary external analysis.

reviews.name: maui
reviews.verdict: Shortlist .NET MAUI when sharing C# and XAML across mobile and desktop fits your product and you can support the documented target toolchains.
reviews.skip_if: Products that require an officially documented Linux desktop target: Microsoft's supplied target list does not include one.

reviews.name: chezmoi
reviews.verdict: chezmoi is worth considering when your dotfiles need different contents on different machines and you want to preview the generated changes.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting home-directory deletions and renames to propagate automatically: issue 4361 describes this as an unresolved workflow request.

reviews.name: hetty
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Hetty on a dedicated research machine only after resolving the missing admin assets and verifying the capture, intercept, and replay workflow yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need this review to demonstrate a working application: our sandbox did not exercise the browser interface or proxy traffic.

reviews.name: How-To-Secure-A-Linux-Server
reviews.verdict: This 171,177-character guide contains sound recovery habits and a panic-password example that deletes `/home`, so it is reference material for experienced home-server operators rather than an execution plan.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners looking for a safe paste-and-run recipe: the guide says it does not teach Linux, and its shortcut commands do not verify their own changes.

reviews.name: phpunit
reviews.verdict: PHPUnit 13.3 is worth evaluating for PHP 8.4 teams that want an xUnit framework with explicit configuration and documented test-double boundaries.
reviews.skip_if: Projects running PHP 8.3 or older: the PHPUnit 13 documentation requires PHP 8.4.

reviews.name: exploitarium
reviews.verdict: Our install finished in 17 seconds and the build in 10 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a polished scanner or one-command security product, because this is a mixed archive Production operators looking for a safe runtime dependency, because the code intentionally demonstrates exploitation Teams that require a clear open-source license, tagged releases, CI, and…

reviews.name: Backend-from-first-Principle
reviews.verdict: Use Backend from First Principles as a backend study reference, then validate individual examples in the environment where you intend to use them.
reviews.skip_if: Learners who require evidence that every chapter example has been executed successfully: our run does not provide that coverage.

reviews.name: vite-plus
reviews.verdict: Evaluate the published Vite+ CLI on a branch if consolidating your Vite workflow would solve a maintenance problem.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking evidence here that the released CLI works with their application: our run did not exercise it.

reviews.name: windhawk
reviews.verdict: Consider Windhawk when a specific Windows mod addresses your need and its process targets and compatibility fit your machine.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking a customization tool for macOS or Linux.

reviews.name: typephp
reviews.verdict: We could not produce an install, build, or test result because our sandbox had no supported PHP runner and the repo had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Existing Laravel, WordPress, or highly dynamic applications expecting drop-in compatibility Teams that need a proven, low-friction production compiler today Developers on PHP versions older than 8.4 Anyone unwilling to maintain C++17, PHP embed, CMake, GMP, and MPFR dependencies

reviews.name: nuclei-templates
reviews.verdict: Nuclei Templates is worth considering for teams that already use Nuclei and can review checks and validate their results.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking the scanner executable itself.

reviews.name: cryptolayer
reviews.verdict: CryptoLayer is useful material for protocol study and disposable prototypes.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking established evidence that CryptoLayer is ready for confidential correspondence: the supplied issue discussion reports fixes but does not provide a completed independent reassessment.

reviews.name: cli
reviews.verdict: Entire CLI is worth evaluating when reviewers need the conversation behind an AI-assisted commit and the team can control transcript storage and pushing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require transcripts to contain no sensitive information: the documented text scanners cannot inspect what screenshots depict, and local transcript copies are not redacted.

reviews.name: dsh-explore
reviews.verdict: Use Deepseek Harness Explore as a focused technical reading resource, not as the foundation of a production system.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a ready-to-deploy agent framework, because this is mainly an explanatory publication Readers who need the full article collection in English, because the articles are stated to be Chinese Buyers who require a stable release, declared license, and production…

reviews.name: defending-code-reference-harness
reviews.verdict: Treat this repository as material for building an internal security workflow, with a named maintenance owner.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a maintained, supported scanner they can deploy without owning the infrastructure.

reviews.name: pr-af
reviews.verdict: PR-AF merits a supervised trial if its agent-based review approach fits your workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking evidence here that the maintained Go node has passed deployment or end-to-end review checks.

reviews.name: Impactor
reviews.verdict: Impactor is worth evaluating for desktop sideloading and its documented certificate, pairing and tweak tools.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting permanent free-account provisioning: the README describes a 7-day limit and restrictions on registered apps or components.

reviews.name: gh-stack
reviews.verdict: gh-stack is worth evaluating for teams that already use GitHub CLI and understand dependent branches.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require an exit code alone to prove remote synchronization completed.

reviews.name: localstack
reviews.verdict: Retain the archived LocalStack source when preserving an existing integration justifies owning its maintenance.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring an actively maintained source repository that accepts upstream fixes.

reviews.name: cli
reviews.verdict: HTTPie CLI is worth evaluating for manual API work if its documented request syntax suits you.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who need a clean test baseline matching our recorded environment: that run reported three failures.

reviews.name: gitea
reviews.verdict: Gitea merits evaluation for teams prepared to operate their own Git host, maintain its data and run Actions infrastructure separately.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need GitHub workflows to retain all their behavior without changes: Gitea documents ignored job environments and unsupported GitHub-only permission scopes, including id-token.

reviews.name: M365-Copilot2API
reviews.verdict: Our M365-Copilot2API run built in 23 seconds and passed all 8 tests, but it did not verify Microsoft account access or coding-client file operations.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses selling API access: the license expressly restricts paid API relay operation without a separate commercial license.

reviews.name: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks
reviews.verdict: Our host build finished in 8 seconds, but pytest stopped after 9 seconds with 3 collection errors because the serving image's `librow_store.so` was absent, so a cheap generic container cannot validate the real appliance.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone without two GB10 DGX Sparks: the image, native cubins, tensor parallel layout, and network checks target that pair.

reviews.name: Edge0
reviews.verdict: Edge0 merits a device-specific evaluation when SSD-streamed MoE inference is the reason you are looking at it.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting the documented Python framework to support Linux or CUDA: the supplied README places CUDA on the roadmap.

reviews.name: useagent
reviews.verdict: Our npm run finished in 9 seconds with 0 packages and no build or test target, so it did not validate useAgent's documented Bun, Postgres, and sandbox path.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a normal root npm project: our npm install added 0 packages, while the documented setup runs Bun separately in nine workspaces.

reviews.name: hyperresearch
reviews.verdict: Our Hyperresearch suite was still at 30% when the 900-second cap stopped it, so this is for Claude Code users who value a deep audit trail more than a fast feedback loop.
reviews.skip_if: People who do not use Claude Code or Anthropic models: the README names both as requirements and describes a Codex port only as something contributors could submit.

reviews.name: d-inference
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Darkbloom if you need to study its provider or network trust model and can test on Apple hardware yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a production recommendation from this review: the measured revision explicitly disclaims production use and support.

reviews.name: deepseek-harness
reviews.verdict: Our DeepSeek Harness build passed in 350 seconds, but its tests timed out at 900 seconds, so we recommend a contained developer evaluation rather than a production commitment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring stable plugin contracts: the README explicitly warns of compatibility-breaking changes during developer preview.

reviews.name: omlx
reviews.verdict: oMLX is worth evaluating on a supported Apple Silicon Mac if its menu-bar controls, model management and tiered prompt cache fit your workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a documented standalone installation for Linux, Windows or Intel Macs: the supplied requirements specify Apple Silicon and macOS 15 or newer.

reviews.name: vllm
reviews.verdict: Consider vLLM when its documented batching and distributed-serving capabilities match a deployment requirement you can test.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified throughput, latency, or accelerator-memory benchmark: our run measured none of these.

reviews.name: llama.cpp
reviews.verdict: Choose llama.cpp when control over GGUF files, native integration, and backend selection matters enough to justify testing your own deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting arbitrary checkpoints to load directly: llama.cpp requires GGUF, with conversion scripts for other formats.

reviews.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Single-DGX-Spark-TensorFold
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run this Qwen3.8 Flash Next recipe because Shell is unsupported by the harness and no Dockerfile was detected, so its serving behavior remains unverified by us.
reviews.skip_if: Ordinary CPU servers or small GPU machines: the recipe targets GB10 hardware with 128 GB of unified memory.

reviews.name: ai-native-callcenter
reviews.verdict: Our AI Native Call Center run passed all 72 tests after a 31-second install and a 59-second build, but current reports document silent Qwen campaign endings and missing supervisor browser-phone provisioning.
reviews.skip_if: Unattended Qwen campaigns that require an audible closing line: open issue 207 reports silent hangups after record_lead and hangup at commit 6e2ee1d.

reviews.name: Relate
reviews.verdict: Our Relate run passed all 39 tests, but npm audit reported 4 known vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 1 high, so I would investigate those findings before importing private chats.
reviews.skip_if: Users who require every conversation to stay on their machine while using a cloud model: the README explicitly allows text to be sent to the AI provider.

reviews.name: vm2api
reviews.verdict: Our vm2api test command ran for 310 seconds and exited 1 despite 9 reported passing tests, while npm audit found 1 moderate vulnerability.
reviews.skip_if: Any business without written permission from the author: the custom license prohibits commercial use, including internal revenue-producing use.

reviews.name: AgentVerse-OS
reviews.verdict: Our AgentVerse OS core build took 150 seconds and all 80 Rust tests passed, which makes the code worth exploring even though the full system is still a single-box alpha.
reviews.skip_if: Teams or families: the README says there are no user accounts or permissions and describes the current system as one person on one server.

reviews.name: superlocal
reviews.verdict: Use SuperLocal as an evaluation checkout if you want to inspect its provider-separated Inbox SDK and fictional-mail demo.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a mail client whose live account workflows this review has verified.

reviews.name: taskview-community
reviews.verdict: Our TaskView install stopped after 1 second because its pnpm 12.6.0 entry file was missing, so a source checkout is not ready to judge by screenshots alone.
reviews.skip_if: Agencies that want to give clients accounts on a shared instance: the license excludes customers and other third parties from permitted users without a separate commercial license.

reviews.name: mlmvpn_windows
reviews.verdict: Our MLMVPN run installed 431 packages, then both the 4-second build and 2-second test command failed, while npm audit found 25 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or Linux users: the supported application targets Windows 10 and 11, and it needs administrator rights for TUN, firewall, DNS, and route changes.

reviews.name: autobrr
reviews.verdict: Consider autobrr when IRC announcements or a shared filtering layer solve a specific gap in your current download workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Users whose existing *arr feed workflow already meets their needs: autobrr's introduction says another RSS layer is unnecessary when feeding only the *arr applications.

reviews.name: owncast
reviews.verdict: Owncast is worth evaluating for a single broadcaster who wants to operate a streaming page and chat.
reviews.skip_if: Services that need several independent broadcasting accounts within one installation: the README describes a single-user server.

reviews.name: openreplay
reviews.verdict: Shortlist OpenReplay when self-hosted replay, browser context and product analytics match your needs and someone can own the infrastructure.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting our source run to demonstrate a working production deployment: it did not exercise deployment, recording or playback.

reviews.name: NetAlertX
reviews.verdict: NetAlertX is worth a controlled evaluation when device discovery and change alerts are the job.
reviews.skip_if: Operators whose deployment policy forbids the host networking and added capabilities in the documented Docker quick start.

reviews.name: zyfun
reviews.verdict: zyfun is worth evaluating if you already have authorized, compatible sources and can work with its Chinese documentation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting an included film or channel catalog.

reviews.name: mailflare
reviews.verdict: Our Mailflare install pulled 982 packages and 1,083 MB, then the build stopped after 12 seconds because Wrangler remote mode required a Cloudflare login.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require an OSI-approved open-source license or a normal public-fork contribution flow: the license forbids redistribution and publishing modified copies without permission.

reviews.name: walgit
reviews.verdict: Our walgit build ran for 643 seconds before `walgit-server` failed with 3 compiler errors, and tests hit the same compilation boundary after 271 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a GitHub or GitLab replacement with issues, pull requests, CI, and code review: the README scopes walgit to repository serving and browsing.

reviews.name: evolution-api
reviews.verdict: Evolution API makes sense when its unusually wide set of WhatsApp, webhook, queue, CRM, and storage connections would replace glue code you already expect to maintain.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean source build from the measured commit: our build stopped on missing Prisma client exports, including `Contact`, `Message`, `Proxy`, and `Prisma.sql`.

reviews.name: tick-stock-panel
reviews.verdict: Tick Stock Panel is a reasonable candidate for Chinese-reading A-share hobbyists willing to validate a local research setup.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need a verified English onboarding path: the supplied README and deployment guide are in Chinese.

reviews.name: dynamo
reviews.verdict: Evaluate NVIDIA Dynamo when you can name a coordination problem across inference workers, such as independent prefill/decode scaling or routing based on KV-cache overlap.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified quick-install result: our recorded run does not establish that Dynamo installed or served requests.

reviews.name: OpenBiliClaw
reviews.verdict: OpenBiliClaw is worth evaluating if you want profile-driven discovery and are willing to manage browser-session access and model configuration.
reviews.skip_if: People who do not want software inferring MBTI, cognitive style, or psychological needs.

reviews.name: portmaster
reviews.verdict: Portmaster is worth evaluating if you want per-app filtering and encrypted DNS on Windows or Linux, with paid history and SPN available separately.
reviews.skip_if: Readers looking for a documented macOS option: the supplied README describes Windows and Linux desktops.

reviews.name: rustdesk
reviews.verdict: RustDesk is worth evaluating when choosing your rendezvous and relay infrastructure matters to your support workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a verified deployment recipe or performance benchmark from this review: our run reached dependency download and compilation attempts, not a working remote session.

reviews.name: grok2api
reviews.verdict: Grok2API is worth evaluating when Grok account pooling is the specific requirement and you can manage the documented credential and deployment responsibilities.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking evidence that live Grok requests, media generation, or client integrations worked in our sandbox.

reviews.name: deepseek-whale-girl
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run DeepSeek Whale Girl because its HTML repository has no supported harness ecosystem or Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Product teams expecting all images to inherit MIT permission: the README excludes artwork from the code license and requires source-specific checks.

reviews.name: floorplan-3d
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run floorplan-3d, and its documented route to a custom apartment requires editing data inside index.html.
reviews.skip_if: Homeowners expecting to import an architectural drawing immediately: the README instructs you to edit layout data in the HTML, and issue 10 asks for drawing import.

reviews.name: spiderbench
reviews.verdict: Our Spiderbench install and build each took 8 seconds, but no tests target was available and gameplay performance remains unmeasured.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for open-source code to reuse in a product: the LICENSE forbids use in distributed works and commercial projects without permission.

reviews.name: PDoomVideo
reviews.verdict: Our PDoomVideo run installed 55 packages in 3 seconds, but npm test failed in 1 second because the project supplies only a placeholder test command.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring executable tests before adopting a renderer: npm test is a placeholder that exits with an error.

reviews.name: threejs-architecture-effects
reviews.verdict: threejs-architecture-effects includes an editable, orbitable construction starter, but our lab did not run it because the harness lacked a supported ecosystem and the repo had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Video producers needing an MP4 exporter or soundtrack: the README says video export and starter music are absent.

reviews.name: vega-app
reviews.verdict: Our Vega App install pulled 1,370 packages and 811 MB, then 6 Jest suites failed and npm audit reported 36 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a ready-made catalog: the README says Vega does not host, store, or provide media, and users manage all third-party sources.

reviews.name: MusicFree
reviews.verdict: Our MusicFree setup stopped after 130 seconds because Yarn saw Node 18.20.8 and `minimatch` required Node 20 or at least 22, so source builders should not trust the stated Node 18 floor without testing their exact lockfile path.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a ready-made streaming catalog: the README says MusicFree includes no music source and depends on plugins for every online result.

reviews.name: Ehviewer_CN_SXJ
reviews.verdict: Our EhViewer build and test steps both ended at `./gradlew: Permission denied`, after 8 and 31 seconds, so source builders should fix and verify the wrapper path before judging the code itself.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users who need full setup and troubleshooting documentation: most of the README, FAQ, and changelog are in Chinese.

reviews.name: scroll-craft
reviews.verdict: The lab found JavaScript but no supported executable target or Dockerfile, so scrollcraft has no independent build or test result on our page.
reviews.skip_if: Developers outside Claude Code who want a documented first-class install path: the README installs it through Claude Code's plugin marketplace.

reviews.name: open-tv
reviews.verdict: Our Open TV v1.9.1 checkout failed its build in 10 seconds, timed out waiting for Chrome for 900 seconds, and reported 89 known dependency vulnerabilities, so source adoption should wait for cleanup.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting channels to be included: the README only describes importing your own M3U or Xtream sources.

reviews.name: webpack
reviews.verdict: webpack is worth retaining or evaluating when its loaders, plugins and chunk controls answer a concrete build requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners whose priority is minimal configuration: webpack's README describes it as a low-level tool that is not always the easiest entry-level solution.

reviews.name: nuxt
reviews.verdict: Nuxt is worth evaluating for a Vue team that wants integrated routing, several rendering modes, and server code.
reviews.skip_if: Teams committed to a different component framework and unwilling to adopt Vue.

reviews.name: 3dicon
reviews.verdict: Trial 3dicon for a reviewed animated app icon if hosted generation fits your workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring offline generation: the documented workflow uses hosted image and video services.

reviews.name: DeepSelect
reviews.verdict: Trial DeepSelect only when its documented TopK contract fits your workload and you can qualify it on the intended hardware.
reviews.skip_if: Applications requiring topk values above 4096 or input types outside the documented paths.

reviews.name: MemOS
reviews.verdict: Evaluate MemOS when editable memory and memory-cube isolation justify its operating requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean test result before adoption: our recorded Python test command exited with code 1.

reviews.name: AI-Engineering-Coach
reviews.verdict: Consider AI Engineer Coach for a personal trial if inspecting coaching rules alongside the sessions they flag would help you.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a ready-to-install Marketplace or Releases package.

reviews.name: GameFactory-3A
reviews.verdict: Trial GameFactory-3A with an engineer responsible for the selected engine, model environment and acceptance evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Creators expecting installation alone to produce a finished game.

reviews.name: robin
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Robin for source-checked dark-web leads if you can operate Tor, control model access and preserve original material.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring demonstrated live onion-search reliability before adoption; our recorded run does not establish it.

reviews.name: godogen
reviews.verdict: Godogen is worth a supervised prototype trial if you want an agent to assemble a game project and you can evaluate the result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking measured evidence that Godogen reliably produces finished games: our run did not test that outcome.

reviews.name: oil-motion
reviews.verdict: Oil Motion warrants a supervised pilot when the central effect needs changing subject imagery and direct user control.
reviews.skip_if: Projects needing only interface transitions, button feedback, or layout motion that ordinary frontend code can handle.

reviews.name: computer
reviews.verdict: Use Cloudflare Computer when durable agent files on Workers are central to the application and its stable filesystem or Worker JavaScript backend fits the task.
reviews.skip_if: Production applications that require the experimental Worker shell, ContainerBackend or synchronization protocol.

reviews.name: agent-of-empires
reviews.verdict: Agent of Empires is worth evaluating when you need management features around several persistent coding-agent sessions.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a coding agent or model: this is a session manager around separately launched tools.

reviews.name: headroom
reviews.verdict: Trial Headroom if repetitive agent context is a problem you can measure and your machine can accommodate the recorded sandbox installation.
reviews.skip_if: Machines where the 6,807 MB recorded sandbox installation is impractical.

reviews.name: Jev-cu
reviews.verdict: Use Jev-cu for a small, supervised trial when labeled macOS controls fit the task and you can verify the result.
reviews.skip_if: Tasks that depend on canvas layout, 3D modeling, or visual-quality judgments.

reviews.name: douyin-downloader
reviews.verdict: Do not choose the Python CLI for dependable everyday Douyin downloads while its documented verification block persists.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs reliable unattended downloads of individual videos, photos, collections, music, likes or favorites while the documented verification block persists.

reviews.name: n8n-workflows
reviews.verdict: The catalog installed in 8 seconds and built in 1 second, but tests were skipped and pip-audit reported 57 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners expecting ready-to-run AI workflows: the checked MongoDB Agent example stores AI-labeled steps as noOp nodes.

reviews.name: corsair
reviews.verdict: Corsair merits a provider-specific evaluation if you want one integration layer for application code and agents.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a successful full-repository build and test run before evaluation: our recorded commands did not meet that condition.

reviews.name: WeMM-Embedding
reviews.verdict: Trial WeMM-Embedding for retrieval across text and visual media if you can validate the model on your corpus and hardware.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that require audio embeddings.

reviews.name: Kronos
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Kronos as a specialized forecasting candidate once you can defend the checkpoint's evaluation window.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a ready-to-deploy trading strategy with validated returns after costs.

reviews.name: codegraph
reviews.verdict: The successful install and build support a contained evaluation of CodeGraph at commit 00d7430.
reviews.skip_if: Release owners requiring a passing verification baseline: the recorded test command exited 1.

reviews.name: genlayer-project-boilerplate
reviews.verdict: Use GenLayer Project Boilerplate to learn and prototype a GenLayer application.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an Ethereum starter or a chain-neutral application template.

reviews.name: hop
reviews.verdict: Evaluate HOP on copies of your documents if opening HWP/HWPX and saving HWP meet your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Workflows that require HWPX saving or autosave/recovery; the supplied development guide says these are unavailable.

reviews.name: TensorFold
reviews.verdict: Evaluate TensorFold when your chosen release documents the checkpoint and hardware you intend to use.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking measured inference speed, usable context or serving memory requirements from this sandbox run.

reviews.name: cve-mcp-server
reviews.verdict: CVE MCP Server has a documented role in consolidating vulnerability research, but our run did not establish a working analyst workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a working installation without dependency investigation: our sandbox captured an MCP 2.x import failure during server startup.

reviews.name: LunaTV
reviews.verdict: Try LunaTV if you can maintain a private Docker deployment and already have authorized source APIs.
reviews.skip_if: Readers expecting an included catalog or ready-to-watch deployment Operators seeking evidence of tested playback, concurrency or production reliability Commercial or public-service deployments: the README explicitly prohibits these uses

reviews.name: ming-official-atlas
reviews.verdict: Use Ming Official Atlas as a browsing aid for Ming institutions, with historical checks at the individual-record level.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers who require a complete annual roster of Ming officials.

reviews.name: BeefTV
reviews.verdict: Our BeefTV backend built in 101 seconds, but its tests timed out at 900 seconds with 17 passes and 4 failures reported.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a green backend suite: our run timed out at 900 seconds with 17 passes and 4 failures reported.

reviews.name: livecanvas
reviews.verdict: LiveCanvas supplies a silent H.264-and-JPEG pairing workflow, but its README explicitly stops short of automatic iPhone Photos import.
reviews.skip_if: Creators needing audio in the supplied Live Photo path: the README and pairing guide restrict it to silent H.264 video with JPEG images.

reviews.name: DeepEP-Ascend
reviews.verdict: Our DeepEP-Ascend test command ended with 12 collection/setup errors and no executed pass or failure results, despite successful install and build steps.
reviews.skip_if: NVIDIA-only deployments: this backend targets Ascend 950 hardware, while the original DeepEP is the NVIDIA route.

reviews.name: jeeves
reviews.verdict: Our Jeeves install used 5,696 MB for 98 packages and passed its build, but our sandbox skipped tests and did not validate inference.
reviews.skip_if: CPU-only servers: the documented quick start requires CUDA, with Apple Silicon as the other stated inference route.

reviews.name: product-film-skill
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run Product Film because its harness had no supported execution path for the TypeScript checkout, so we cannot vouch for a finished render.
reviews.skip_if: Claude chat-app users: the README requires Claude Code running a local toolchain and explicitly excludes the chat apps.

reviews.name: shipvideo
reviews.verdict: Our Shipvideo run installed 39 packages in 15 seconds and passed its build in 5 seconds, but had no test target and did not establish a completed video render.
reviews.skip_if: Projects requiring included music, recorded footage, or a talking presenter: the scene tool rejects audio and video elements.

reviews.name: FounderOS
reviews.verdict: Our FounderOS install took 29 seconds, but npm audit reported 66 vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 52 high, and build and tests were skipped.
reviews.skip_if: Founders expecting an npm-only desktop app: the README requires PostgreSQL with pgvector, Redis, Go, and the Elixir knowledge engine.

reviews.name: dasheng
reviews.verdict: Dasheng is a candidate for evaluating transcript-based English reading feedback, especially for developers comfortable with Chinese documentation.
reviews.skip_if: Learners who need acoustic assessment of pronunciation, stress, or accent.

reviews.name: G0DM0D3
reviews.verdict: Our G0DM0D3 run installed 817 packages and used 592 MB, then failed its 44-second build while npm audit reported 31 vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a green production build: our Next.js build failed on a TypeScript Map iteration error at commit f630176.

reviews.name: editaplot2026
reviews.verdict: Our EditaPlot run installed 35 packages and built successfully, but the 291-test run ended with 19 failures and 34 collection/setup errors, so this is a promising specialist tool that is not ready for a blind rollout.
reviews.skip_if: Mac, Linux, WSL, Wine, Parallels, or virtual-machine users: the README says the full Origin path is supported only on physical Windows 10/11 x64 computers.

reviews.name: post-production-skill
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run this 15.3 MB prompt bundle because it has no supported executable ecosystem or Dockerfile, and the repository supplies no automated checks.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting video generation or editing: the skill outputs one prompt and does not submit a generation job by default.

reviews.name: uplifting-biomolecular-modeling
reviews.verdict: Our `af2ig/opt/` run installed 36 packages in 27 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but it ran 0 tests and exercised no GPU inference.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require upstream support or ongoing fixes: Anthropic labels this a reference release, says it is not maintained, and does not accept contributions.

reviews.name: jev-review
reviews.verdict: Our Jev Review install took 3 seconds and npm audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, but the repository had no build or test target and whole-codebase review followed at most 8 signals.
reviews.skip_if: Go, Rust, Python, Java, or mixed-language repositories: the source discovery pattern accepts only JavaScript and TypeScript extensions.

reviews.name: video-generator-client
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 51 packages, built in 7 seconds, and passed all 4 tests in 9 seconds, which makes Video Generator Client easy to inspect and try.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a stable model catalog: the README and `catalog.py` list different model IDs, and open pull request 2 exists to reconcile them.

reviews.name: haiming-app-monetization
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run Haiming App Monetization because the repository has no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile, so v0.1.0 should be judged as a four-file advice package rather than working monetization software.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the README, skill, acceptance cases, and default prompt are Chinese, with no English guide.

reviews.name: itsgiving
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 61 packages into 978 MB and found 2 known vulnerabilities, while the repository supplied no test target, so It's Giving is a playful source project rather than meeting-ready software.
reviews.skip_if: Work meetings where a false reaction would be costly: the README warns that effects fire automatically and everyone sees the result.

reviews.name: mobilecode
reviews.verdict: Our MobileCode install took 94 seconds, added 2,362 packages, and used 2,470 MB, while the root test command deliberately refused to run package tests.
reviews.skip_if: iOS developers working from Linux or Windows: iOS preview requires macOS and Xcode.

reviews.name: image-to-3d-pipeline
reviews.verdict: Our build of the 70 MB web explorer passed in 14 seconds with 0 audit findings, but the complete reconstruction stack has no unified install or test target.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting one command to install and run the complete reconstruction stack: `setup.sh` only clones 4 upstream tools, while their Python environments and model weights remain separate.

reviews.name: BrowserKitten
reviews.verdict: BrowserKitten is a candidate for a supervised trial when operating inside an already logged-in Chrome session is the requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who require a Chrome Web Store installation: the README explicitly says the extension is not on the store.

reviews.name: interdimensional-game
reviews.verdict: Our LAST FRAME install pulled 307 packages and used 604 MB, then built in 30 seconds, but it offered no test target and npm reported one high and one moderate vulnerability.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need code they can legally reuse or redistribute: the repository has no detected license, so default copyright restrictions apply.

reviews.name: infinite-livestream
reviews.verdict: Our FastH3 install took 124 seconds and its 1-second build passed, but pytest executed no tests because `numpy` was missing during collection.
reviews.skip_if: Ordinary self-hosters: the model README calls for four NVIDIA B200 GPUs, CUDA 13, and roughly 148 GB of weights.

reviews.name: bkn-foundry
reviews.verdict: Our BKN Foundry install pulled 339 npm packages in 21 seconds and used 179 MB, yet it exposed no build or test target because that root package only supports API docs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a normal npm application: our 21-second root install covered only API documentation tooling, while the product deploys as a Kubernetes platform.

reviews.name: mindcraft
reviews.verdict: Our Mindcraft install failed after 113 seconds because its Mineflayer patch targeted 4.33.0 while npm installed 4.39.0, so commit 5f3acc8 is not a clean-start recommendation.
reviews.skip_if: Public-server operators who want coding enabled: the README warns that prompt injection can lead the model to execute code on the host.

reviews.name: sdf-js
reviews.verdict: Our sdf-js run installed 116 packages in 14 seconds and passed its tests in 31 seconds, but npm audit found 2 high-severity vulnerabilities and no build target existed.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial product teams without a separate agreement: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 covers the Atlas code and COMMERCIAL.md says commercial use requires another license.

reviews.name: agency-agents-zh
reviews.verdict: Consider agency-agents-zh when Chinese role instructions and China-specific business contexts match your work.
reviews.skip_if: Readers expecting the role library alone to run an autonomous team Teams requiring measured output quality or independently verified compatibility across all advertised tools Operators seeking verified legal, financial or medical decisions without specialist review Readers who need this review…

reviews.name: gsd-core
reviews.verdict: GSD Core merits a trial for projects that need persistent planning records and a repeatable agent workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring evidence of a completed end-to-end agent workflow before adoption: our run covered repository setup, build, and an incomplete test command.

reviews.name: GamePhanes
reviews.verdict: Use GamePhanes to inspect and develop runtime acceptance contracts for game-project repairs.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers who need our run to establish game-engine performance or agent repair ability: it covers the repository's Node test command.

reviews.name: personaplex
reviews.verdict: Evaluate PersonaPlex when overlapping speech and prompted voice or role control are central to your project.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting this review's successful client build to establish working model inference or real-time audio performance.

reviews.name: OpenCluely
reviews.verdict: Evaluate OpenCluely only for permitted practice where its floating answer window serves a specific need and you can investigate setup.
reviews.skip_if: Candidates whose interview rules prohibit outside assistance.

reviews.name: miles
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Miles when you need configurable model post-training infrastructure and can validate the chosen GPU environment.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified laptop walkthrough: the documented Qwen3-4B quick start specifies eight H100, H200 or B-series GPUs and at least 500 GB of free disk.

reviews.name: Code-as-World
reviews.verdict: Our 3-CPU, 8 GB sandbox produced no install, build, or test result for commit 87d4159 because the lab lacked a supported Python ecosystem and the repo had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need a CPU setup: the README requires Python 3.10 or 3.11 on a CUDA host, and its serving recipe uses vLLM with GPU memory settings.

reviews.name: GamePhanes
reviews.verdict: Consider GamePhanes, now presented as GameForgeBench, when your research needs game-project repairs checked through runtime behavior.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking measured agent-repair performance from our review: our run did not evaluate a coding agent.

reviews.name: PRAXIST
reviews.verdict: PRAXIST is worth a bounded evaluation when you already own a runnable research project, a credible evaluator, and an operating budget.
reviews.skip_if: Projects without a runnable baseline or measurable evaluation path.

reviews.name: tutti
reviews.verdict: Tutti is worth evaluating if you regularly carry context between supported agents.
reviews.skip_if: People who need a Linux desktop download from the supplied Quick Start: it lists macOS and Windows, but no Linux package.

reviews.name: GPT-SoVITS
reviews.verdict: Shortlist GPT-SoVITS for an attended dubbing workflow that needs recording preparation and reference-based speech.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring measured synthesis quality or throughput before choosing a tool: our run contains neither measurement.

reviews.name: unilm
reviews.verdict: Use UniLM to locate and study a named research project, and consider PFPO when reproducing its pseudo-feedback method is your goal.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting one installation and support boundary for all UniLM projects.

reviews.name: biosecurity-agent
reviews.verdict: Biosecurity Agent version 0.1.2 is worth evaluating as a supervised evidence-workflow experiment: our recorded install, build and test commands succeeded.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking clinical diagnosis: the pinned README explicitly excludes that purpose.

reviews.name: cloudflare-os
reviews.verdict: Cloudflare OS is worth a bounded engineering pilot if personal AI-built applications and explicit service permissions match your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Nontechnical teams expecting a finished office suite with little operational work Organizations requiring a documented production deployment on their own servers today; the supplied README marks that tooling and guidance as coming soon Buyers requiring independently verified isolation, integration reliability…

reviews.name: Pentest-Swarm-AI
reviews.verdict: Pentest Swarm AI is a reasonable candidate for a supervised lab evaluation if its shared-board architecture interests you.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone without explicit written permission to test the target Teams requiring independently demonstrated autonomous assessment quality Buyers who need verified scope enforcement, report accuracy or production reliability before adoption Operators unable to isolate tool execution and review consequential actions

reviews.name: Open-Generative-AI
reviews.verdict: Open Generative AI is worth evaluating when you want its Muapi interface or selected desktop local engines.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need this recorded checkout to pass a production build without further investigation.

reviews.name: cwc-workshops
reviews.verdict: Use cwc-workshops for exercises you are prepared to verify and maintain.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a maintained production starter or upstream maintenance support.

reviews.name: deepwiki-rs
reviews.verdict: Litho is worth a limited trial if you want model-generated C4 documentation and can review the result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require verified sentence-level source citations before accepting generated claims.

reviews.name: plandex
reviews.verdict: Plandex merits a restricted evaluation if its plan-and-diff workflow fits your work and you can operate the local server.
