reviews.skip_if: New users seeking Plandex Cloud: the README says it began winding down on October 3, 2025 and no longer accepts new users.

reviews.name: orca
reviews.verdict: Orca is worth evaluating if comparing several CLI-agent attempts in separate worktrees is a recurring task.
reviews.skip_if: Developers whose existing single-agent terminal workflow already meets their needs.

reviews.name: QuantDinger
reviews.verdict: QuantDinger is worth evaluating for Python research and paper trading if your team can operate its service stack.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking investment advice, guaranteed returns, or an unattended profitable trading system.

reviews.name: OpenMetadata
reviews.verdict: OpenMetadata is worth evaluating when a platform team needs catalog discovery, lineage, quality, governance, and assistant access to maintained metadata.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a local trial below the documented Docker allocation of 6 GiB of memory and 4 vCPUs.

reviews.name: MaxKB
reviews.verdict: MaxKB is worth a focused trial if its documented combination of RAG, workflows, and MCP tools matches your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who need demonstrated retrieval quality, provider compatibility, or production capacity from this review: our run measured repository setup only.

reviews.name: cc-switch
reviews.verdict: CC Switch is worth evaluating when changing providers and maintaining configuration across several coding tools has become routine work.
reviews.skip_if: Users whose operating system does not meet the documented requirements: Windows 10+, macOS 12+, or Linux with glibc 2.35+ and WebKitGTK 4.1.

reviews.name: faceswap
reviews.verdict: Faceswap is worth evaluating if preparing datasets and training a face-swapping model are part of the work you want to do.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting an immediate swap without dataset preparation or model training.

reviews.name: wenzi-xiaohongshu-workflow
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run Wenzi's skills pack because no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile was available, so neither agent behavior nor publishing outcomes were verified.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the README and inspected skill bodies are Chinese, with no English README listed.

reviews.name: turnstile-token
reviews.verdict: Our turnstile-token run passed all 49 tests, but the verify command checks token format without confirming Cloudflare acceptance.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking actual token validation: the README says verify checks shape only, and only Cloudflare can determine acceptance.

reviews.name: captcha-api
reviews.verdict: Our captcha-api run passed all 36 tests, but its batch response drops the browser identity the README says follow-up requests need.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a self-hosted solver: the README requires a Clearance account and API key.

reviews.name: third-hand
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run Third Hand because commit 412fbb8 requires a macOS Swift environment and offers no Docker route, while the downloadable v0.1.3 sits 23 commits behind current source.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Macs or systems below macOS 14: the downloadable app targets Apple Silicon and macOS 14 or newer.

reviews.name: repopilot
reviews.verdict: RepoPilot merits a bounded trial for maintainers who can supply trusted tests, explicit task selection and an isolated worker.
reviews.skip_if: Repositories outside the documented public, text-only scope or above its 10,000-file / 16 MiB limits.

reviews.name: stonkfly
reviews.verdict: Our Stonkfly run passed 41 tests, but installing its 151 packages produced a 489 MB environment with 20 known vulnerabilities, so we would keep v0.1.0 away from live Coinbase credentials.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a profitable trading bot: the project explicitly says no profitable learning or strategy improvement has been demonstrated.

reviews.name: mactap-app
reviews.verdict: We did not run MacTap because our sandbox lacks a supported Swift path and the repository has no Dockerfile, while 3 open issues include confirmed accidental triggers in release 2.1.2.
reviews.skip_if: Original M1 MacBook Air owners and other Macs that do not expose the required SPU HID motion report: the README says knock detection will not work and there is no keyboard fallback.

reviews.name: Rose
reviews.verdict: Our Rose install took 10 seconds, but pytest hit an X display error and pip-audit found 51 known vulnerabilities before we ever reached a Windows League client.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or Linux users: the README requires Windows 10 or 11, and the packaged build depends on Windows tooling.

reviews.name: laya
reviews.verdict: Our Laya install pulled 141 packages and 527 MB, but pytest stopped after 3 seconds because `pytest_asyncio` was missing and the audit found 5 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a verified clean install: our environment had 5 known vulnerabilities, and pytest stopped because `pytest_asyncio` was missing.

reviews.name: prod-FARM-IOS-Core
reviews.verdict: Our Phone Farm iOS install failed after 39 seconds when `node-native-ocr` hit `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` under Node 22.23.2, so setup needs hands-on investigation before a device ever connects.
reviews.skip_if: Linux-only or Windows-only operators: the setup requires macOS, full Xcode, a signed WebDriverAgent, an Apple Developer team, and a physical iPhone.

reviews.name: invisible_dots
reviews.verdict: Consider invisible_dots for a supervised trial when persistent files and browser identities justify running a QEMU VM per agent.
reviews.skip_if: Readers expecting the current documentation to describe a dedicated AIHawk job application workflow.

reviews.name: follow-builders
reviews.verdict: Use Follow Builders as a personal trial if its curated sources suit you and you already have an agent.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need to add or remove sources locally.

reviews.name: fire-your-seo-agency
reviews.verdict: Use fire-your-seo-agency as a supervised Claude Code audit workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers seeking independently demonstrated traffic or citation gains from this repository.

reviews.name: AI-Trader
reviews.verdict: Our AI-Trader run installed 46 packages in 10 seconds with 0 audit findings, but the repository exposed neither a build target nor a test target for us to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a tested path to real brokerage execution: the detailed skill describes simulated trading, while external trades are recorded from prices supplied by the caller.

reviews.name: outlook-auto-register
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 51 packages in 24 seconds and built in 5 seconds, but commit 397165a offered no test target, so Outlook Auto Register is easy to assemble and hard to trust unattended.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning bulk account creation without written permission: the README says users must comply with Microsoft terms and accept the consequences.

reviews.name: camofox-browser
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Camofox Browser if you need Camoufox behind a REST service and can operate that service yourself.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a source installation verified by our sandbox: this run stopped before build or tests.

reviews.name: skypilot
reviews.verdict: SkyPilot merits evaluation when a shared task interface across different infrastructure is the requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking evidence here of successful GPU launches, provider compatibility, or cost savings: our recorded run measured none of those.

reviews.name: terraform
reviews.verdict: Terraform merits evaluation when versioned infrastructure configuration and reviewable plans fit your team's workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations whose licensing requirements exclude BSL 1.1 before the applicable version's change date.

reviews.name: nuvex-services
reviews.verdict: Our Gild Contract checkout, now Nuvex services, installed 316 packages in 18 seconds, built in 16 seconds, and passed all 5 reported Vitest tests.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking the on-chain contracts: the README explicitly places the protocol in a separate repository.

reviews.name: tax-doc-classifier
reviews.verdict: Our tax-doc-classifier install stopped after 18 seconds on unapproved esbuild scripts, so the repository did not clear the first setup gate despite its small 0.2 MB checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Scanned-document workflows without OCR: a page with no text layer is reported as blank.

reviews.name: lead
reviews.verdict: Our Lead run installed 83 packages, then both build and tests stopped because `$PGRX_HOME` did not exist, so adoption starts with the exact pgrx setup the README specifies.
reviews.skip_if: Production search workloads: the README calls Lead intentionally unsuitable because every scan returns all heap pages for PostgreSQL to recheck.

reviews.name: TradeGenuis-box
reviews.verdict: Our TradeGenuis-box run installed 35 packages in 23 seconds and built in 9, but the repository offered no test target, so it is easy to prepare and unproven where money decisions start.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs English setup or strategy documentation: the only guide in commit a319a19 is Chinese.

reviews.name: instagram-private-graph
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 46 packages in 18 seconds and found 0 known vulnerabilities, but the repository supplied no test target and its score model has no published calibration.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking proof of a follow, friendship, identity, location, or offline relationship: the README explicitly says graph lines and scores do not establish those facts.

reviews.name: timeseries-atlas
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run Time Series Atlas because it found Python files but no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting an installable Python package: the repository has Python files, but no `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, requirements file, or Dockerfile.

reviews.name: vitess
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Vitess when you need to shard MySQL and can fund an application and operations trial.
reviews.skip_if: Applications whose existing MySQL deployment meets their requirements and whose teams have no concrete need for sharding.

reviews.name: Crucix
reviews.verdict: Crucix merits a private evaluation if you want a broad OSINT watch screen and will verify its output.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking an independently validated intelligence or trading system.

reviews.name: czsc
reviews.verdict: CZSC merits evaluation when Chan theory and Chinese documentation fit the research team.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need an English tutorial path established by this review: the supplied first-party extracts are primarily Chinese, and their English coverage was not verified.

reviews.name: harvey-labs
reviews.verdict: Harvey LAB is worth considering when your question concerns an agent's finished legal work and your team can audit the grading criteria.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a small checkout: our recorded checkout occupied 3,223.9 MB.

reviews.name: minio
reviews.verdict: For a new production deployment requiring upstream maintenance, evaluate a replacement before adopting MinIO community source.
reviews.skip_if: New deployments that require maintenance from this community upstream.

reviews.name: world-execute-me-dsh-pv
reviews.verdict: Our run installed world-execute-me-dsh-pv's 2 npm packages in 9 seconds, but skipped build and test steps, leaving the finished video unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting the exact published video: the README documents replacement dancer footage, different checkpoint numbers, and button-color differences.

reviews.name: xss-specialist
reviews.verdict: Our xss-specialist run passed all 43 tests in 4 seconds after an install that used 5,868 MB, making the repository workable for a research evaluation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams replacing a production web scanner: the README calls this a research prototype with authorized-pilot status.

reviews.name: blueprint-animation
reviews.verdict: Blueprint Animation v1.3.1 supplies a Claude Design skill and sample scene, but leaves out the animation starter its workflow requires.
reviews.skip_if: Agencies or paid-product teams assuming unrestricted commercial use: the README requires written permission under CC BY-NC 4.0.

reviews.name: saas-motion-kit
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run saas-motion-kit because the harness found no supported ecosystem and no Dockerfile, leaving its setup and rendering reliability unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking unattended batch production: the skill explicitly stops for a human decision at every stage.

reviews.name: MHI2Q-CarPlay-AltScreen
reviews.verdict: We did not run MHI2Q-CarPlay-AltScreen, and its latest LTE display fix still lacks vehicle validation according to the release notes.
reviews.skip_if: MHI2 owners or anyone outside AUG22: the README excludes MHI2 and says the installer rejects other firmware.

reviews.name: xgoduck_hardware
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run XGO-Duck, and its hardware docs warn that older expansion boards reverse ground and signal on three servo connectors.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners expecting a finished print profile: the README says the validated profile is still undocumented.

reviews.name: jev-browser
reviews.verdict: Our Jev Browser run installed 65 packages, then failed its build and 16 of 92 tests, so this checkout needs repair before it can serve as a release gate.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean build and suite before adoption: our report-template copy failed, and 16 tests failed during the browser-start path.

reviews.name: AirCard-Windows
reviews.verdict: Our run of AirCard-Windows installed 305 packages, then failed to build in Debian on Windows-only APIs after 123 seconds, so Windows operation remains unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users expecting a portable Rust app: our Debian build failed on Windows-specific APIs.

reviews.name: ZygiskNext
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run ZygiskNext at commit 22fe320 because the C repository has no supported harness ecosystem or Dockerfile, so we have no independent build or test result.
reviews.skip_if: Security teams that require auditable implementation source: the current main branch exposes an API header and documentation, while the README reserves all rights and forbids modification, redistribution, and extracting code.

reviews.name: expo-dynamic-notifications
reviews.verdict: Our install pulled 596 packages and occupied 1,361 MB, yet the repository supplied no build or test target, so this is expensive source to adopt without an automated safety net.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting an npm library: `package.json` marks the project private, and the README installs it by cloning the whole app.

reviews.name: wx-cli-again
reviews.verdict: Our wx-cli-again run built in 219 seconds and passed all 280 tests, making the public Rust snapshot unusually convincing on code health.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the public README and operating guidance are in Chinese, with no English version linked.

reviews.name: regen-icons
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 0 packages in 6 seconds, then the build and tests both failed on a missing generator module, so Regen Icons is safer to adopt as an SVG source than as a turnkey authoring tool.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a published npm dependency: the README says the `regen-icons` package is prepared but not published.

reviews.name: AnyPS5
reviews.verdict: AnyPS5 is worth evaluating for relinker and system-library research.
reviews.skip_if: Players choosing software on the assumption of broad PS5 game compatibility: the supplied evidence does not establish that coverage.

reviews.name: DuoFold-Android
reviews.verdict: Our DuoFold build and test commands both stopped after 6 seconds with `./gradlew: Permission denied`, so the source checkout did not clear the first reproducibility check.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone uncomfortable granting Shizuku and accessibility access to an app that captures the current display, even though the README says it has no Internet permission and does not save normal screen images.

reviews.name: DuoLikeAnimation
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox produced no install, build, or test result for commit 0aa5256 because Swift/Xcode is outside its supported ecosystems.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a Swift Package dependency: the repository ships an Xcode app project, not a packaged library.

reviews.name: routeVSCODE
reviews.verdict: Our routeVSCODE run installed 78 packages in 19 seconds with 0 known vulnerabilities, but the repository gave us no build or test target to verify.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams that need support material they can hand to every developer: the README, setup guide, and troubleshooting guide are written mainly in Indonesian.

reviews.name: selfdb
reviews.verdict: Our selfdb converter install took 17 seconds and 37 packages, but pytest found 0 tests in 2 seconds; the meaningful project checks are Nix-driven shell scripts that our run did not execute.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone shipping redistributed software today: GitHub detects no license, and open issue #1 asks the author to add one.

reviews.name: h4cker
reviews.verdict: Use H4cker for cybersecurity resource discovery.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring evidence that individual scripts and labs have passed automated validation: our run does not provide it.

reviews.name: dex
reviews.verdict: Our Dex checkout installed 672 packages in 171 seconds, then all 7 test targets failed before any test passed because the embedded web bundle was absent.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that require stable upgrades today: the README calls Dex pre-launch and warns that breaking changes may arrive before formal launch.

reviews.name: opcode
reviews.verdict: Our Opcode install pulled 516 packages and 390 MB, while npm audit found 15 known vulnerabilities and the repository offered no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean dependency audit: our npm audit found 15 known vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 8 high.

reviews.name: OhMyKeymint
reviews.verdict: Our OhMyKeymint run installed 209 packages, then both the 118-second build and 6-second test step failed at the `bssl-sys` placeholder crate.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial products or paid services: the additional Oh My Keymint License expressly prohibits commercial use.

reviews.name: Telegram
reviews.verdict: Use DrKLO/Telegram when the official Android client source is the starting point you need and you can meet its documented build, identity and source-publication requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a small client-library example: our dated checkout measured 49,719 files, approximately 7,911,420 source lines and 1,248.3 MB.

reviews.name: gotohp
reviews.verdict: Our gotohp build took 6 seconds, but all 7 `go test` targets failed after 45 seconds because two Linux libraries were unavailable.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who requires an official Google-supported sign-in flow: the README calls gotohp unofficial and asks users to copy an `oauth_token` cookie, use ReVanced with ADB, or intercept a rooted Android app.

reviews.name: marktext
reviews.verdict: MarkText is worth evaluating if you want visual Markdown editing and do not need built-in knowledge management or tags.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need knowledge management and tags: MarkText's FAQ explicitly excludes those features.

reviews.name: teamai-cli
reviews.verdict: Consider TeamAI CLI for a limited pilot when shared agent configuration already belongs in your Git workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring identical capabilities across every listed client: the README matrix contains explicit gaps.

reviews.name: gpuix
reviews.verdict: GPUIX is worth a platform trial for React or Solid teams that specifically want GPUI rendering without a webview.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring verified application behavior from this review: our run covered dependency installation and a source build, not a running interface.

reviews.name: darwin-vm
reviews.verdict: Our darwin-vm checkout installed 60 Rust packages in 9 seconds, but both the 10-second build and 4-second test run stopped because `MESON_BUILD_ROOT` was absent.
reviews.skip_if: Mobile app teams that need a visual iPhone simulator: the README rules out a screen, graphics, GUI apps, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and full SpringBoard.

reviews.name: lazycodex
reviews.verdict: LazyCodex is worth evaluating if you specifically want OmO's documented planning, project-memory, and execution workflows inside Codex.
reviews.skip_if: Users who want to keep their Codex home free of additional managed configuration, roles, links, and plugin state.

reviews.name: UniGetUI
reviews.verdict: UniGetUI is worth evaluating if you want one graphical interface across several package managers.
reviews.skip_if: People who require independently verified installation, performance, or reliability results before adoption People expecting UniGetUI to guarantee the safety of third-party packages Teams requiring proven unattended deployment or identical behavior across operating systems; neither was evaluated here

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: HumanLayer Skills is worth evaluating one task at a time: the README now lists seven skills, including rpi and visual-pr alongside the React and recurring-workflow procedures.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need measured evidence that these skills work in their agent environment.

reviews.name: power-platform-skills
reviews.verdict: Power Platform Skills is worth a scoped trial for developers who already understand their Power Platform environment and can review agent changes.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking evidence that the entire marketplace has passed integration or deployment testing: our recorded run covers only selected local Power Automate checks.

reviews.name: sliver
reviews.verdict: Sliver is worth evaluating for authorized teams that need the cross-platform implants and C2 transports documented by the project.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a vulnerability scanner Teams without authorization or a defined testing scope Buyers who need this review to demonstrate a working installed server or client Organizations unable to review licensing and validate their deployment

reviews.name: social-analyzer
reviews.verdict: Our Social Analyzer run reported 29 known dependency vulnerabilities, and its test command only printed a placeholder error, so I would restrict it to a contained local evaluation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a public investigation service: the README says the app has no access control and is meant for local use.

reviews.name: cyclomatic-complexity-skill
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox could not run commit 567886f because the repository has no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile, so there is no execution evidence behind this skill yet.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an analyzer they can run in CI: this repository contains instructions for Claude and delegates measurement to outside tools.

reviews.name: refactoring-ui-skill
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run commit 4887214 because this CSS-classified repository has no supported build ecosystem or Dockerfile, so adoption rests on reading the instructions and reviewing Claude's output.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require executable tests before adopting generated design rules: the repository has no supported build ecosystem or Dockerfile, so our lab could not run it.

reviews.name: iroh
reviews.verdict: Iroh is worth evaluating for Rust applications that need public-key dialing with direct connections and relay fallback.
reviews.skip_if: Readers looking for a complete file-sync application: the README lists blob transfer, gossip, and document storage as separate protocols built on Iroh.

reviews.name: argent
reviews.verdict: Trial Argent for assistant-controlled app diagnosis, with an explicit check of failing actions before accepting flow verdicts as release evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking verified device operation or release-gate reliability from this review.

reviews.name: archify
reviews.verdict: Consider Archify for interactive architecture handoffs when you already use a compatible agent and can check the diagram against its sources.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring hosted sharing or WYSIWYG editing, which the README excludes from scope.

reviews.name: roslyn
reviews.verdict: Use Roslyn when your tool needs the C# or Visual Basic compiler model, custom diagnostics or analysis across a solution.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a general parser for languages beyond C# and Visual Basic.

reviews.name: herdrm
reviews.verdict: herdrm is worth evaluating if you already use herdr and want a native Mac overview of agents and terminals across machines.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking this macOS application for Windows, Linux or macOS 13 and older.

reviews.name: babua-dsa-patterns-course
reviews.verdict: Use Babua DSA Patterns Course if Hindi instruction and a fixed daily sequence help you keep practicing.
reviews.skip_if: Learners who need English spoken instruction: the README says the explanations are in Hindi, although the main written pages are in English.

reviews.name: paper
reviews.verdict: Read this paper if you are designing a serious plugin host or self-modifying agent runtime, because it gives unusually precise names and rules to problems that are often handled with restart hooks.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for an installable library in this repository: it contains only a README and PDF, while the implementation lives separately in `cordiverse/cordis`.

reviews.name: gortex
reviews.verdict: Gortex is worth a controlled trial when your agents need relationships across repositories.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking independently verified indexing accuracy, query latency or token savings from this review: our run measured none of those workloads.

reviews.name: agentsview
reviews.verdict: Evaluate AgentsView for local transcript retrieval with a small archive you can check against the originals.
reviews.skip_if: Readers requiring a successful installation demonstrated by our sandbox.

reviews.name: union
reviews.verdict: Our Union run installed 2,068 packages in 42 seconds and used 2,010 MB, while build and tests were skipped because the selected route had no targets.
reviews.skip_if: Teams restricted to a Node-only toolchain: the README's development shell also supplies Go and Rust, and contracts include Solidity.

reviews.name: bilibili-video-downloader
reviews.verdict: Bilibili Video Downloader is worth evaluating for Chinese-reading users who want the README's Emby metadata and graphical download workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who require supplied English setup documentation: the provided README and issue extracts are Chinese Users seeking independently verified desktop installation, account login, or download reliability: our run did not cover those workflows Users expecting restricted third-party plugins: the maintainer…

reviews.name: actors
reviews.verdict: Rivet Actors merits a focused evaluation when durable state, scheduling, and realtime connections belong to the same application entity.
reviews.skip_if: Applications whose stateless request handling does not need durable actors.

reviews.name: GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold
reviews.verdict: Our GLM recipe build passed in 1 second, but pytest failed with an internal error and ran no tests, so this run does not validate the inference service.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a laptop installation: the README requires paired GB10 systems, a ConnectX-7 link, NVIDIA containers, and substantial free memory.

reviews.name: Astra-Ares
reviews.verdict: Our Astra-Ares run installed 5 packages in 2 seconds and passed all 65 tests, but it did not measure the patched Codex compilation or token savings.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting an npm-only setup: the README requires a patched Codex compilation and offers no prebuilt Ares download.

reviews.name: agent-jev
reviews.verdict: Our AgentJev run installed 74 packages and used 5,638 MB, then ended with 19 passing cases, 2 setup errors, and 9 known dependency vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing tools to stop whenever safety inspection is unavailable: the bundled Claude Code hook proceeds on server errors.

reviews.name: JevHarness
reviews.verdict: Our JevHarness run installed in 39 seconds and built in 12 seconds, but tests finished with 17 failures, including explicit macOS sandbox requirements.
reviews.skip_if: Linux operators who need functional Python nodes: the README requires a macOS native sandbox, and our Debian run hit that restriction.

reviews.name: minorun-marp-skill
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run commit 736fd5e because it found no supported ecosystem and no Dockerfile, so this review cannot promise that the six checkers work on your machine.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the README, three skill files, tool output, and editing rules are written in Japanese, with no English guide included.

reviews.name: openjev-sglang
reviews.verdict: Evaluate SGLang's native decisions API for a new service.
reviews.skip_if: New adopters looking for the maintainer's recommended implementation.

reviews.name: codex-astra-luna-orchestrator
reviews.verdict: Consider this bundle if you already use Codex and want reusable role configurations for work that benefits from separation.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking demonstrated token savings or faster coding: our recorded run measured neither.

reviews.name: agent-lightning
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Microsoft Agent Lightning when preserving an existing agent's execution flow is a training requirement and you can validate the GPU stack.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring reproduced GPU training results or benchmark improvements from this review.

reviews.name: cc-connect
reviews.verdict: CC-Connect is worth evaluating if you need chat access to local coding agents across several messaging platforms and can operate the bridge yourself.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking a hosted service without local agent setup Teams that need independently verified end-to-end chat operation before choosing a tool Operators who cannot restrict access to local projects and privileged commands Buyers requiring a reconciled clean build and test…

reviews.name: codex-with-chatgpt
reviews.verdict: Treat Codex with ChatGPT as a trial for a specific workflow: ChatGPT plans and reviews, while Codex executes.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs this review to establish successful installation or a working ChatGPT connection: our run established neither.

reviews.name: northcinder
reviews.verdict: NorthCinder is a candidate for supervised shopping experiments, with documented boundaries around evidence, ranking, and purchase approval.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers seeking qualified routine shopping research: the README explicitly says no host and model combination is qualified.

reviews.name: lean-ctx
reviews.verdict: LeanCTX merits a controlled evaluation for developers whose agents repeatedly read files and noisy shell output.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who mostly use tiny repositories or need raw logs throughout: the README identifies these as cases with lower payoff.

reviews.name: open_deep_research
reviews.verdict: Open Deep Research is worth studying if you want a configurable LangGraph research workflow and can own its maintenance.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need upstream maintenance: GitHub marks this repository archived and read-only.

reviews.name: swarm-forge
reviews.verdict: SwarmForge is a brilliantly unconventional tool for developers who live in the terminal.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners unfamiliar with `tmux`, shell scripting, or advanced git concepts like worktrees.

reviews.name: OpenHands
reviews.verdict: OpenHands Agent Canvas is worth evaluating when managing agents across several execution backends solves a specific workflow problem.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting the direct launcher to restrict the agent's access to the host filesystem.

reviews.name: reverse-skill
reviews.verdict: reverse-skill is a brilliant and wildly ambitious attempt to solve a real problem: AI agents are powerful but lack strategic, domain-specific knowledge for complex security tasks.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners in cybersecurity.

reviews.name: playport
reviews.verdict: Our PlayPort web client installed 19 packages in 6 seconds and passed its build and test commands in 3 seconds each, but the macOS receiver was outside that run.
reviews.skip_if: Raspberry Pi or Linux deployments: the README says Linux is unsupported because the Bluetooth bridge is macOS-only.

reviews.name: Comma
reviews.verdict: Our Comma run used 1,618 MB after a successful 75-second pnpm install, while build and tests were skipped, so full-stack readiness remains unmeasured.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting a pnpm install to start the whole product: the README's self-host route also operates PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO, ClickHouse, and Mailpit.

reviews.name: ProsperoEden
reviews.verdict: Our ProsperoEden build failed after 116 seconds, and the test step failed after 6 seconds at the same native-dependency setup script.
reviews.skip_if: Owners of unmodified PS5 consoles: the documented installation requires a homebrew environment and ShadowMountPlus.

reviews.name: zulu
reviews.verdict: Our Zulu Go-service run passed all 14 reported tests after a 54-second build, but it did not validate the Swift iOS or Mac apps.
reviews.skip_if: iPhone users below the documented iOS 27 minimum.

reviews.name: knoweldge-base
reviews.verdict: Our knowledge-base run passed all 53 tests, but pip-audit reported 120 known vulnerabilities, so I would keep adoption to an isolated trial until those findings are reviewed.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring an English interface immediately: the checked-in login and navigation screens are Chinese, despite the English README.

reviews.name: jeff
reviews.verdict: Trial jeff for local Jev-compatible decisions, with a workload comparison as the next step.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean test result from the recorded environment.

reviews.name: FounderOS-DEMO
reviews.verdict: Our Founder OS run passed all 3,464 tests, but its 30-second production build failed and npm audit found 23 vulnerabilities, so this is a strong interface reference rather than a ready public deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a working business backend after one launch: the repository identifies itself as a demo, and all names, clients, finances, and social figures are placeholders.

reviews.name: life-recorder
reviews.verdict: Our receiver install took 24 seconds and the build passed in 8, but pytest collected 0 tests, so Life Recorder is an inspectable personal project rather than a verified recording appliance.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot obtain informed consent where recording is required: the app can continue capturing with the screen locked and while other apps are open.

reviews.name: bank-sampah
reviews.verdict: Our install pulled 81 npm packages and used 147 MB, but the build failed after 12 seconds, so Bank Sampah Digital is a source base to inspect rather than a deployment we can vouch for.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations outside Indonesia that cannot translate the product and remodel its local administrative hierarchy: the README, locale, and roles are Indonesian, and no English guide is provided.

reviews.name: usque-custom-pro
reviews.verdict: Our usque-custom-pro run installed 45 packages in 18 seconds with 0 known vulnerabilities, but it had no build or test target and the repository has no stated license.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that need clear reuse rights: GitHub reports no license, and the repository tree contains no license file.

reviews.name: ace-step-ui
reviews.verdict: Our ACE-Step UI run installed 172 packages in 5 seconds and built in 3 seconds, but npm audit found 13 vulnerabilities and the repository supplied no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting the 5-second Node install to produce music by itself: the README also requires ACE-Step 1.5, Python 3.10 or newer, FFmpeg, model downloads, and usually an NVIDIA GPU.

reviews.name: go-music-dl
reviews.verdict: Go Music DL is worth a limited trial for Chinese-speaking NAS users who want several music sources and local-library tools together.
reviews.skip_if: Users who require an English setup guide in the supplied documentation.

reviews.name: ever-gauzy
reviews.verdict: Ever Gauzy is compelling when its unusual combination of ERP functions and employee time and activity tracking closely matches your operating model.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a five-minute, one-command install; our dependency installation did not finish in 15 minutes Buyers who need a clearly stable hosted service today; the README labels the SaaS offering as alpha Organizations uncomfortable with AGPL-3.0 obligations for modified network…

reviews.name: wttr.in
reviews.verdict: Consider wttr.in for terminal forecasts and status displays where its documented presentation formats fit your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking proof of an installed, working server from our lab record: it contains no installed-binary check or served-weather workload.

reviews.name: HAMi
reviews.verdict: HAMi merits a hardware-specific trial when a Kubernetes platform needs accelerator sharing or heterogeneous scheduling.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who need in-container quotas to provide a hard security boundary against hostile workloads with enough privilege to bypass their own hooks.

reviews.name: remux
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Remux separately if its documented remote sources and Jellyfin-compatible API meet your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs this review to demonstrate a working server deployment or playback compatibility.

reviews.name: boop
reviews.verdict: Boop is worth evaluating if you want a self-hosted developer-event inbox and can own the iOS signing and APNs setup.
reviews.skip_if: People who need a ready mobile client without Apple signing work.

reviews.name: snagtime
reviews.verdict: Keep SnagTime in local evaluation until you can reproduce its documented setup, produce a build, and explain the database-related test failures.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a verified deployment ready for customer bookings: our sandbox did not establish one.

reviews.name: awg-manager
reviews.verdict: AWG Manager is a reasonable candidate for Keenetic owners who want browser control and can validate their own router setup.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking verified router deployment, throughput or reliability results from this review Users seeking a general Linux VPS installer rather than a Keenetic management interface Anyone who requires an English installation guide already verified here; the supplied current README exposes…

reviews.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Dual-DGX-Sparks
reviews.verdict: Our 2026-08-29 sandbox did not execute commit 344f9d0 because this Shell repository has no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone with one DGX Spark or a different GPU layout: the documented topology assumes two GB10 nodes joined by a direct ConnectX-7 link.

reviews.name: spacedrive
reviews.verdict: Our Spacedrive install failed after 76 seconds at its Bun-only preinstall guard, which makes the current v2 alpha suitable only for developers testing with disposable data.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to test with disposable data first: open issue 3056 reports that v2.0.0-alpha.2 deleted a nonempty root-level `tmp` folder on tracked Windows volumes.

reviews.name: aegis-vault
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Aegis Vault with disposable credentials first.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs this review to establish that important credentials are safe: our sandbox did not exercise vault behavior.

reviews.name: FreeTube
reviews.verdict: FreeTube is worth considering for account-free desktop viewing and local subscriptions, provided you accept its beta status and configure IP protection separately when needed.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting installation alone to make video requests anonymous.

reviews.name: TokenHub
reviews.verdict: TokenHub merits a controlled evaluation when project ownership, routing policy and provider-bill reconciliation address a specific platform need.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who need this review to establish production reliability, throughput or billing accuracy.

reviews.name: documenso
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Documenso when self-hosting document signing is an operational choice with an owner assigned.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a verified production signing deployment from this review: our run covered dependency installation and a build, not signing workflows.

reviews.name: Pumpkin
reviews.verdict: Pumpkin is worth evaluating for Rust development or a disposable staging server.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who need this review to establish vanilla gameplay parity, live performance, or world migration reliability: our recorded run measured none of those.

reviews.name: OpenList
reviews.verdict: OpenList is worth a provider-specific trial if its documented previews, direct downloads, and multi-storage interface fit your needs.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a verified backup target or measured transfer performance: our recorded run tested neither.

reviews.name: Olares
reviews.verdict: Olares merits a controlled evaluation if you want Kubernetes-backed storage, networking, apps and local AI in one environment.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking only a storage dashboard or Docker app interface who have no need for Olares's broader platform Anyone expecting this review to establish installed-system reliability, GPU performance or backup recovery Contributors who require a clean source-check result before proceeding:…

reviews.name: fanqiang
reviews.verdict: Our Fanqiang install stopped after 11 seconds because a replaced local Go module was missing, so developers should not expect the measured checkout to build as-is.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the main README and linked setup guides are Chinese, and the FQNews page has only a brief English project note.

reviews.name: 30-Days-Of-React
reviews.verdict: Our Node 22 sandbox installed 1,223 packages in 82 seconds, but both the build and test commands failed, so use 30 Days of React as course text and bring a current practice environment.
reviews.skip_if: Complete programming beginners: the README requires intermediate HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and points weaker JavaScript learners to a separate 30-day course first.

reviews.name: linuxdo-idea-ui
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run linuxdo-idea-ui because the JavaScript userscript exposed no supported ecosystem and the repository had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who does not read Chinese: the README and interface description are Chinese, with no English guide linked.

reviews.name: layer5
reviews.verdict: Our Layer5 install pulled 1,990 packages and used 1,861 MB, then the 249-second build failed and npm audit reported 84 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for the Meshery management plane: that product lives in `meshery/meshery`, while this repository builds the Layer5 website.

reviews.name: octo-web
reviews.verdict: Our OCTO Web install consumed 1,178 MB, then both the 8-second build and 10-second test steps failed, so this checkout is a risky foundation unless your team can trace a large pnpm monorepo.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a standalone chat application: the README says the client expects `octo-server` at `http://localhost:8080`, and several features belong to other OCTO repositories.

reviews.name: OpenCut
reviews.verdict: Our OpenCut rewrite build installed 649 packages, ran for 204 seconds, and failed because `xkbcommon-x11` was missing, while its desktop app currently only opens a window.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs a working editor from this repository today: its README directs users to `opencut-classic`, and the desktop guide says it only opens a window.

reviews.name: Offensive-Security-AI-Models
reviews.verdict: Offensive-Security-AI-Models supplies a README and an image rather than a runnable security assistant, and our lab did not run it.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a working security assistant: the repository contains a README and an image, with no application to deploy.

reviews.name: Deepseek-Harness-Easy-Setup
reviews.verdict: We could not execute commit 27460bc because our sandbox supports neither this PowerShell ecosystem nor a Docker path, so there is no lab proof that its installer completes.
reviews.skip_if: macOS, Linux, Windows on Arm, or 32-bit Windows users: the build and bundled runtime target Windows 10 or 11 x64.

reviews.name: Covalent-MAS
reviews.verdict: Our Covalent-MAS run passed 2 tests in 3 seconds, but those tests cover contract wiring and JSONL storage rather than drug generation, docking execution, or the published benchmark claims.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers seeking a ready covalent-molecule generator or optimizer: the repository defines protocols for both but includes no implementation of either.

reviews.name: claude-siri-ai
reviews.verdict: Claude for Siri requires macOS 27 with both SIP and AMFI disabled, making it a development-Mac experiment rather than a daily assistant.
reviews.skip_if: Daily-driver Macs: the README requires both SIP and AMFI to be disabled, reducing two macOS protections.

reviews.name: NeuralScreen
reviews.verdict: NeuralScreen is worth considering as a noncommercial Windows experiment if whole-desktop or one-window NVIDIA processing is your goal and the README's hardware limits fit your machine.
reviews.skip_if: Competitive online players: the README explicitly advises against this use because of anti-cheat risk.

reviews.name: xialingguo-ip
reviews.verdict: xialingguo-ip offers nine Chinese cover styles and a 21:9 default, but it ships no renderer, model, English guide, or license.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the README, skill instructions, and style reference have no English version.

reviews.name: cek-probe-model
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 13 seconds and passed its 4-second build, but it found no test target for the code that assigns model-trust labels.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who need proof that a provider served a named model: the main script relies on the model describing its own identity, which is not independent verification.

reviews.name: unigit-ecosystem
reviews.verdict: Our install added 0 packages, and the repository offers no build or test target, so UNIGIT Ecosystem is a 22-file public information hub rather than a product you can evaluate locally.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking an open-source AI workbench: the scope document excludes the desktop, mobile, server, admin, website, routing, billing, tool, and context implementations.

reviews.name: unreel
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox built UNREEL in 26 seconds, but npm audit found 2 vulnerabilities and the repository provides no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require an explicit open-source license: GitHub reports no license, and the repository tree has no LICENSE file.

reviews.name: DLSS-NR-on-AMD
reviews.verdict: Our lab recorded no runnable result for commit 057c873, and release v0.4.3 ships a 15.9 MB Windows executable without the implementation source.
reviews.skip_if: Open-source contributors: the repository has no implementation source, and its license forbids modification, reverse engineering, derivatives, and redistribution.

reviews.name: agenticSeek
reviews.verdict: AgenticSeek merits a controlled evaluation by developers who can troubleshoot its stack and limit the files and credentials it can reach.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting this review to establish safe unattended operation: our recorded run did not evaluate that.

reviews.name: shrimply
reviews.verdict: Our Shrimply checkout pulled 858 packages, then both build and test stopped because the system had Pango 1.50.12 instead of the required 1.57.
reviews.skip_if: Editors protecting paid work: the README warns about irreversible project-file breakage, crashes, resource leaks, and performance regressions.

reviews.name: skill
reviews.verdict: Skill Store is useful for discovering Chinese-language agent skills and inspecting a documented catalog updater.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a bundle whose individual workflows have all been tested: our run did not exercise them.

reviews.name: logocreator
reviews.verdict: Evaluate LogoCreator if its Together AI interface and documented brand-kit workflow match your needs, but make a compatible-runtime install your first checkpoint.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs a self-hosting path already verified by our run: installation failed before build or application checks.

reviews.name: Hands-On-AI-Engineering
reviews.verdict: Our measured OCR example installed 95 packages and used 445 MB, then its build failed in 7 seconds and exposed no test target, so this collection is reference material rather than production-ready code.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a collection-wide production standard: open issue 118 documents a customer-routing example that can silently turn the string `false` into a true legal or repeat-contact flag.

reviews.name: learnopencv
reviews.verdict: Use LearnOpenCV when a specific article provides the example you need.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking one package with a shared API and installation procedure.

reviews.name: MoGe
reviews.verdict: MoGe is worth evaluating when you need single-image geometry outputs and can validate them on your own scenes.
reviews.skip_if: Developers requiring supported macOS installation: the README says macOS is unsupported because MoGe-3 depends on FlexGEMM and Triton has no macOS wheels.

reviews.name: opengrok
reviews.verdict: opengrok is worth evaluating for developers who specifically want outside models inside Grok Bot and can inspect the resulting requests.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking proof that cloud routing, model switching or voice worked in our sandbox.

reviews.name: Fizgig
reviews.verdict: Fizgig is worth evaluating if block-level LoRA editing and epoch comparison would help your workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking verified training quality or repair results from this review: our recorded run did not measure either.

reviews.name: gpt-image-skill
reviews.verdict: We did not run commit 3be04a6 because our lab had no supported ecosystem target for it and the repository had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: ChatGPT Free users expecting the skill to unlock image generation: the README says the current Free plan does not include it.

reviews.name: watermark-remover
reviews.verdict: Our watermark-remover build passed in 7 seconds, but the 80-second test run failed across installer paths because `install_skill.py` was missing from the tested checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking proof that a vendor detector will fail: the README explicitly says the tool cannot certify that outcome.

reviews.name: tradingview-mcp
reviews.verdict: Consider TradingView MCP Bridge for supervised local research and disposable Pine Script experiments.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking real trade execution: the README explicitly excludes it.

reviews.name: lampOS
reviews.verdict: Consider lampOS for an evaluation on a supported desk robot when you can maintain its configuration and verify physical behavior.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting ready-made wheel or leg locomotion: the porting guide says those need a separate LocomotionService.

reviews.name: ComfyUI-ALLinONE-MinimaxH3
reviews.verdict: Consider this beta node if you already run ComfyUI and want a common interface for MiniMax H3 workflows.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting bundled models or a standalone application from the custom-node clone.

reviews.name: claurst
reviews.verdict: Claurst merits a contained evaluation if provider choice and ACP integration fit your workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a review backed by a source build, executed tests or a measured coding workload: our run supplied none of those results.

reviews.name: everyone-can-use-english
reviews.verdict: Enjoy is worth evaluating if you read Chinese and want its documented speech and shadowing workflows.
reviews.skip_if: Learners who need verified whole-passage pronunciation assessment: in issue #1410, a collaborator states that each assessment is limited to 30 seconds.

reviews.name: gptme

reviews.verdict: pi-subagents installed in 6 seconds in our sandbox, but its test command timed out at 900 seconds without a final suite result.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting our lab to establish a passing full suite: the test command timed out after 900 seconds.

reviews.name: kimi-code
reviews.verdict: Our Kimi Code source checkout built in 91 seconds but finished its test run with 15 failures, so it does not provide a green contributor baseline at commit 743f140.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who require a green baseline before starting: our recorded test command ended with 15 failures.

reviews.name: smg
reviews.verdict: SMG's documented cache-aware routing makes it a candidate for teams with an existing inference fleet.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a standalone local model runner: the gateway quick start expects inference-worker URLs.

reviews.name: dsh-purge
reviews.verdict: Our dsh-purge installation took 7 seconds and recorded 3 dependencies, but build and tests were skipped, leaving host patching unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing permissive redistribution rights from the current branch: its license identifies it as proprietary and restricts public source redistribution.

reviews.name: AIStudio2API
reviews.verdict: AIStudio2API is a candidate for a controlled trial when an AI Studio web-protocol bridge is specifically required.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose account policies prohibit the documented Google Drive authorization or saved Google login state.

reviews.name: mesh-llm
reviews.verdict: Our Mesh LLM install failed after 12 seconds before the Rust compiler ran, leaving inference unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the automatic quick start to stay private: serve --auto joins a discovered public mesh.

reviews.name: agent-router
reviews.verdict: Our Agent Router build succeeded in 326 seconds, but the 712-second test step failed, so this run leaves upgrade behavior unresolved.
reviews.skip_if: MCP deployments requiring uninterrupted existing sessions through the default v1.2.0 upgrade: the release says clients must initialize again after the seed change.

reviews.name: gpt4free
reviews.verdict: Our GPT4Free install succeeded in 40 seconds and its build passed, while tests were skipped because no target was found, so the run supports a setup trial rather than a provider-reliability claim.
reviews.skip_if: Services that require a listed model to behave consistently across providers: the README explicitly makes availability and behavior provider-dependent.

reviews.name: verl
reviews.verdict: Our verl install occupied 6,106 MB and built successfully, but its test command ended with exit 137 after 73 seconds without a final count.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or Windows users expecting the documented uv commands to run locally: that workflow targets Linux.

reviews.name: graphiti
reviews.verdict: Our Graphiti build succeeded in 5 seconds, but its tests timed out after 900 seconds with errors and failures still unresolved.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a ready-to-expose memory endpoint: the reference MCP and REST servers intentionally omit authentication and authorization.

reviews.name: SillyTavern
reviews.verdict: Consider SillyTavern when lorebooks and prompt controls justify learning the interface and maintaining a separate backend.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a hosted chat account: the maintainers provide no online or hosted services.

reviews.name: promptfoo
reviews.verdict: Our Promptfoo run recorded 2,334 dependencies and 3,190 MB, then failed its source build and test commands, so contributors should reproduce those failures before relying on that workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean source build before adoption: our measured build and test commands both exited 1.

reviews.name: 9router
reviews.verdict: Our 9Router source build succeeded in 96 seconds, but npm audit reported 7 high-severity findings and our run found no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Operators expecting safe public exposure from copied defaults: the README defaults API-key enforcement and secure auth cookies to false.

reviews.name: langfuse
reviews.verdict: Our Langfuse source build failed after a successful 89-second installation, and the overall test command also failed, so this run does not establish a working developer setup.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a single service with no data infrastructure: the Compose example includes PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Redis, and MinIO.

reviews.name: OpenViking
reviews.verdict: Pilot OpenViking when inspectable context justifies operating a separate service.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that require a strict total search-result limit without handling duplicates: the retrieval guide says merged results may exceed the per-query limit and need not be deduplicated.

reviews.name: freellmapi
reviews.verdict: The supplied FreeLLMAPI run passed 3,950 tests, but npm audit reported 29 known vulnerabilities, including 5 critical.
reviews.skip_if: Customer-facing services: the README limits the project to personal experimentation and learning and recommends a paid API before shipping.

reviews.name: airllm
reviews.verdict: AirLLM installed in 74 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but the sandbox supplied no test or generation result.
reviews.skip_if: Mac users expecting the general model list to establish compatibility with the Mac path.

reviews.name: lucky
reviews.verdict: The recorded Lucky source build succeeded in 2 seconds, but the test step failed with package build errors and did not validate a live network service.
reviews.skip_if: Operators requiring current releases to have public source: upstream says there are no current plans to open-source versions after 1.4.10.

reviews.name: zapfast
reviews.verdict: ZapFast's build failed after 707 seconds in our sandbox because pkg-config could not find PipeWire's development metadata, so we cannot judge its desktop behavior from this run.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unable to risk an account restriction: the README warns that unofficial-client use could get an account suspended.

reviews.name: aivpn
reviews.verdict: Our AIVPN build succeeded in 201 seconds, but two network-cleanup tests failed, leaving crash recovery unverified in our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone requiring guaranteed anonymity or blocking resistance: the README explicitly disclaims both.

reviews.name: Free-GST-Billing-Software
reviews.verdict: Our source build at c40309e failed after 20 seconds, and the overall test command failed after 1 second.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring an internet-facing billing service: the README says the server has no login and must not be put online.

reviews.name: AiSOC
reviews.verdict: AiSOC merits a supervised evaluation for security teams with known telemetry sources and an existing retention system.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a drop-in SIEM replacement for long-term retention and compliance search.

reviews.name: billd-desk
reviews.verdict: Reserve the public BilldDesk edition for development evaluation: its guide advises against production use, and our installation stopped before a remote session.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a production-ready public edition: its guide explicitly advises against production use.

reviews.name: umami
reviews.verdict: Our Umami build stopped after 4 seconds because DATABASE_URL was missing, and tests stopped after 5 seconds for the same setting.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a static dashboard without a database: the README requires PostgreSQL and a database connection URL.

reviews.name: mathua
reviews.verdict: Our Mathua build succeeded in 68 seconds, but verification ended with 53 passes and 1 unexplained failure.
reviews.skip_if: Learners who want unrestricted topic access: the scheduler withholds concepts with unmastered prerequisites.

reviews.name: redlib
reviews.verdict: Our Redlib build succeeded in 188 seconds, but cargo reported 57 passing tests and 4 failures, so this run does not establish a reliable everyday reader.
reviews.skip_if: People whose essential workflow requires signed-in participation: the README describes mostly signed-out functionality.

reviews.name: Mailu
reviews.verdict: Our Mailu sandbox installed in 30 seconds and built in 9 seconds, then pytest stopped after 6 seconds because it could not import Flask.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking long-term professional support from this project: the setup guide explicitly points readers seeking that service elsewhere.

reviews.name: immich-go
reviews.verdict: Commit 6ee7ad5 built in 27 seconds and its Go test summary reported 27 passed and 0 failed out of 27.
reviews.skip_if: People who still need a photo server: Immich-Go requires a running Immich instance with API access.

reviews.name: InvisiProxy-Legacy
reviews.verdict: InvisiProxy built in 2 seconds in our sandbox, but its endpoint check failed after 62 seconds with refused localhost:8080 connections.
reviews.skip_if: New deployments expecting continued work in this repository: it is archived and its README points to a successor.

reviews.name: mihon
reviews.verdict: Mihon's source build failed after 18 seconds in our sandbox because Gradle could not find an Android SDK location, leaving Android reading behavior unassessed.
reviews.skip_if: Readers expecting an included catalog: Mihon's README explicitly says the application hosts zero content.

reviews.name: changedetection.io
reviews.verdict: Shortlist changedetection.io for a self-hosted watch dashboard when you can tune selectors and configure its fetchers and notifications.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting Browser Steps to work without configuring Playwright.

reviews.name: appsmith
reviews.verdict: Trial Appsmith when several internal tools justify a shared platform with an assigned owner.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require legacy Appsmith AI datasource queries to continue unchanged: the v2.5.1 notes say existing queries have stopped working even without an upgrade.

reviews.name: skywalking
reviews.verdict: The successful source run supports a trial of commit 2a25e04 for a platform team able to operate storage, telemetry senders, a separate UI and protected admin access.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a bundled backend and dashboard: the v11.0.0 release notes say OAP no longer bundles its web UI.

reviews.name: qBittorrent
reviews.verdict: Our qBittorrent search build passed in 3 seconds, but pytest ran no tests and exited 5.
reviews.skip_if: Source builders who require upstream support while using older, unsupported dependency configurations.

reviews.name: harbor
reviews.verdict: Our Harbor sandbox built in 26 seconds but recorded 137 failures out of 393 in the go test summary, leaving the source run short of a clean result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that only need a private registry endpoint: Harbor's project administration, identity integrations and replication may add responsibilities they don't need.

reviews.name: signoz
reviews.verdict: Our SigNoz run passed all 215 reported Go tests after a 115-second install and a 218-second build, supporting a source-level trial rather than a production capacity claim.
reviews.skip_if: Self-hosters specifically seeking the Noz investigation assistant: the README makes that feature exclusive to SigNoz Cloud.

reviews.name: SmartTube
reviews.verdict: Our SmartTube build and test steps each stopped after 1 second with exit 126 and a Gradle-wrapper permission error, leaving playback unassessed.
reviews.skip_if: Owners of Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, or VegaOS Fire TV devices: the README excludes those platforms.

reviews.name: copyparty
reviews.verdict: Commit 8b4593c installed in 25 seconds and passed all 31 tests in the supplied sandbox run.
reviews.skip_if: Operators expecting restricted access from a bare launch: running without arguments grants everyone read/write access to the current folder.

reviews.name: frigate
reviews.verdict: Frigate is worth a camera trial for Home Assistant owners who want local object detection and can manage streams, storage, hardware access, and MQTT.
reviews.skip_if: Windows-only operators who require official platform support.

reviews.name: runtime
reviews.verdict: Evaluate E2B Embed when a single Linux machine with hardware virtualization fits your deployment and you can provide the required network and recovery arrangements.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring built-in TLS: Embed serves plain HTTP.

reviews.name: consul
reviews.verdict: Evaluate HashiCorp Consul when health-aware service discovery and its broader networking capabilities address a shared infrastructure requirement.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a secure deployment without configuration: HashiCorp says Consul is not secure by default.

reviews.name: gogs
reviews.verdict: Our Gogs run installed 416 dependencies in 15 seconds, but skipped build and tests, leaving the Go server unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need a firm API stability promise: the README explicitly calls API support experimental.

reviews.name: MicYou
reviews.verdict: Our MicYou build passed in 308 seconds after a 12-second install, with tests skipped because no script or target was found.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting phone pairing alone to create an input in every calling app: the README requires virtual microphone routing.

reviews.name: anki
reviews.verdict: Our Anki source build failed after 2 seconds on a missing output directory, despite a successful 13-second install, so this run does not establish a working contributor setup.
reviews.skip_if: Learners considering a source checkout just to try Anki: the README directs them to packaged versions.

reviews.name: SpiderPanel
reviews.verdict: SpiderPanel installed in 363 seconds and built in 1 second in our sandbox, but customer delivery remains unverified because no transaction was exercised and tests were skipped.
reviews.skip_if: Sellers needing unattended payment confirmation: the documented purchase flow requires an administrator to approve or reject a receipt.

reviews.name: Nova-Proxy
reviews.verdict: Build and tests each failed after 1 second at commit d25a40d in the October 14, 2026 sandbox run, so that checkout did not establish a working deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring readable, maintainable panel source: the public repository distributes a minified and obfuscated Worker while keeping that source private.

reviews.name: navidrome
reviews.verdict: Evaluate Navidrome if you want to stream a music collection you already own, and follow its release guidance.
reviews.skip_if: Listeners seeking a supplied subscription music catalog.

reviews.name: tornado
reviews.verdict: Tornado merits a trial for long-lived Python connections when the team can keep handlers non-blocking and manage server processes.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring officially supported Windows production deployment.

reviews.name: phaser
reviews.verdict: Phaser built in 12 seconds in our sandbox, but its test step exited with 4 failed tests and 2 failed test files.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a continuing Canvas-first renderer path: the Phaser 4 migration guide calls Canvas rendering deprecated.

reviews.name: floating-ui
reviews.verdict: Floating UI completed our sandbox build and recorded 30 passing Vitest tests, while its contributor dependencies occupied 1,171 MB.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting pre-built React components: the React package supplies primitives and explicitly requires additional component work.

reviews.name: firefox
reviews.verdict: Firefox's npm dependency step completed in 13 seconds in our sandbox, while build and tests were skipped, leaving a compiled browser unverified.
reviews.skip_if: People who only want to browse the web: the README links to Firefox downloads, while this repository is for source work.

reviews.name: wagtail
reviews.verdict: Our Wagtail sandbox passed all 1,297 Jest tests, while npm audit reported 85 known vulnerabilities, so a green frontend suite leaves substantial dependency review and the Python deployment unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Owners expecting to assemble a finished website without code: Wagtail's design guide explicitly says to expect programming.

reviews.name: ardia

reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac, Windows or Linux users looking for a supported daily download: the README specifies Apple Silicon and macOS 14 or later.

reviews.name: Leaflet
reviews.verdict: Leaflet built in 5 seconds in our sandbox, but its test command exited 1 with no tests executed, so browser behavior remains unverified.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the library to supply a production basemap service: the quick start requires a tile URL and explicitly sends production users to the provider usage policy.

reviews.name: emdash
reviews.verdict: Our EmDash CMS build passed in 98 seconds, but its test command exited 1 after 36 seconds with an unexplained admin-package error.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean contributor test run before evaluation: our command exited 1 with an admin-package error whose cause is absent from the supplied tail.

reviews.name: javranking-extension
reviews.verdict: The measured checkout built successfully and passed 55 tests with 0 failures.
reviews.skip_if: Users who require documented browser-store installation and automatic Chromium updates.

reviews.name: styled-components
reviews.verdict: Our styled-components run built in 115 seconds and passed all 1,502 tests.
reviews.skip_if: Applications requiring edge-only server rendering: the 6.6.0 release notes require the Node.js runtime for routes rendering styled-components.

reviews.name: astryx
reviews.verdict: Astryx built in 138 seconds in our sandbox, but its tests exceeded the 900-second cap, leaving full-suite verification unfinished.
reviews.skip_if: Applications staying on React 18: the README requires React 19 or later.
